[Image #1] The red dot seemed to be stuck. Once I've answered the question, the red dot stays around for way longer than it needs to. I'm expecting it to transition to the next dot (i.e., the red dot should only be there when it's present and the question is still unanswered).  This was found before the latest install. 

Make sure you use Opus sub-agents to do all your work. They are effectively free. Parallelize them as much as possible. Have Fable and Sol, and Opus agents review any production code work or plans. There are architect agents for plan reviewing and code review agents for code reviewing. Save your context Any finished agents remove them to keep statusbar clean. Speak to me only in plain English business terms. You do pure co-ordination

Read-only: never edits code. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- architect-opus: Designs implementation architectures: analyzes existing codebase patterns, then delivers a blueprint — files to create/modify, component design, data flow, build sequence, risks, alternatives. Read-only: never edits code. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- architect-sol: Designs implementation architectures: analyzes existing codebase patterns, then delivers a blueprint — files to create/modify, component design, data flow, build sequence, risks, alternatives. Read-only: never edits code. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- code-reviewer-fable: Adversarial code review of diffs/commits/PRs: correctness, security, data integrity, conventions. Verifies each finding before reporting, ranks BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR with file:line and concrete failure scenario. Read-only: never fixes. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-reviewer-opus: Adversarial code review of diffs/commits/PRs: correctness, security, data integrity, conventions. Verifies each finding before reporting, ranks BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR with file:line and concrete failure scenario. Read-only: never fixes. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-reviewer-sol: Adversarial code review of diffs/commits/PRs: correctness, security, data integrity, conventions. Verifies each finding before reporting, ranks BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR with file:line and concrete failure scenario. Read-only: never fixes. (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, LSP, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- project-structure-validator: Validates project structure against co-location and architecture patterns defined in AGENTS.md (Tools: All tools)

- sol: General-purpose subagent running on Codex GPT-5.6 Sol via the claude-all gateway. Use for heavy implementation, deep debugging, second-opinion reviews, or any Task the orchestrator wants executed by GPT-5.6 Sol instead of a Claude model. Accepts any prompt a general-purpose agent would. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- understand-anything:architecture-analyzer: Analyzes a codebase's file structure, summaries, and import relationships to identify
logical architectural layers and assign every file to exactly one layer. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:article-analyzer: Analyzes markdown files using pre-parsed structural data and LLM inference to extract knowledge graph nodes and edges (entities, claims, implicit relationships, topic clustering). (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:assemble-reviewer: Reviews the output of merge-batch-graphs.py for semantic issues the script
cannot catch. Recovers dropped nodes/edges and fills cross-batch gaps. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:domain-analyzer: Analyzes codebases to extract business domain knowledge — domains, business flows, and process steps. Produces a domain-graph.json that maps how business logic flows through the code. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:file-analyzer: Analyzes batches of source files to produce knowledge graph nodes and edges.
Extracts file structure, functions, classes, and relationships using a two-phase
approach: structural extraction script followed by LLM semantic analysis. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:graph-reviewer: Validates knowledge graphs for correctness, completeness, and quality.
Runs systematic checks and renders approval or rejection decisions. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:knowledge-graph-guide: Use this agent when users need help understanding, querying, or working
with an Understand-Anything knowledge graph. Guides users through graph
structure, node/edge relationships, layer architecture, tours, and
dashboard usage. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:project-scanner: Scans a codebase directory to produce a structured inventory of all project files,
detected languages, frameworks, import maps, and estimated complexity. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:tour-builder: Designs guided learning tours through codebases, creating 5-15 pedagogical steps
that teach project architecture and key concepts in logical order. (Tools: All tools)

- access-new-relic-logs: Use when you or the user wants to investigate logs for app.
- access-outlook-business-email: Use when you or the user wants to read, search, triage, or reason about a Microsoft 365 business mailbox, or draft a reply or new email for the user to review and send. This skill never sends — it only creates drafts.
- access-xero-for-px: Access Pharmacy-Xpress Xero data through the official Custom Connection and confirmed logged-in web routes. Use for Xero reads, writes, reports, bank statement lines, reconciliation, VAT, forecasts, analytics, budgets, files, or assets.
- anvil-yaml: Update Anvil app manifest files in `anvil.yaml`, including services, app metadata, and `db_schema`, using the Anvil YAML type reference available to this agent and `anvil --json validate`.
- brand-guidelines: Applies Anthropic's official brand colors and typography to any sort of artifact that may benefit from having Anthropic's look-and-feel. Use it when brand colors or style guidelines, visual formatting, or company design standards apply.
- call-another-llm: Call Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI with a prompt and save the response to tmp/llm-responses/. Use when you need a second opinion, want to offload a subtask, or compare answers across LLMs.
- canvas-design: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
- chatgpt-pro-browser-query: Query ChatGPT through the user's already signed-in browser session while proving ChatGPT Pro and Extended Pro are active before sending. Use this whenever the user asks an agent to ask ChatGPT, use ChatGPT Pro, compare with ChatGPT, query the ChatGPT web app, or get a second opinion specifically from their ChatGPT subscription instead of the API.
- chrome-control: Shared Chrome DevTools control bridge that owns the single CDP connection so multiple Chrome-using skills run from one Chrome "Allow control" approval. Use as STEP 1 of any skill that drives the user's Chrome (ChatGPT browser query, ChatGPT image generation, future browser-driving skills).
- chrome-devtools-cli: Use this skill to write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate tasks in the browser or otherwise use Chrome DevTools via CLI.
- claude-epic-pr-review: Token-intensive, maximal review of a large pull request or branch. Runs three parallel review streams — a 5-agent Codex xhigh swarm with overlapping coverage, an adversarial multi-agent epic-review workflow, and a fork that validates every existing PR comment after checks pass — then consolidates all findings, auto-fixes valid code bugs in parallel while asking the user about UX / DB-schema / new-file decisions, runs /code-review max + /simplify max, and replaces the PR. Use for large, high-risk, or cross-cutting changes when an exhaustive, deliberately expensive review is wanted.
- claude-team-review-plan-implementation: Launch a large team of agents (Codex, Opus teammates) to line-by-line compare a reference plan against its implementation across multiple repos, extract deviations, validate, fix, verify, triage design decisions with the user, simplify, and create PRs. Accepts a reference file name as its argument.
- client-forms: Create, inspect, edit, style, validate, and convert Anvil client Forms under `client_code`, including Form Python, HTML templates, event wiring, Data Bindings, RepeatingPanel item templates, reusable Forms, theme CSS, and legacy YAML templates.
- client-modules: Edit Anvil client code Python modules under `client_code` that are not form definitions, without touching read-only dependencies or form templates.
- codex-image-generation: Generate or edit images through Codex CLI's built-in image_gen tool, driven headlessly via `codex exec` on the user's ChatGPT subscription (no OPENAI_API_KEY, no browser). Use whenever the user asks an agent to "generate an image", "make an image with Codex/ChatGPT", edit an existing image, produce icons/mock-ups/hero art/social assets, or create transparent-background PNGs. Supports single generate, multi-prompt batch, image editing, and chroma-key transparency. Final images are written to `<cwd>/tmp/codex-image-generation` by default (override with `--output-dir`).
- data-models: Design idiomatic Anvil data models and client/server data flow for new apps, CRUD workflows, Data Tables, model classes, buffering, drafts, Data Bindings, and server methods. Use before choosing an architecture for persisted domain data, when the user asks about Anvil models/model classes, or when deciding whether to pass rows, model objects, dicts, or server-callable payloads.
- doc-coauthoring: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- gws-calendar: Google Calendar: Manage calendars and events.
- gws-docs: Read and write Google Docs.
- gws-drive: Google Drive: Manage files, folders, and shared drives.
- gws-gmail: Gmail: Send, read, and manage email.
- gws-keep: Manage Google Keep notes.
- gws-people: Google People: Manage contacts and profiles.
- gws-script: Manage Google Apps Script projects.
- gws-shared: gws CLI: Shared patterns for authentication, global flags, and output formatting.
- gws-sheets: Google Sheets: Read and write spreadsheets.
- gws-slides: Google Slides: Read and write presentations.
- gws-tasks: Google Tasks: Manage task lists and tasks.
- implement-good-test-patterns: Use datasette-enrichments as a testing reference and imitate its pytest patterns when adding or restructuring tests. Use when writing tests, improving test structure, or aligning a Python project with good integration-style pytest patterns.
- initiate-smoke-tests: Interactive smoke-test runner. Reset the Neon test branch, patch in the fixtures the tests need, then walk the user through each UI smoke test one at a time via AskUser — the question names the exact app, care home, patient(s), med(s), and action. Forks (`subagent_type "fork"`, full context) do every DB sanity check, doc status update, and bug fix. Use when the user says "initiate smoke tests", "let's run the smoke tests", "start/resume smoke testing", or wants to execute a smoke-test doc against the test environment.
- mailshot-carehomes: Use when you or the user wants to send a single bulk announcement (mailshot) to every care-home portal contact - e.g. a new branding link, a portal change, a service notice. Gathers all care-home recipient emails from the Anvil carehome_portal_users table and the Neon "PX" script-copy table, then drafts ONE email (FROM team@, CC stacey@, BCC every care-home contact + zoe@/paresh@/mandeep@) via the access-outlook-business-email skill. Never sends - it only creates a draft for the user to review and send.
- manage-m365-tenant: Use when you or the user wants to administer the Microsoft 365 tenancy — users, groups, licenses, roles, domains, devices, policies, security alerts, audit logs, SharePoint sites, Teams, and usage reports. Full read/write control via Microsoft Graph.
- mk-feature-plan-mode: Plan and prototype a feature before implementation. Map the codebase, grill decisions, persist domain knowledge through /domain-modeling, and invoke /prototype for every UI change or material behaviour uncertainty. Reviewers iterate the plan and prototype together until the user approves the experience. Then write and open a self-contained feature_plan_<feature>.html, plus a test-verified migration.py only for non-additive schema changes. Use for "feature plan mode", "plan this feature", "design doc for ...", or any reviewable UX/architecture plan.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- performance-metrics-from-new-relic: Use when you or the user wants frontend performance metrics from New Relic, including Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, poor distributions, and worst URLs or sessions.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- pr-swarm-review: Fetch comments from an open GitHub pull request, then use a single sub-agent to extract every reviewer's substantive concerns and validate each one against the codebase in one pass, and consolidate the verdicts back in the main agent for triage and fixing. Use when the user wants existing PR comments triaged before deciding what to fix.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- quick-smoke-tests: Generate an ordered, dependency-aware list of UI smoke tests for the work just completed in this session. Walk the user through every test using the AskUser tool — one question per test with all details embedded in the question — then validate each reported result against the database. Use when the user says "smoke test what we just did", "let's quickly verify the changes in the UI", or similar after implementation work.
- server-code: Edit Anvil server code Python modules under `server_code`, including server-callable functions, background logic, and server packages, while keeping changes isolated to the app workspace.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- sync-global-user-instructions-md: Sync one canonical global instruction file into user-global Codex and Claude instruction files. Use when you need to update the canonical user-global instructions, diff installed global files against canon, reconcile drift, or replace user-global AGENTS/CLAUDE files from the canonical source.
- sync-mcps: Sync canonical MCP server manifests into Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor config files. Use when you need to add, remove, or update an MCP across all agents from one source of truth, or to diff installed MCP configs against canon.
- taste: Reverse-engineer the design taste of any website. Given a URL, captures DOM data and a screenshot via real browser, then runs a 4-step analysis to produce {domain}.md + {domain}.json with practical design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, grid) AND taste DNA (Trigger → Decision → Reason → Evidence trade-offs explaining WHY the design works). Use whenever the user wants to extract a site's design system, study a competitor's visual language, port an aesthetic to a new project, or generate design guidance for an AI coding agent. Triggers on '/taste <url>', 'analyze the design of X', 'what makes X's site good', 'extract design tokens from X', 'give me X's design DNA', 'build something in the style of X', 'I want my app to feel like X'. Output rejects AI slop ('clean', 'modern', 'user-friendly') in favor of concrete px/hex values and restraint trade-offs. Do NOT use for scraping data, summarizing page content, or tasks unrelated to visual design.
- theme-factory: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.
- webapp-testing: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
- windows-computer-use: Drive the Windows desktop UI the way a user can — list monitors/windows, read UIA element trees, click/right-click/double-click, type text, send key chords, scroll, drag, and capture screenshots across multiple monitors and any app type. For controlling a web browser, prefer chrome-control / the browser skills instead.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate

- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- understand-anything:understand: Analyze a codebase to produce an interactive knowledge graph for understanding architecture, components, and relationships
- understand-anything:understand-chat: Use when you need to ask questions about a codebase or understand code using a knowledge graph
- understand-anything:understand-dashboard: Launch the interactive web dashboard to visualize a codebase's knowledge graph
- understand-anything:understand-diff: Use when you need to analyze git diffs or pull requests to understand what changed, affected components, and risks

- understand-anything:understand-explain: Use when you need a deep-dive explanation of a specific file, function, or module in the codebase
- understand-anything:understand-knowledge: Analyze a Karpathy-pattern LLM wiki knowledge base and generate an interactive knowledge graph with entity extraction, implicit relationships, and topic clustering.
- understand-anything:understand-onboard: Use when you need to generate an onboarding guide for new team members joining a project
- superset:10x: Personalized audit that teaches advanced Superset features the user isn't using yet — automations, parallel agents, tasks, multi-host, terminals, custom commands, MCP. - superset:doctor: Diagnose and fix Superset problems — connection failures, offline hosts, terminals not attaching, auth or update issues. Use when the user reports something broken or misbehaving in Superset itself, before filing feedback.
- superset:feedback: Collect and submit feedback about Superset — bug reports, feature requests, or general feedback — privately to the Superset team or as a public GitHub issue. Use when the user wants to report a Superset bug, request a feature, or send feedback about Superset.
- superset:orchestrate: Coordinate multiple terminal coding agents through the Superset CLI by creating isolated workspaces, launching workers, sending follow-ups, reading terminal output, tracking dependencies, and collecting structured results. Use when asked to delegate or parallelize coding work, coordinate agents across workspaces or hosts, hand work between agents, monitor worker progress, or run a multi-agent workflow with Superset. Do not use for ordinary single-agent workspace, task, or automation management.
- superset:setup: Make a repository Superset-ready — author .superset/config.json with setup/teardown/run scripts so every new workspace boots configured, then verify with a real workspace. Use when the user wants to set up a project or repo for Superset, configure workspace setup scripts, or fix a failing workspace setup.
- superset:standup: Digest of what your Superset agents did — sweeps workspaces, tasks, and agent terminals, then reports what finished, what needs review, and what's blocked. Use when the user asks what their agents did, wants a standup or summary of agent work, or returns after being away.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

`PostToolUse` tool=`AskUserQuestion` → `pane-map-hook.ts:2152-2158` removes the `.askq` owner, returns `Start` → renderer `statusTransitions.ts:76-85` sets `working`, clears `permission`. Sub-second when it lands.

- Renderer: `statusTransitions.ts:90` PermissionRequest sets permission; `:64-71` **SubagentActive sets working and clears NOTHING**; `:76` Start clears permission. `store.ts:541-556`.

<agent-message from="clear-trace">
CLEAR-STATUS TRACE — investigation complete, read-only, nothing edited.

ROOT CAUSE (one line): "Clear Status" clears the HOST binding + the manual mark, but the dot renders from the RENDERER store's latched axes, and the only renderer clear it performs drops `review` entries. Red, yellow and blue survive untouched.

=== 1. THE MENU ITEM ===
Live (v2, the one the user clicks):
- apps/desktop/src/renderer/routes/_authenticated/_dashboard/components/DashboardSidebar/components/DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem/components/DashboardSidebarWorkspaceContextMenu/DashboardSidebarWorkspaceContextMenu.tsx:293-298 — `{hasStatus && <ContextMenuItem onSelect={onClearStatus}>...Clear Status`
  - prop declared :63, destructured :164
- hasStatus={!!workspaceStatus} — DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem.tsx:289, :415
- workspaceStatus = useV2WorkspaceDisplayStatus(id) — DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem.tsx:89
- onClearStatus={handleClearStatus} — DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem.tsx:318, :444
- handler — useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts:292-311

Dead (v1 screens/main, fork is v2-only): WorkspaceContextMenu.tsx:203-206 -> WorkspaceListItem.tsx:477 -> useTabsStore.resetWorkspaceStatus. Different store, not the fork's dots.

=== 2. WHAT THE HANDLER MUTATES (useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts:292-311) ===
a) clearWorkspaceAttention() — LOCAL closure at :62-78 (NOT the store method of the same name at store.ts:691):
   - clearManualUnread(workspaceId) -> store.ts:271-285. Deletes ONLY source key `manual:<workspaceId>` + the manualUnread map entry.
   - per binding: markTerminalSeenAndReportRead -> companionAlertSync.ts:371-413 -> markTerminalSeen (store.ts:286-315). Bumps terminalSeenAt; deletes the terminal's `sources` entry ONLY IF `entry.status === "review"` (store.ts:293). Retracts the phone alert only when a review was actually dropped.
b) tRPC terminalAgents.clearWorkspaceStatuses.mutate({workspaceId}) — packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/terminal-agents/terminal-agents.ts:277-287 -> TerminalAgentStore.clearWorkspaceStatuses (packages/host-service/src/terminal-agents/store.ts:187-200): sets each binding lastEventType="Stop", preserves lastEventAt, persistence.upsert (:194), emit change.
c) queryClient.invalidateQueries(terminal-agent-bindings).

NOT touched: .askq markers, backgroundRunningTerminals, shellRunningTerminals, companion question-store, outstandingReadyAt (except via the review path).

=== 3. WHY THE DOT SURVIVES ===
The rendered dot never consults host bindings:
- useV2WorkspaceDisplayStatus (store.ts:1196-1202) -> selectV2WorkspaceDisplayStatus (store.ts:1167-1193) folds getSourceDisplayStatus (store.ts:945-982) over state.sources + shellRunningTerminals + backgroundRunningTerminals. Same for tab chips (useV2WorkspaceTabChips, store.ts:1011) and pane/tab dots.
- The handler's only removal is gated on status === "review" (store.ts:293). `status` = highest-precedence live axis (deriveAgentStatus store.ts:94-99; precedence permission > working > review at store.ts:89-93):
    permission latched -> status "permission" -> NOT removed -> stays RED
    working latched    -> status "working"    -> NOT removed -> stays YELLOW
    review + permission-> status "permission" -> NOT removed -> stays RED (green hidden under red survives too)
    background/shell   -> separate maps       -> NOT touched -> stays BLUE
    review alone       -> removed             -> clears (the only working case)
Every case a user would reach for the escape hatch for does nothing.

THE CORRECT MUTATOR ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT CALLED: useV2NotificationStore.getState().clearWorkspaceStatuses(workspaceId) at store.ts:648-689 purges all sources for the workspace (:650-658), backgroundRunningTerminals (:660-676) and manualUnread (:679-684). The handler calls the HOST's identically-named method instead.

Secondary re-assertion (matters for the fix; not the primary cause since the dot never leaves):
- resyncAgentStatus.ts:660-683 — on socket open, row.pendingPermission === true replays PermissionRequest -> red back (:678-683). pendingPermission === null (unreadable dir) EXPLICITLY re-latches the prior red (:663-677). No branch retracts red. Trigger: HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:146 (runResync on socket open / workspace-set growth).
- pendingPermission comes from hasPendingQuestionMarker (packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/notifications/agent-status-snapshot.ts:127-172) reading ~/.superset/agent-subagent-running/<terminalId>.askq/, DELIBERATELY independent of lastEventType (documented :15-19) — so forcing bindings to Stop cannot clear it. The dir is written/cleared only by the Python hook: apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:602-710 (_askq_dir/_reap_askq/_clear_dir), :1865, :1919-1920, :1986-1992, :2104, :2132 — on answer / SubagentStop / new prompt / session end.
- useTerminalInterruptClear.ts:40-58 has the IDENTICAL defect: host mutation + invalidation, zero renderer-store writes. Confirmed as you suspected.

DEAD CODE FOUND: clearV2TerminalRunStatus (store.ts:812-826) clears a terminal's source entry AND its background-running blue. Its doc block claims interrupt (useTerminalInterruptClear) and pane close (usePaneRegistry onAfterClose) both route through it. Repo-wide grep: NO callers — only the barrel re-export at apps/desktop/src/renderer/stores/v2-notifications/index.ts:2. Comment is stale; that wiring was lost.

=== 4. EVERY STATE LOCATION A WORKING CLEAR MUST TOUCH ===
1. Renderer `sources` axes per source — store.ts:648 clearWorkspaceStatuses(workspaceId). THE MISSING CALL. Covers permission/working/review across terminal, chat, manual sources.
2. Renderer blue axes — backgroundRunningTerminals covered by #1 (store.ts:660-676); shellRunningTerminals is NOT — needs a per-terminal clear unless the agent-terminal gate at store.ts:971-976 already suppresses it.
3. manualUnread — covered by #1 (store.ts:679-684) and by clearManualUnread (store.ts:271).
4. Host binding lastEventType — already done (packages/host-service/src/terminal-agents/store.ts:187-200) + persistence.upsert (:194).
5. .askq markers — ~/.superset/agent-subagent-running/<terminalId>.askq/*. No clear path touches them. Until emptied, the next socket-open resync re-paints red (resyncAgentStatus.ts:678-683). Fix belongs in the host procedure (terminal-agents.ts:277) — only place with both fs access and terminal scope.
6. Companion question-store — packages/host-service/src/companion/question-store.ts (phone/watch blocked-question alerts) + outstandingReadyAt retraction via reportTerminalSeen / clearOutstandingReady (companionAlertSync.ts:397-411). Today handled only for terminals that had a green.
7. Persisted renderer state — store is persist-wrapped to sessionStorage (store.ts:255-264); #1 writes through, no extra step. But an unrepaired .askq survives a restart and re-reds on the cold-start resync.
8. terminalSeenAt — already bumped by markTerminalSeen; needed so the bindings-derived chip status (deriveTerminalAgentStatus, DashboardSidebarWorkspaceStatusProvider.tsx:283-291) resolves idle not review.

=== ABSOLUTE PATHS ===

- Remote/relay hosts: markers deleted on the **host's** disk — the reason this is not in Electron main.

- The `SubagentActive` volume — not a fault at 0.04% error.

# Blueprint: stuck red dot (MUST-1) + broken manual "Clear Status" (MUST-2)

## Correction to the investigation report — MUST-1's mechanism is different

The report's cause ("POST times out under host saturation; add retry/queue") is wrong, which changes the fix. Evidence from this machine:

- Host `127.0.0.1:55331`: healthy until 03:00 today, then **zero** successful posts. Hourly: `02` = 786 ok / 0 err; `03` = 1 ok / 926 err; `04`-`12` = 0 ok / 3880 err. A cliff, not 32% loss.
- `netstat -ano`: **55331 is not listening.** Live host is `48056` (pid 21352).
- `~/.superset/host/30e16b5a-.../manifest.json` → `"endpoint":"http://127.0.0.1:48056"`, rewritten 03:01. One org, one manifest.
- 6 terminals still POST to the dead 55331. All 6 have `terminal_sessions` rows in the **live** host's `host.db`; 2 are `status=active`.

This is the known **frozen hook URL** bug — `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\plans\agent-hook-url-frozen-port.md`. The env var is baked into the PTY at creation; host-service restarted onto a new port; PTYs survive in the pty-daemon with the dead address.

That plan's fix shipped **only to the shell templates**. `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\agent-setup\templates\notify-hook.template.sh:170-205` builds candidates from every `~/.superset/host/*/manifest.json`. The fork's Python hook, which owns every dot decision, was never ported: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts:2430` reads the env var, `:2247-2253` posts to it, done.

**Why the symptom is specifically a stuck red.** `~/.claude/settings.json` routes `PermissionRequest` → `notify.sh` (has failover) and every other event → `superset-notify.py` (does not). The red-**setter** still reaches the live host; the red-**clearer** (`pane-map-hook.ts:2152-2159`) is lost. Confirmed in `~/.superset/agent-dot-render.log`: `d3ce7c25` red 10:36:33, answer 10:55:38 logged `post-error`, cleared 11:13:02 (37 min). `72d85ab1` red 10:39:05, still red past 11:14. Control terminal `d603171b` on the live host flips `permission`↔`working` in seconds.

The report's "SubagentActive flood" is a red herring — the flooded host runs 19,459 posted / 8 errors.

## Clear-status trace: confirmed, with two refinements

Your trace is correct on every line reference I checked. Two refinements:

1. **`outstandingReadyAt` and the companion ready-alert are already handled today**, not missing. The hook-local `clearWorkspaceAttention` (`...\useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts:62-79`) calls `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead` per binding (`...\V2NotificationController\lib\companionAlertSync.ts:390-412`), which bumps `terminalSeenAt`, reports read to the host, and clears `outstandingReadyAt` **on acceptance**. Green and its phone alert do come down. Only red/yellow/blue survive. Widening the store purge is still worth doing as belt-and-braces for the rejected-report case, but it is not the defect.
2. **`shellRunningTerminals` genuinely needs clearing, for plain shells only.** The agent-terminal gate at `store.ts:971-974` suppresses shell-blue on agent terminals, so a stuck agent dot is unaffected. But `selectV2WorkspaceDisplayStatus:1183-1190` yields a status for open terminals with **no** source entry, so a plain shell's blue renders even after every source is purged.

Also confirmed: `clearV2TerminalRunStatus` (`store.ts:812-826`) has exactly two references — its own definition and the barrel re-export at `...\stores\v2-notifications\index.ts:2`. Dead, and its doc comment falsely claims interrupt and pane close route through it.

**Scope correction:** there is **one** Clear Status item, on sidebar workspace rows (`...\DashboardSidebarWorkspaceContextMenu.tsx:293-298`). No tab-level clear exists. The v1 `...\screens\main\...\WorkspaceListItem.tsx:223` drives the tabs store and is dead under the v2-only rule. The item *is* reachable when a red is stuck — its `hasStatus` gate reads `useV2WorkspaceDisplayStatus` (`store.ts:1196-1205`), the same store holding the latched red. The bug is the handler, not the gate.

Two re-assertion vectors survive the click, both from the surviving marker:
- `...\resyncAgentStatus.ts:678-685` re-applies `PermissionRequest` from `pendingPermission`, derived from the marker dir at `...\agent-status-snapshot.ts:127-167`. Forcing the binding to `Stop` cannot help — `pendingPermission` is deliberately independent of `lastEventType` (`agent-status-snapshot.ts:13-19`). The `pendingPermission === null` branch at `:660-677` re-applies only `preEntry.axes.permission`, so once the renderer clears locally it re-latches nothing; it is a hazard only while the local clear is missing.
- The hook's central guard: while the marker exists, untagged tool completions return `SubagentActive` (`pane-map-hook.ts:2214-2216`), which clears nothing (`statusTransitions.ts:64-74`). The red is self-perpetuating.

---

## 1. Recommended approach

### MUST-1 — port the manifest failover into the embedded Python hook

Env URL first (unchanged fast path), then each `~/.superset/host/*/manifest.json` endpoint, stopping at the first response not containing `"ignored": true`.

Alternatives and why each loses:
- **Queue + retry in the hook** (report's proposal): retrying a permanently dead port never delivers, and a background drain process is the `(HOOK-FORK-DIET)` fork cascade this fork banned.
- **Raise the 1.5 s timeout**: nothing is slow, the port is gone. Pure agent stall, zero delivery.
- **Reduce the SubagentActive flood**: the flooded host has a 0.04% error rate.
- **Marker-driven resync alone**: heals the dot but every other event from those terminals still vanishes.
- **Stable socket / port pinning**: rejected at `plans\agent-hook-url-frozen-port.md:90-91`; reasons hold.

Decisive advantage: `writeNotifyScriptIfChanged()` (`pane-map-hook.ts:2736`) rewrites the script every desktop start and Python re-reads it per fire, so **this heals the 6 already-orphaned live terminals on their next event** with no terminal restart.

`(HOOK-FORK-DIET)` risk: **none.** That footgun is `.sh` templates forking subprocesses under emulated msys2. This is one Python process doing stdlib file reads and in-process `urlopen`.

Cost: fast path unchanged. A dead env URL already costs 1.5 s (3 s when the companion retry fires, `:2623-2642`); drop the per-candidate timeout to **0.75 s** and the worst case halves while actually delivering.

### MUST-2 — make the marker the thing manual clear deletes, and give the renderer the axis clear it never performed

**Host half (authoritative).** New mutation `terminalAgents.dismissWorkspaceStatuses`: per terminal in scope, delete the `<terminalId>.askq` directory, force the binding to `Stop` via the existing `store.clearWorkspaceStatuses`, and settle any pending companion question via `markStale`.

**Renderer half.** `handleClearStatus` awaits that mutation, then calls the already-existing, uncalled `useV2NotificationStore.clearWorkspaceStatuses(workspaceId)` (`store.ts:648-690`) — your name-collision finding.

On sharing one path with the automatic answer-clear: **they cannot be one function**, because they differ on the only axis that matters — manual may drop a live red, automatic may not. What they share, and what removes the duplication that matters, is the **marker mutation and its path derivation**. The `.askq` path is built in three places today: the Python hook (`pane-map-hook.ts:602-629`), the Electron watcher (`agent-jsonl-watcher.ts:505-546`), and the host reader (`agent-status-snapshot.ts:127-138`). A fourth ad-hoc copy is exactly the parallel mechanism to avoid, so the new writer goes **in `agent-status-snapshot.ts`, sharing one path builder and one `SAFE_MARKER_SEGMENT` guard with the reader.** Full unification across Python/main/host needs a rewrite and is out of scope; I am not pretending otherwise.

Host-side rather than Electron main because the marker lives on the machine the agent runs on — for a relay or remote host, main's `homedir()` is the wrong disk. The host also already holds the binding and the companion store, so one round trip does all three.

`markStale` not `resolve`: `resolve` stamps answered-by provenance (`question-store.ts:757-761`) and nobody answered. `markStale` (`:1976-1991`) is terminal, non-provenance-bearing, and still routes through `settle()` → `onSettled` → `push.cancelPending` (`companion\index.ts:663-676`), so the phone notification retracts. Same retraction, honest record.

**Deliberately not deleted: the run-dir subagent markers.** They do not re-assert red on resync — resync replays `lastEventType`, forced to `Stop`. They only shape the *next* hook decision, and a running subagent re-asserting yellow at its next event is correct. Deleting them would corrupt live subagent tracking.

**Cross-window propagation by convergence, not broadcast.** Marker gone plus binding `Stop` means any other window's next resync converges to cleared. I considered broadcasting `Detached` (clears both axes at `statusTransitions.ts:51-62`, chime-exempt at `lifecycleEvents.ts:74-88`) — rejected, because `Detached` also means "session ended" (`map-event-type.ts:11`) and asserting it about a live agent is a lie told to fix a refresh delay.

---

## 2. Files to create/modify

### MUST-1

**`...\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts`** — embedded `NOTIFY_SCRIPT` (`:312`+):
- New `_hook_candidate_urls(env_url)` near `_post_hook` (`:2238`): `[env_url]` + `<endpoint>/trpc/notifications.hook` per manifest glob, deduped, order-preserving. Root = `os.environ.get("SUPERSET_HOME_DIR")` or `Path.home()/".superset"`. Per-manifest failure skips and logs, never raises.
- New `_deliver(candidates, body)`: POST each in order; return on the first body **not** containing `"ignored": true` / `"ignored":true`. Raise the last exception if all fail. Keying on *absence of `ignored:true`* rather than presence of `ignored:false` means an upstream body change degrades to "delivered to the first host that answered" instead of "probes forever". `notifications.ts:357` returns `ignored:false` on delivery; `:221-225`, `:275-279`, `:293-297` return `ignored:true` on drops.
- `_post_hook:2253`: timeout `1.5` → `0.75`.
- Call site `:2606-2649`: `_post_hook` → `_deliver`; log the delivering url in the `posted` record. The companion strip-and-retry at `:2623-2642` re-runs through `_deliver` with the same list.
- Total-failure path `:2643-2648`: also emit one `_decision_log` line naming every candidate tried. Reuses the always-on rotating audit channel (`:415`).
- **`_log` rotation** (`:401-412`): copy the rotate-at-1 MB idiom from `_decision_log:428-438`. Live file is **508,757,788 bytes**. MUST, not SHOULD — two lines, same function family, and an unbounded append inside the agent's hook window is itself latency.

**`...\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.test.ts`** — new `describe("superset-notify endpoint resolution")`. Harness at `:12-97` already gives real Python, throwaway `HOME`, real `Bun.serve` sink. Cases: dead env URL → delivered via manifest; live env URL → manifests unprobed; wrong-org sink returning `ignored:true` → probing continues; all dead → `post-error` + a `dot-decisions.log` line. The existing sink at `:43` returns no `ignored` field, which counts as delivered under the predicate, so existing tests pass unchanged — the wrong-org case must return `ignored:true` explicitly.

### MUST-2

**`...\packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\notifications\agent-status-snapshot.ts`** — extract the path builder inline at `:133-138` into `askqMarkerDir(terminalId)`, used by both the existing `hasPendingQuestionMarker` and a new `clearPendingQuestionMarkers(terminalId): Promise<boolean>` (`rm` recursive+force; `ENOENT` is success; any other error throws so the caller fails loud). Reader and writer share one derivation and one `SAFE_MARKER_SEGMENT` check (`:80`).

**`...\packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\terminal-agents\terminal-agents.ts`** — new `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` mutation beside `clearWorkspaceStatuses` (`:277-287`), input `{workspaceId, terminalId?}`. Per terminal, in order: `clearPendingQuestionMarkers` → existing `ctx.terminalAgentStore.clearWorkspaceStatuses` → companion dismissal. Returns `{cleared, markersRemoved, questionsDismissed}` so the renderer can surface partial failure. A marker delete that throws fails the whole mutation loud — a green UI over a surviving marker is the exact bug being fixed. `clearWorkspaceStatuses` stays **unchanged**: `useTerminalInterruptClear.ts:46` depends on its non-red-dropping semantics.

**`...\packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\notifications\companion-question-sink.ts`** — add `dismissByTerminal({hostTerminalId, reason})` to the `CompanionQuestionSink` interface (`:78-87`) and a `forwardCompanionDismissal(...)` mirroring `forwardCompanionCapture` (`:264-311`). No-op when no bridge is registered.

**`...\packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts`** — implement `dismissByTerminal` on the sink registered at `:1161`: `store.byHostTerminal(id)` then `store.markStale(id, reason)`. Both already on `QuestionStore` (`question-store.ts:749`, `:777`); no question-store change.

**`...\useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts`** — `handleClearStatus` (`:292-307`) calls `dismissWorkspaceStatuses`, and **on success** the store's `clearWorkspaceStatuses(workspaceId)` plus the existing `clearWorkspaceAttention()` and query invalidation. Host first, renderer second: a failed host call must not leave a cleared-looking UI the next resync un-clears. Existing `toast.error` at `:302-306` is the loud path.

**`...\apps\desktop\src\renderer\stores\v2-notifications\store.ts`** — `clearWorkspaceStatuses` (`:648-690`) additionally clears `shellRunningTerminals` (for plain-shell blue, per the refinement above) and `outstandingReadyAt` for the workspace's terminals. Add the `ndots` mutation log line the sibling `clearWorkspaceAttention` writes at `:704-713`.

**Dead code (same PR).** Delete `clearV2TerminalRunStatus` (`store.ts:812-826`) and its barrel re-export (`...\stores\v2-notifications\index.ts:2`). Zero callers; its doc comment at `:808-811` and `:827-829` falsely documents the interrupt and pane-close paths, which is actively misleading anyone debugging exactly this bug. Deleting beats fixing the comment: the correct behaviour it describes now lives in the dismiss path and in `useTerminalInterruptClear`.

**Tests**: `...\stores\v2-notifications\store.test.ts` (all maps cleared); a router test for the host mutation (marker dir gone, binding `Stop`, `markStale` called, throw on undeletable marker).

**`FEATURES.md`** — two feature rows plus markers, tab-separated per `:150-215`:
```
(HOOK-ENDPOINT-HEAL)	apps/desktop/src/main
(HOOK-ENDPOINT-HEAL)	apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.test.ts
(MANUAL-DISMISS)	packages/host-service/src
(MANUAL-DISMISS)	apps/desktop/src/renderer
```
The test-pinned marker matters: without it a merge could take upstream's router and leave the dispatch untested — the reasoning already written at `notifications.ts:16-22` for `(COMPANION-CAPTURE-HOOK)`.

### SHOULD (separable, user's call)

**A. `resyncAgentStatus.ts:660-685`** — add the missing `else` for `pendingPermission === false`, clearing the permission axis via `applySourceAxes(..., {set:[], clear:["permission"]}, row.lastEventAt)`, shaped like `:664-676`. Today resync can only add red. Safety rests on the marker being the invariant; residual risk is a question opening between the host's `readdir` and the apply. **Verify the `preEntry.occurredAt > row.lastEventAt` fence at `:460-463` covers a mid-flight `PermissionRequest` before shipping.** If not, unsafe — do not ship.

**B. `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:135-172`** — A only helps on reconnect: `runResync` fires on socket open or workspace-set growth. On a stable socket it never runs, which is today's stuck case. Add a bounded 60 s re-run reusing `runResync` and its generation guard.

**C. `useTerminalInterruptClear.ts:40-58`** — same host-only defect you found: clears the binding, never the renderer's latched axes. Fix by clearing the terminal's own axes locally after the mutation resolves. **Do not point it at the new dismiss mutation** — an interrupt is not a dismissal and must keep no-drop-live-red semantics. Partly mitigated today: the watcher clears `_main` on a detected interrupt (`agent-jsonl-watcher.ts:1043-1044`).

### Explicitly do not do

**Leaked `.askq/_main` reap.** 24 leaked markers, oldest 2026-07-07. The no-reap policy is argued at `agent-status-snapshot.ts:104-122`: nothing host-side can prove a leak, and the mtime-vs-`startedAt` fence drops live reds in exactly the case it targets. Not an aggravator here — markers on both stuck terminals were correct throughout. MUST-2 gives the user a deliberate way to clear them, which is the right answer.

---

## 3. Data flow

**MUST-1, today** — user answers → `PostToolUse` → `_remove(askq/_main)` **[local, succeeds]** → `"Start"` **[correct]** → POST `55331` **[dead, 1.5 s]** → `post-error` into a 508 MB file. Binding stays `PermissionRequest`; renderer stays red.

**MUST-1, after** — … → `"Start"` → candidates `[55331/…, 48056/…]` → `_deliver` candidate 2 → `200 {"ignored":false}` → `notifications.ts:312` broadcast, `:320` binding persisted → `statusTransitions.ts:76-87` sets working, clears permission. Sub-second.

**MUST-2, after** — right-click → Clear Status → `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` → per terminal: `rm -rf <terminalId>.askq` → binding `Stop` → `byHostTerminal` + `markStale` → `settle()` → `onSettled` → `push.cancelPending` (phone retracts). On resolve: `clearWorkspaceStatuses(workspaceId)` drops sources, background, shell, manual, outstanding-ready; `clearWorkspaceAttention()` marks seen and reports read; bindings query invalidated. Next resync reads `pendingPermission: false` and re-asserts nothing; the hook's central guard sees an empty dir and stops holding `SubagentActive`.

Validation stays at the tRPC input boundary; ownership stays the DB read (`notifications.ts:256-261`); the `.askq` directory remains the single source of truth for red.

---

1. `_log` rotation. Verify: suite green; shipped script rotates at 1 MB.
2. `_hook_candidate_urls`, unused. Verify: candidate list over a temp `SUPERSET_HOME_DIR` with 0/1/2 manifests plus one malformed.
3. `_deliver` + 0.75 s, wired into the call site and companion retry. Verify: four new cases; full `bun test apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/`.
4. Mutation check (matching `plans\agent-hook-url-frozen-port.md:116`): break the manifest glob, confirm exactly the failover tests fail, restore.
5. **Live heal, no rebuild needed**: start the desktop so `writeNotifyScriptIfChanged` lands the script, answer a question in `72d85ab1` or `d3ce7c25`, watch `~/.superset/agent-dot-render.log` for `permission → working` within a second and a `posted` line naming `48056`.
6. `clearPendingQuestionMarkers` + shared path builder. Verify: unit test incl. traversal-guard rejection.
7. `dismissByTerminal` on sink and bridge. Verify: `markStale` fires, push retraction observed.
8. `dismissWorkspaceStatuses`. Verify: marker gone, binding `Stop`, question stale, throw on undeletable marker.
9. Renderer store widening + `handleClearStatus` + dead-code deletion. Verify: store test, then CDP per `.agents/skills/cdp-verification/SKILL.md` — stick a red, click Clear Status, confirm the dot dies and **survives a forced resync**.
10. `FEATURES.md`; `node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs`.
11. SHOULD A (gated on the step-7 fence check in §2), then B, then C.
12. `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `/simplify` before commit.

---

## 5. Risks and edge cases

**MUST-1**
- Multi-org double delivery impossible — a terminal id lives in one host's `terminal_sessions`; others answer `ignored:true`.
- A stale manifest from a crashed host adds 0.75 s. Manifests are rewritten per start (`apps\desktop\src\main\host-service\index.ts:126-138`), one per org. Do not add a cache for a two-entry loop.
- Predicate drift: if upstream ever returns a body containing literal `"ignored": true` for a delivered event, detection inverts. Covered by tests.
- Ordering: `_deliver` must stay strictly after the marker mutations in `_decide_event_type` (`:2500-2513`) so markers survive total delivery failure.
- `SUPERSET_HOME_DIR` honoured for the manifest glob, **not** for marker paths — the host reads markers at a hardcoded `homedir()` (`agent-status-snapshot.ts:133-138`), so unifying would silently break the resync. Comment it; do not "clean it up".

**MUST-2**
- **Dropping a live red is intended** and is the user's explicit decision. A genuinely blocked agent shows red again at its next hook event; between click and event the dot lies. This is why no automatic path may reuse it.
- Marker delete racing a *new* owner mid-dismiss destroys that question's red. Bounded to milliseconds, self-heals at the next event. Do not add locking.

- Remote/relay hosts: markers deleted on the **host's** disk — the reason this is not in Electron main.
- Other windows lag until their next resync: ≤60 s with SHOULD-B, until reconnect without it.
- No schema change, no migration, no new persisted key (`partialize` at `store.ts:745-753` already covers the maps).
- Three similarly-named functions (host `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, renderer `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, new `dismissWorkspaceStatuses`) is a real readability hazard — the name collision already caused this bug. Cross-reference all three in comments.

---

## 6. Out of scope

- Events lost between 03:00 and the fix: gone. MUST-1 heals forward only.
- Preventing the port from moving (pinning, stable socket) — rejected in the plan doc.

- The other three shell templates — already fixed.
- Adding a **tab-level** Clear Status. None exists; the mutation takes an optional `terminalId` so it is cheap later, but the UI is a scope change.

- Surfacing "agent status unavailable" in the UI (`plans\agent-hook-url-frozen-port.md:138`).

content.text:
Plan is in, with a correction: the real cause isn't a slow service. The status service restarted overnight onto a new address, and running terminals kept sending updates to the old dead address. The "question asked" signal has fallback logic to find the new address; the "question answered" signal doesn't. So red arrives, its clearing never does. Fix: give the answer signal the same fallback, plus rebuild Clear Status so it wipes every copy of the status including the on-disk marker.

Sending the plan to Fable and Sol architects for review now.

input.message:
Two architect reviews of your blueprint are back. User approved full scope: MUST-1, MUST-2, and ALL THREE SHOULDs (A gated as you specified, B, C). Revise the blueprint into a FINAL implementation spec addressing every point below, resolving the one disagreement, then send the final spec to "main". Where the two reviews agree, adopt; where you disagree with a finding, justify with code evidence.

CONSENSUS AMENDMENTS (both reviewers):
1. _deliver predicate polarity: do NOT accept "response not containing ignored:true". Parse the tRPC envelope JSON and require explicit ignored === false (result.data.json.ignored per notifications.ts:312-357; notify.sh does positive check at template :204-206). Malformed/foreign/HTML body must NOT count as delivered.
2. All-ignored path is undefined: ghost terminal gets ignored:true from every candidate (precedent agent-status-snapshot.ts:41-48). Define: all probed, ≥1 2xx, none accepted → delivered no-op (notify.sh parity), single log line; must NOT trigger companion strip-and-retry or post-error on every event.
3. Marker deletion safety: SAFE_MARKER_SEGMENT guard must live INSIDE askqMarkerDir/clearPendingQuestionMarkers, plus zod boundary validation; derive the workspace terminal set server-side (Fable: enumerate terminal_sessions rows for the workspace — DB as source of truth — so leaked markers of binding-less terminals are also swept; Sol: never rm from raw input). Traversal/refusal tests.
4. Dismiss durability across resync (Sol BLOCKER-2 / Fable MAJOR-5): forcing binding to Stop while keeping lastEventAt means resync re-raises GREEN (review) for terminals whose seen watermark doesn't cover lastEventAt (resyncAgentStatus.ts:515-575), and SHOULD-B would re-raise it within 60s. Fix: dismiss mutation returns affected terminalIds + host lastEventAt; renderer marks each seen through that generation (markTerminalSeen primitive, resync uses it at :509-511) — or a durable dismissal generation on the host. Make convergence provable.
5. Companion dismiss must publish question.stale / advance gseq like existing settle paths (companion/index.ts:1779-1806, reconcile :970-997, :1019-1041), with a manual-dismiss reason — otherwise paired phone UI keeps stale question state. Also: sink may be null (bridge not running) → questionsDismissed=0, not throw. Wrapper at companion/index.ts:1161-1163 needs dismissByTerminal too.
6. SHOULD-B: runResync dedupes on syncedKeyRef (HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:139-146) — periodic tick must force/reset the guard safely, prevent overlapping runs, clean up on unmount. And B ships only together with amendment 4.
7. SHOULD-C: must NOT clear the permission axis (that would drop a live red from an automatic path). Clear working/review/background only.
8. Marker race honesty: rm racing a NEWLY-raised question's marker write (pane-map-hook.ts:2137-2141 writes before returning PermissionRequest) silently drops that new question's red and no next hook event comes from a blocked AskUserQuestion. Either fence dismissal against binding/question generation or document as a real accepted live-red race — not "self-heals".

DISAGREEMENT TO RESOLVE:
- Timeout: your 0.75s vs Fable's keep-1.5s (dead loopback port = instant ECONNREFUSED, so failover doesn't need a shorter timeout; halving risks spurious failover + duplicate delivery on a slow live host on this emulated ARM64 box). Sol adds: prefer the terminal's own SUPERSET_ORGANIZATION_ID manifest (terminal/env.ts:251-275) first, and bound total probe budget. Pick one design and justify.

ALSO INCORPORATE:
- Sol MAJOR: outstandingReadyAt must NOT be unconditionally deleted in renderer clearWorkspaceStatuses (store.ts:149-177 — it's the retraction evidence for ready alerts; cleared only after host accepts seen report, companionAlertSync.ts:381-410). Use markTerminalSeenAndReportRead + compare-and-clear on ack.
- Fable MINOR: handleClearStatus ordering means host-down = zero visible effect + toast (behavior regression vs today) — decide explicitly and state the decision.
- Fable: SHOULD-A gate VERIFIED SOUND (fence :460-463 covers it; loop synchronous) — ship A, mirror the null-branch workspaceId check (:664-666) in the else-branch. A also strengthens your cross-window convergence claim, which is otherwise unproven for the permission axis.
- Sol MINOR test list: rotation >1MB, all-ignored, malformed response, unsafe terminal id, ENOENT vs non-ENOENT, workspace isolation, partial failure, markStale + push cancel + question.stale frame, renderer seen/outstanding handling, resync-after-dismiss, cross-window convergence, mutation failure leaves local dots unchanged.
- FEATURES.md: needs BOTH human-readable feature rows AND machine marker lines token<TAB>root (FEATURES.md:110-120); two lines with different roots is legal.

Confirmed-correct items you should keep unchanged: existing clearWorkspaceStatuses mutation untouched; markStale-not-resolve; no Detached broadcast; no subagent run-dir deletion; no leaked-marker reap; log rotation as MUST; Codex hooks covered by same script (pane-map-hook.ts:2660-2668).

## 0. Disagreement resolved: keep 1.5 s. Fable's conclusion is right, its premise is wrong.

Fable argued a dead loopback port gives instant ECONNREFUSED, so failover needs no shorter timeout. **Measured on this box just now:**

```

59999 (dead, never used)    2039.5 ms  ConnectionRefusedError [WinError 10061]
48056 (live host)               0.6 ms  connected
```

A dead loopback port takes **~2040 ms** to refuse here, not microseconds. That is precisely why 5,099 of 5,103 logged failures read `<urlopen error timed out>` and only 3 read anything else — the 1.5 s deadline expires ~540 ms *before* Windows surfaces the RST. The hook has never once seen a refusal.

**Decision: keep `timeout=1.5`.** My 0.75 s proposal is withdrawn, for reasons the measurement supplies rather than Fable's:

- 1.5 s already caps the dead-port cost *below* the 2040 ms OS refusal, so shortening buys 750 ms, not 2 s. Small prize.
- Against that: 0.6 ms live vs 750 ms budget looks like a huge margin, but I have **no p99 measurement of live-host response latency** on this emulated ARM64 box, and the healthy host's 8 errors in 19,459 posts prove slow responses exist. Trading an unmeasured correctness risk for 750 ms is a bad trade.
- "Never worse than today" is the right bar for a fix. 1.5 s meets it exactly.

Two bounds adopted from Sol instead:

- **Total probe budget 4000 ms** across all candidates, checked before each attempt. Worst realistic case (2 candidates) = 3 s, inside budget; a pathological manifest set cannot turn one hook event into a 10 s stall. On budget exhaustion: stop, log, treat as undelivered.

## 4. Risks

- **Duplicate delivery** if a slow live host processes a request we abandoned and the next candidate also accepts. Two identical broadcasts: harmless on the dot axes, and the companion path is already protected — the retry re-sends the *same* `companionLifecycleEventId`, which the sink matches against its applied-id window (`pane-map-hook.ts:2543-2555`). Bounded further by keeping 1.5 s.
- **Foreign server on a recycled port** answering 200 with arbitrary text: rejected by positive envelope parsing. This is the concrete reason the polarity flip matters.
- **All-ignored** on a genuinely wedged pane: one log line per event, no error spam, no retry. Matches notify.sh.
- **Marker fence residual**: a question whose marker write and our `stat` interleave inside one mtime tick. NTFS granularity ~100 ns against a multi-millisecond mutation; not a practical window. A `stat` failure never deletes.
- **Dismissal is still allowed to drop a live red** — the reds that existed at click time. That is the user's explicit decision. The fence narrows it to exactly that set; it is no longer an unbounded race, and I am not claiming it self-heals.
- **`pendingAfter: true`** means a newer question survived the dismissal. The renderer must not present that terminal as cleared; surface it rather than hide it.
- **Total probe budget** could in principle truncate a legitimate multi-org probe. 4 s against two 1.5 s candidates leaves headroom; log on exhaustion.
- **Host-down click**: green clears, red/yellow stay, toast fires. Deliberate, stated above.
- **Three similarly-named functions** (host `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, renderer `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, new `dismissWorkspaceStatuses`). The collision already caused this bug — cross-reference all three in comments.
- No schema change, no migration, no new persisted key (`partialize`, `store.ts:745-753`, already covers the maps).

## 0. Disagreement resolved: keep 1.5 s. Fable's conclusion is right, its premise is wrong.

Fable argued a dead loopback port gives instant ECONNREFUSED, so failover needs no shorter timeout. **Measured on this box just now:**

```
55331 (dead, was the host)  2043.6 ms  ConnectionRefusedError [WinError 10061]
59999 (dead, never used)    2039.5 ms  ConnectionRefusedError [WinError 10061]
48056 (live host)               0.6 ms  connected
```

A dead loopback port takes **~2040 ms** to refuse here, not microseconds. That is precisely why 5,099 of 5,103 logged failures read `<urlopen error timed out>` and only 3 read anything else — the 1.5 s deadline expires ~540 ms *before* Windows surfaces the RST. The hook has never once seen a refusal.

**Decision: keep `timeout=1.5`.** My 0.75 s proposal is withdrawn, for reasons the measurement supplies rather than Fable's:

- 1.5 s already caps the dead-port cost *below* the 2040 ms OS refusal, so shortening buys 750 ms, not 2 s. Small prize.
- Against that: 0.6 ms live vs 750 ms budget looks like a huge margin, but I have **no p99 measurement of live-host response latency** on this emulated ARM64 box, and the healthy host's 8 errors in 19,459 posts prove slow responses exist. Trading an unmeasured correctness risk for 750 ms is a bad trade.
- "Never worse than today" is the right bar for a fix. 1.5 s meets it exactly.

Two bounds adopted from Sol instead:

- **Total probe budget 4000 ms** across all candidates, checked before each attempt. Worst realistic case (2 candidates) = 3 s, inside budget; a pathological manifest set cannot turn one hook event into a 10 s stall. On budget exhaustion: stop, log, treat as undelivered.

## 4. Risks

- **Duplicate delivery** if a slow live host processes a request we abandoned and the next candidate also accepts. Two identical broadcasts: harmless on the dot axes, and the companion path is already protected — the retry re-sends the *same* `companionLifecycleEventId`, which the sink matches against its applied-id window (`pane-map-hook.ts:2543-2555`). Bounded further by keeping 1.5 s.
- **Foreign server on a recycled port** answering 200 with arbitrary text: rejected by positive envelope parsing. This is the concrete reason the polarity flip matters.
- **All-ignored** on a genuinely wedged pane: one log line per event, no error spam, no retry. Matches notify.sh.
- **Marker fence residual**: a question whose marker write and our `stat` interleave inside one mtime tick. NTFS granularity ~100 ns against a multi-millisecond mutation; not a practical window. A `stat` failure never deletes.
- **Dismissal is still allowed to drop a live red** — the reds that existed at click time. That is the user's explicit decision. The fence narrows it to exactly that set; it is no longer an unbounded race, and I am not claiming it self-heals.
- **`pendingAfter: true`** means a newer question survived the dismissal. The renderer must not present that terminal as cleared; surface it rather than hide it.
- **Total probe budget** could in principle truncate a legitimate multi-org probe. 4 s against two 1.5 s candidates leaves headroom; log on exhaustion.
- **Host-down click**: green clears, red/yellow stay, toast fires. Deliberate, stated above.
- **Three similarly-named functions** (host `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, renderer `clearWorkspaceStatuses`, new `dismissWorkspaceStatuses`). The collision already caused this bug — cross-reference all three in comments.

- C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.test.ts

FIX-1 (strip-retry dead code). `_deliver` now catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` separately: sets `saw_response`, records `http_error = "HTTP <code> from <url>"`, logs `hook-candidate-http-error`, continues. `_undelivered` carries `superset_saw_response` (renamed from `superset_saw_2xx`; no readers left). Retry gate at the call site is now "a server answered", not "2xx with body". Outcome tuples are 5-wide: `("delivered", url, status, raw, http_error)` / `("ignored-everywhere", None, None, last_ignored_body, http_error)`. When the sweep concludes ignored-everywhere BUT saw an HTTP error status, the stripped retry runs first — a foreign host's `ignored:true` can no longer mask the owner's 400. With no companion to strip, that same case is reported as post-error instead of a delivered no-op.

FIX-2 (bogus ignored-everywhere). New `_hook_ignored(raw)` — valid envelope with `ignored is True` only. `saw_ignored` (not `saw_2xx`) gates the ignored-everywhere return. Malformed/foreign/204/HTML 2xx bodies now fall through to the raise path → post-error.

FIX-3 (budget overshoot). `_post_hook(url, body, timeout)`; `_deliver` passes `min(1.5, 4.0 - elapsed)` per attempt and skips once `remaining <= 0`. Per-candidate cap still 1.5s. Budget log gained `elapsedMs`. Worst case is now ~4.0s, was up to ~5.4s.

FIX-4 (stale manifests). New `_pid_alive(pid)`; `_hook_candidate_urls` skips a manifest whose `pid` is a positive int and provably dead, logging `hook-candidate-manifest-dead-pid`. Windows path uses ctypes `OpenProcess(0x1000, 0, pid)` with explicit `c_void_p` restype, `CloseHandle` on success, and `GetLastError() != 87` so ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (elevated/other-user host) stays a candidate. No `os.kill(pid, 0)` anywhere. POSIX branch uses `os.kill(pid, 0)`. Fails open on any error, inside the per-manifest try.

FIX-5 (lost diagnostic body). `_deliver` carries `last_ignored_body` out; both the `ignored-everywhere` and `companion-rejected-dot-ignored-everywhere` records now include `responseBody`.

Tests: 59 pass / 0 fail / 366 expect() across 2 files, 28.1s (`bun test apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/`). Was 54 tests; 5 added:
- owner 400 → stripped retry fires → dot delivered (`companion-rejected-dot-posted`, no post-error)
- owner 400 + foreign `ignored:true` → retry still fires, zero `ignored-everywhere` records
- malformed-2xx-only sweep → post-error, not ignored-everywhere
- manifest with a dead pid is skipped (sink never hit)
- manifest with our own live pid is kept and delivers
Plus two existing tests extended: `ignored-everywhere` now asserts `responseBody` contains the host's reason, and the budget test asserts `elapsedMs <= 4200`. New sink mode `reject-companion` (400 when the body carries companion fields, else accept) and `writeHostManifest` gained an optional pid param.

`node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` → all 241 markers present. Embedded Python compiles clean (`py_compile`).

Deviations / notes worth your call:
1. I added one behaviour the brief did not list: ignored-everywhere + an HTTP error status + NO companion fields is now reported as post-error rather than a delivered no-op. Same masking bug, no retry available to run, so reporting it was the only honest option.
2. New comment marker token `(HOOK-STALE-MANIFEST)` on the pid code. Not in FEATURES.md — I was scoped out of that file, and the gate does not object. Add it there if you want it protected.
3. The pid probe runs while the candidate list is built, so it costs one OpenProcess syscall per manifest plus a one-time ctypes import even when the env URL is live. The list already read every manifest from disk unconditionally, so the fast path is unchanged in shape; I did not restructure to defer it.
4. `_deliver`'s failure message changed from "no hook endpoint answered" to "no hook endpoint accepted the event" — no test asserted on it, and it is now accurate.
</agent-message>

- `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion/app-phone/src/main/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/phone/ui/question/QuestionSheet.kt`
  - :83 `QuestionSheet(state, nowMs, onDismiss, onChoose, …)` — a `ModalBottomSheet` (:96) containing ONE `LazyColumn` (:102).

  - :110 context block, :123-140 question blocks, :142 footer.

## 2. What's on the wire per question — the answer to the core question
`/v1/question` (§7.4, `PROTOCOL.md:1683-1721`) returns `QuestionResponse.source` = **IDs ONLY**:
- Kotlin: `core/…/protocol/Question.kt:52-59` `QuestionSource(projectId, workspaceId, terminalId, agentKind, subagent)`.

No names. Same for the event-stream `QuestionSummary` (`types.ts:930-941`) and the tree's `PendingQuestionRef`.

- project name + workspace name: YES, from the cached tree. `/v1/tree` carries `Project.name` and `Workspace.name` (`core/…/protocol/Tree.kt:66-100`). Resolvable by the ids in `source`.

The renderer pushes a per-workspace snapshot of tab titles; `AlertContextRegistry.lookup(hostWorkspaceId, hostTerminalId) → {tabTitle, tabCount}` (:113-130). Created `index.ts:726`. Resolver `index.ts:754-796 resolveAlertContext()` already returns `{terminalHandle, projectName, workspaceName, tabTitle, tabCount}` — project/workspace off host.db (`findWorkspace`/`findProject`), tab off the registry, never throws, every field degrades independently.
It is wired ONLY into the push path (`index.ts:854 resolveContext`). `ReadDeps` (`read-api.ts:399-431`) has no reference to it, and neither does QuestionStore.

## 4. Watch

`sourceLabel` is minted ON THE PHONE, not by the host: `app-phone/…/phone/wear/WatchBridge.kt:667-673`
```kotlin
private fun sourceLabelFor(source: QuestionSource): String? {
    val snapshot = repository.tree.value
    val project = snapshot.projects.firstOrNull { it.projectId == source.projectId } ?: return null
    val workspace = project.workspaces.firstOrNull { it.workspaceId == source.workspaceId }
        ?: return project.name
    return "${project.name} / ${workspace.name}"
}
```
This is the reusable helper. Watch gets a tab name for free only if it's added to `WatchQuestion` (`core/…/wear/WearProtocol.kt:297` currently has `sourceLabel: String?` and nothing else) — the wire class is enumerated by tests (`WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt:56` asserts exact JSON), so a new field breaks those goldens.

## 5. Minimal change surface
**Project + workspace names: client-only, zero host/protocol change.**
1. Hoist `sourceLabelFor` out of `WatchBridge.kt:667` into a shared helper (e.g. beside `AgentTree.kt:384 findTerminal` / `:426 findTerminalForQuestion`), taking `(TreeSnapshot, QuestionSource)`.
2. Resolve in `CompanionShell.kt` (already has `tree` at :57) and pass into `QuestionSheet`, or store on `QuestionSheetState` at install time (`ConversationViewModel.kt:250-265`; the VM already reads `repository.tree` in `watchOpenSheet`).
