4. Same names into `ChatScreen.kt:110-120` TopAppBar (already pinned — add a subtitle line; needs 2 new params on `ChatScreen` + `AgentsPane`).

**Tab name: requires a host-side addition.** Cheapest correct route: thread `resolveAlertContext`'s tab lookup into the question read and add ONE optional field to `QuestionResponse.source`:
- `packages/host-service/src/companion/types.ts:900` add `tabTitle?: string` (+ optionally `tabCount`).
- `question-store.ts:1713 resolveSource` (or `toResponse` at :2137) call a new injected `resolveTabTitle(hostWorkspaceId, hostTerminalId)`; wire the registry through `createReadApi` (`index.ts:1004`) / QuestionStore deps. Must never throw — mirror `index.ts:754`'s degrade-per-field contract.
- Kotlin: `core/…/protocol/Question.kt:52-59` add `val tabTitle: String? = null`; `BridgeMapping.kt:206-220` maps it. **Forward-compatible both ways** — `CompanionJson.kt:25 ignoreUnknownKeys = true`, and the Kotlin default covers an older bridge that omits it. No protocol version bump needed; §7.4 in PROTOCOL.md needs the doc edit.

## 6. Notes / gotchas
- Vocabulary inversion, stated at `AgentTree.kt:36-39`: `UserLabels.PROJECT = "Workspace"`. In CODE `project` = repo row, `workspace` = branch/worktree; the user says these the other way round. Whatever gets pinned should follow the push's own wording — title `<project> · <workspace>`, tab named separately — so app and notification agree.
- Name resolution can return null: a question opened from a push is routinely absent from the last tree (noted at `ConversationViewModel.kt:~58-64` on `openedAtMs`), and `sourceLabelFor` returns null when the project isn't in the snapshot. Header must degrade to nothing rather than render `" · "`. Precedent: `AlertContext.kt:43 isNamed` is all-or-nothing for exactly this.
- `AlertContext.kt:52 namesTab` gates the tab on `tabCount >= 2` for notifications. In-app the disambiguation argument is weaker; decide explicitly rather than inheriting it.
- Tab titles are process-local and non-durable on the host (`push-context.ts:22-26`) — a host-service restart empties the registry until the renderer re-syncs, so tab name is best-effort by construction.
- Privacy: names in a push are covered by a NARROW waiver; `AlertContext.kt:14-18` forbids names in `toString`, exceptions and logs. A tab title added to `/v1/question` rides the sealed AES-256-GCM channel (not FCM), so it's outside the waiver's blast radius — but keep it out of `read-api.ts:1413`'s `companion.question.served` log line.
- `FEATURES.md:23` `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` is a marker-gated feature; markers listed at `FEATURES.md:236-240`. Any host-side edit here must keep those markers.

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

ALTITUDE REVIEW — agent-status-dot diff. 6 findings, all fixable in-diff, none change behavior. Plus verdicts on the 4 suspects you named.

## Findings

**1. HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:145-157, 202-284, 411-427, 497-510 — hand-rolled single-flight spread across 4 bare refs.**
`resyncInFlightTokenRef` / `queuedResyncKeyRef` / `resyncDeadlineTimerRef` / `periodicTimerRef` have one invariant ("they move together") enforced at 4 sites. Two blocks are verbatim duplicates: the abandon triple (422-427 == 505-510) and the drain sequence (221-228 == 272-281). Cost: any future edit to the gate has to be made twice in each pair, and a missed copy leaks the gate for the life of the socket — the exact failure the deadline exists to prevent. The token is also a second copy of generation semantics `resyncGenerationRef` already owns.
Right form: one closure/object in-file owning `{token, queuedKey, deadlineTimer}` with `begin(gen)`, `settle(gen)`, `abandon()`. The four sites become one call each; the periodic tick's suppression check becomes `flight.busy`.

**2. pane-map-hook.ts:2472-2555 (`_deliver`) + 2962-3013 (`main`) — `_deliver`'s verdict is finished by its caller, twice.**
`("ignored-everywhere", …, http_error)` with a non-None `http_error` is never a success, and `main()` says so in two places (2971-2978 and 3006-3013). The second comment names the duplication itself: "SAME promotion the first sweep makes below". Cost: the rule that decides whether a dot was delivered lives outside the function that gathered the evidence, so both call sites must stay in sync and a third caller of `_deliver` would silently inherit the wrong verdict.
Right form: `_deliver` raises `_undelivered(...)` when `saw_ignored and http_error`. Both promotion blocks delete; the first sweep still triggers the companion retry via `exc is not None and saw_response`, the retry still lands in `except: exc = retry_exc`. Same outcomes, one owner. The tuple collapses to 4 fields.

**3. pane-map-hook.ts:2962-3040 — positional indexing of a 5-tuple across ~80 lines.**
`outcome[4]`, `retry_outcome[3]`, `outcome[1]` appear 12 times. Cost: reordering or extending the tuple is a silent breakage, and the reader must hold the field order from 2476-2478 in their head through the whole tail of `main()`.
Right form: `collections.namedtuple("_Delivery", "kind url status body http_error")`. Pure rename; pairs naturally with #2.

**4. pane-map-hook.ts:415-427 vs 447-457 — the log-rotation block is now duplicated verbatim.**
The diff copies `_decision_log`'s 10-line stat/unlink/rename idiom into `_log` and the comment says so ("the same idiom as `_decision_log` below"). Cost: two files rotate under two copies of the same 1MB rule; the next tweak (size, backup count) gets applied to one.
Right form: `def _rotate(log_path, backup_path):` above both, called from each. Both callers already swallow all exceptions, so the extraction is mechanical.

**5. pane-map-hook.ts:2456-2470 — `_undelivered` staples attributes onto whatever exception it was handed.**
`exc.superset_saw_response = ...` on an arbitrary caught exception, read back with `getattr(exc, "superset_saw_response", False)` at 2958, inside a `try/except: pass` because some exception types reject attribute assignment. Cost: the signal that decides whether the companion retry runs at all can vanish silently — a `__slots__`-bearing exception makes the retry dead in exactly the case it exists for, with no log line. `superset_tried_urls` (2466) is set and never read anywhere — dead payload the diff adds.
Right form: `class _HookUndelivered(RuntimeError)` with `saw_response` as a real field and the original as `__cause__`; `main()` tests `isinstance`. Drop `superset_tried_urls` (the candidate list is already logged at 3046).

**6. store.ts:690-741 — third copy of the same filter-a-map-by-workspace loop.**
`sources`, `backgroundRunningTerminals` and the diff's new `shellRunningTerminals` are three structurally identical loops with three parallel `changed` flags, then three `if (xChanged)` assigns. Cost: adding a fourth workspace-keyed map (the pattern is clearly growing — this diff added the third) means a fourth copy plus a fourth flag in the early-return condition, and forgetting the flag makes the purge silently partial.
Right form: `function omitByWorkspace<T extends {workspaceId: string}>(map: Record<string,T>, workspaceId: string): [Record<string,T>, boolean]` in-file; three calls, and the early return folds to checking the three booleans it returns.

## Lower-value, listing for completeness

- **agent-status-snapshot.ts:123, 180** — `ClearMarkersDeps` injects `stat` only, while `readdir` (193, 245), `unlink` (230) and `rmdir` (259) stay hard-bound. The seam is shaped by which branches the tests wanted rather than by what the function depends on; the double-readdir race the docstring calls load-bearing is the one thing it can't drive. Either inject all four or none.
- **companion/index.ts:1762** — `QuestionCaptureSink & Pick<CompanionQuestionSink, "dismissByTerminal">`. The only consumer (index.ts:1163) passes it to `setCompanionQuestionSink`, which wants a `CompanionQuestionSink`. Declaring that directly says the same thing and stops the reader chasing two interfaces to learn one object's shape.

## Suspects you named — cleared

- **`lastEventType !== "PermissionRequest"` guard (resyncAgentStatus.ts:719)** — right layer. The evidence it needs is already on the row; pushing it host-side would mean folding binding-state inference into `pendingPermission`, whose documented contract (snapshot.ts:27-32) is a clean statement about the marker directory only. Only nit: "leave the axis alone" now has two disjoint paths (`null`, and `false` + PermissionRequest) with no shared name. Not worth churn.
- **`pendingAfter` re-latch (useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts, `applyWorkspaceStatusDismissal`)** — right layer. Purge and re-latch are back-to-back synchronous `getState()` calls, so there is no visible intermediate state, and pushing an exclusion set into the store action would generalize a store primitive for one caller.
- **`dismissStartedAtMs` threading** — already single-owner. Captured once in `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` and passed down; the two consumers fence different things (mtime vs `askedAtMs`) and neither can re-derive the other's. Explicit param is correct.
- **ignored-everywhere/http_error promotion in `main()` vs `_deliver`** — you were right, that's finding #2.

Note in passing, not a finding: the removed `clearV2TerminalRunStatus` (store.ts) had zero callers at HEAD despite its docstring claiming two, so deleting it is dead-code removal, not a regression — `clearInterruptedTerminalAxes` is not a relocation of a live helper.

Cost: small but multiplied by manifest count per event; first `import ctypes` in the process is the expensive part and is already unavoidable, the reload is not.
Cheaper: module-level lazy singleton (`_KERNEL32 = None`, initialize once).

**E5. `stat()` per `_log` call for rotation.** `pane-map-hook.ts:418` — `_log` is on by default (only `SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG == "0"` silences it) and is called several times per event, each now paying a `stat` before the append.
Cost: N stats per process where 1 suffices — a hook process writes a handful of lines totalling <10KB, so it cannot cross 1MB mid-process.
Cheaper: module-level `_ROTATION_CHECKED` flag; check once per process. Rotation guarantee is unchanged.

**E6. The 60s periodic resync turns a rare store-write storm into a permanent per-minute one.** `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:57` + `:449` → `resyncAgentStatus.ts` row loop → `store.ts:445 applySourceAxes`. `applySourceAxes` has NO no-op short-circuit: when the derived status is unchanged it still builds a fresh entry object and calls `set`, which (a) invalidates `sources` for every dot subscriber, (b) triggers the `persist` middleware to JSON-serialize all seven slices into sessionStorage, and (c) emits an `ndots` `console.info` that the main process forwards into electron-log (`store.ts:464`, `store.ts:23`). Previously this ran only on reconnect; now it runs for every row, every 60s, per host, for the life of the session.
Cost: with R agent terminals, R store writes + R full sessionStorage serializations + R main.log lines per host per minute (~1,440 × R log lines/day) with nothing changed. Same unbounded-log shape the diff just fixed in the Python hook.
Cheaper, in order of safety:
 1. Silence the log on no-change: skip `ndots` when `prev` exists, `from === to` and the axis map is unchanged. `resyncAgentStatus` already emits a summary line per resync. No state semantics touched.
 2. Coalesce the persist write: wrap `createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)` with a `setItem` that defers via a queued microtask/`setTimeout(0)`, so one resync pass writes storage once instead of R times. In-memory state and every fence are untouched.
 3. NOT recommended without a correctness pass: an equality short-circuit in `applySourceAxes` returning the existing entry object. It would kill the churn at the source, but `sources` entry IDENTITY is the resync sweep's staleness fence ("byte-for-byte the object that was there before the request went out"), so it changes what the sweep concludes. Flagging as available, not as safe.

**E7. Per-terminal dismiss reads every terminal row in the workspace.** `packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/terminal-agents/terminal-agents.ts:211-217` — the query filters on `originWorkspaceId` only and then `.filter()`s down to `input.terminalId` in JS. The right-click-one-terminal path is the common caller.
Cost: a full workspace row set materialized to drop all but one.
Cheaper: `and(eq(terminalSessions.originWorkspaceId, ...), eq(terminalSessions.id, input.terminalId))` when the id is present. Same DB-is-the-source-of-truth guarantee — the id is still intersected server-side, never trusted from the client.

**E8. Nits, low value.** `store.ts:669-684` — the new logging block iterates all sources in a pass separate from the `set()` that follows; one extra O(sources) walk per dismissal (rare, user-gesture-only). `agent-status-snapshot.ts` `clearPendingQuestionMarkers` — `survivors.includes(owner)` inside the `remaining` loop is O(n²); n is 1-3 owners, so this is cosmetic (`Set`).

**Considered and REJECTED — do not let anyone "optimize" these:**
- Parallelizing the per-terminal loop in `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` (`terminal-agents.ts:220`). The abort message names exactly the terminals that completed BEFORE the failure; concurrency makes that list meaningless and changes which terminals get swept on a fault.
- One parent `readdir(~/.superset/agent-subagent-running)` to skip terminals with no marker dir. It would collapse N ENOENT readdirs into 1, but a dir created between the parent listing and the per-terminal call would be invisible → `pendingAfter: false` for a question raised after the click. That is the exact fence the change exists to hold.

**OUT OF ANGLE, but found and load-bearing — route to a correctness reviewer.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2301` defines `_pid_alive`, and `pane-map-hook.ts:736` ALREADY defines `_pid_alive` in the same emitted Python module (NOTIFY_SCRIPT spans ~370-3068). The new definition shadows the old one, so the existing codex-job caller at `pane-map-hook.ts:880` now runs the manifest implementation. They are not equivalent: the old one returns True for `pid <= 0` (new returns False), and the old one checks `GetExitCodeProcess == STILL_ACTIVE` so an exited-but-still-openable process reads dead, while the new one calls any successful `OpenProcess` alive — which would pin a codex hold's dot. Efficiency-wise it is also a dead duplicate definition.

Everything else in the diff (HostNotificationSubscriber refs/timers, `useEffectEvent` closures, `companion-question-sink` forwarding, `applyWorkspaceStatusDismissal`'s fire-and-forget per-terminal reports) is clean — no captured-scope leaks, no sequential work that should be concurrent, no added startup blocking.

Trace re-verified against both repos. Two corrections to it, both material, flagged inline below.

---

## 1. Recommended approach

**Host puts the names on the wire; clients render them. No client-side join for the question sheet.**

Two host emissions, both fed by resolvers that already exist:

- **MUST** — `/v1/question` `source` gains `projectName`, `workspaceName`, `tabTitle`. Resolved by the EXISTING `resolveAlertContext` (`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts:754`), injected into `ReadDeps`.
- **SHOULD** — `/v1/tree` `Terminal` gains `tabTitle?`. Resolved by `alertContexts.lookup` (`...\companion\push-context.ts:121`), injected as a second narrow dep.

### Correction 1 to the trace: the sheet must NOT resolve project/workspace from the cached tree

The trace's option (a) says hoist `sourceLabelFor` and resolve project+workspace client-side from `/v1/tree`. That fails in the primary flow. Their own code says so: `...\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\ConversationViewModel.kt:55-62` — *"a question opened from a push is routinely absent from the last tree simply for having been captured after it."* And `CompanionShell.kt:98-108` opens the sheet regardless of whether `tree.findTerminalForQuestion` resolved.

So the notification-tap path — the main way the sheet opens — is exactly the path where a tree-derived header renders nothing. Since the host is already resolving all three names for the push that woke the phone, sending them in the question response makes the sheet self-sufficient: no join, no staleness, no fallback ladder to drift.

Cost: 3 strings on the sealed channel. No new privacy class — `/v1/tree` already carries project and workspace names in the clear over that channel (`Tree.kt:66-100`), and FCM already carries all three under the 2026-08-16 waiver.

### Correction 2: without the tree change, the chat screen cannot name the tab

`ChatScreen`'s title is `terminal.title` (`ChatScreen.kt:112-116`), which the host derives as literally `"Claude"`/`"Codex"`/`"Agent"`/`"Shell"` (`read-api.ts:738-742`). Two Claude tabs in one workspace stay indistinguishable. Chat's project+workspace ARE derivable client-side (a chat terminal is by construction in the tree, `CompanionShell.kt:117`), so the tree only needs `tabTitle`.

I would ship both in one host commit. They share the same registry, the same commit, one FEATURES.md row. If the tree half is dropped, chat gets `Project · Workspace` under `"Claude"` and the tab ambiguity survives — say so explicitly rather than calling the feature done.

- **tabTitle on `QuestionSource` only, project/workspace from the tree** (the trace's minimal). Loses: dead header on the notification-tap path (above).
- **Resolve in `question-store.ts` `resolveSource`** (`question-store.ts:1713`). Loses: `resolveSource` also feeds `summarize()` (`:1671-1694`), which builds the §9.4 event-stream summary — the one projection contractually carrying no content. Injecting the renderer name cache there puts a private name one line away from the broadcast stream. Also: 6 test files construct `QuestionStoreDeps`, vs 2 for `ReadDeps` (`curation-gates.test.ts:1483`, `session-tree.test.ts:79`). `toResponse` has exactly one caller (`read-api.ts:1407`), so nothing is lost by resolving at the serving boundary.
- **Names on the tree only, sheet reads the tree.** Same cold-tree failure as the trace's (a).
- **Reuse core `AlertContext` for the in-app header.** Its `parse`/validation is FCM-map-shaped and its `namesTab` rule (`AlertContext.kt:52`, tabCount >= 2) is the wrong rule in-app. Reuse only the separator constant.

---

## 3. Data flow

### Question sheet (the flow that matters)

```
renderer  --tab-title snapshot-->  AlertContextRegistry.sync()   [validated: workspace membership,
                                   push-context.ts:120              <=256 terminals, <=512 chars]
push       --FCM v3-->  phone notification  (unchanged)
user taps  --questionId-->  CompanionShell:98  -->  ConversationViewModel.openQuestion:250
```

Validation sits at two boundaries and nowhere else: the registry's `sync` (already there, refuses a whole bad snapshot rather than truncating), and Kotlin deserialization with defaults. Nothing new is persisted — the registry is process-local memory by design (`push-context.ts:22-27`).

### Watch

Another Claude session sent a message:
<agent-message from="simp-simple">
SIMPLIFICATION REVIEW (quality only, no correctness hunt). 14 findings, ordered by value.

**1. `apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2301` — second `def _pid_alive(pid)` in the SAME embedded script; shadows the pre-existing one at :736.**
Both are module-level inside NOTIFY_SCRIPT (312-3068). Python binds at call time → the (BF) codex-stale-job call at :880 now runs the NEW body, not the one written for it. Bodies differ: old returns False when OpenProcess fails and also checks GetExitCodeProcess/STILL_ACTIVE; new returns True unless GetLastError==87 and never checks exit code.
Simpler form: rename the new one `_manifest_pid_alive`, or fold the manifest case into the existing function. Flagging under duplication, but it crosses into behavior — worth a correctness reviewer confirming.

**2. `pane-map-hook.ts:2472-2560` + `:2956-3045` — `_deliver` returns a 5-tuple read positionally at 14 sites (`outcome[0]`, `outcome[3]`, `outcome[4]`, `retry_outcome[1..4]`).**
Two positions are dead in the "ignored-everywhere" arm (url/status always None), and `[4]` (http_error) vs `[3]` (body) is unguessable at the call site.
Simpler form: return a dict — `{"kind":…, "url":…, "status":…, "body":…, "http_error":…}`. Same values, call sites become `outcome["kind"]`.

**3. `pane-map-hook.ts:2425-2454` — `_hook_accepted` / `_hook_ignored` are the same 6 lines twice, differing only in `is False` vs `is True`.**
Simpler form: one `_hook_ignored_flag(raw)` returning True/False/None (None = unparsable/foreign). `_hook_accepted(raw)` becomes `flag is False`, `_hook_ignored(raw)` becomes `flag is True`. Also halves the parse work per response.

**4. `pane-map-hook.ts:405-431` — the new 1MB rotation block in `_log` is a verbatim copy of `_decision_log`'s at :443-457** (its own comment says so). 14 duplicated lines, and the `backup.exists()/unlink()` dance is redundant.
Simpler form: one `_rotate(log_path, backup_path)` helper called by both, body `if log_path.stat().st_size > 1048576: log_path.replace(backup)` — `Path.replace` overwrites on Windows too, so the exists/unlink/try-except goes away entirely.

**5. `pane-map-hook.ts:2456-2469` — `superset_tried_urls` is written and never read anywhere in the repo.**
Dead. Simpler form: drop the attribute and the `tried` parameter of `_undelivered`; callers already build the count into the message themselves.

**6. `pane-map-hook.ts:3013` — `retry_after or outcome[4]`: `retry_after` is provably None at this line.**
Every truthy-`retry_after` path either returns (:2991/:3002) or sets `exc` (:2978, :3004), and the guard is `exc is None`. Simpler form: `exc = RuntimeError(outcome[4])`.

**7. `pane-map-hook.ts:2499/2550` — `saw_ignored` is derivable from `last_ignored_body is not None`.**
`_hook_ignored(raw)` can only be true for a parsable non-empty body, so the two are always set together. Simpler form: drop the flag, test `last_ignored_body is not None`.

**8. `pane-map-hook.ts:2971-2978` vs `:3006-3013` — the "ignored-everywhere that also saw an http_error is really a refusal" promotion is written twice**, with near-identical 8-line comments. Simpler form: one `_promote_masked_refusal(outcome)` returning an exception or None, called on both sweeps.

**9. `pane-map-hook.ts:2374-2382` — this terminal's own org manifest is appended, then the glob re-adds the same path**, so it is opened, JSON-parsed and `_pid_alive`-probed twice on every hook event. Dedupe is only on the resulting URL. Simpler form: track seen paths (`if manifest_path in seen_paths: continue`) alongside the existing `seen` URL set.

**10. `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:220-227` vs `:267-280` — release-the-gate-and-drain-the-queue is written twice** (owner check → clear deadline timer → null token → run queued key). Simpler form: one `releaseResyncGate(generation)` effect-event called from both the `finally` and the deadline timer.

**11. `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:422-426` vs `:505-509` — the abandon block (null token, null queued key, clear deadline timer) is duplicated verbatim** between the disconnect branch and unmount, with `periodicTimerRef` teardown duplicated a third time at :411-413. Simpler form: one `abandonResync()` covering all four refs, called from both.

**12. `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:145` — `resyncInFlightTokenRef` carries no information beyond null-ness.** While non-null it always equals `resyncGenerationRef.current` (the generation is bumped and the token set with no await between, and the gate blocks a bump while non-null). Simpler form: a boolean `resyncInFlightRef`, ownership test `resyncInFlightRef.current && resyncGenerationRef.current === generation`. Low priority — the token makes the invariant explicit and the win is one ref; listing it because you asked which refs are derivable. The other three (queue, deadline, generation) are not.

**13. `apps/desktop/src/renderer/stores/v2-notifications/store.ts:668-745` — three copy-paste map-purge loops in one action** (sources, backgroundRunningTerminals, shellRunningTerminals), each with its own `changed` flag; the last two operate on the identical `Record<string, V2ShellRunningEntry>` type and identical predicate. Simpler form: `const dropWorkspace = <T extends {workspaceId: string}>(map: Record<string,T>, id: string) => {next, changed}` used for all three. Also `:669-687` duplicates the ndots snapshot loop from `clearWorkspaceAttention` at :750+ — one `logWorkspaceSourceClears(mutation, workspaceId, predicate)` covers both.

**14. Smaller ones:**
- `packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/terminal-agents/terminal-agents.ts:211-217` — reads every terminal row for the workspace then `.filter()`s in JS to at most one. Simpler: `and(eq(originWorkspaceId,…), input.terminalId ? eq(id, input.terminalId) : undefined)` in the `where`.
- `packages/host-service/src/companion/index.ts:1762` — return type `QuestionCaptureSink & Pick<CompanionQuestionSink, "dismissByTerminal">` is an ad-hoc intersection at the signature. Simpler: name it once (`type NotifyingCaptureSink = …`) next to the interface.
- `HostNotificationSubscriber.test.tsx:131-132` re-declares `PERIODIC_RESYNC_MS` / `RESYNC_DEADLINE_MS` as literals. Export them from the component module and import, so a tuning change cannot silently pass a stale test.
- `useFolderFirstImport.test.ts:36-43` and `useFileContent.test.ts:21-28` carry a byte-identical 5-line comment + `realReact` spread. Two copies only — extract a shared `spreadReactMock` helper if a third appears.
- `packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/notifications/agent-status-dismiss.test.ts:92` contains a RAW NUL byte inside the test string (`"t\0x"` written literally). `file` reports the source as `data` and `grep -r` skips it as binary — I had to use `--text` to search it. Simpler: write the escape `"t\0x"`; same value, file stays text.

Clean elsewhere: `clearPendingQuestionMarkers`' removed/survivors arrays are justified (tests assert the owner names), the new hook test file is well factored around its helpers, and no leftover callers of the deleted `clearV2TerminalRunStatus` exist.
</agent-message>

<agent-message from="simp-eff">
EFFICIENCY REVIEW — uncommitted diff. 8 findings + 1 out-of-angle. Ranked by cost.

**E1. Manifest failover is EAGER on the hook fast path.** `apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2927` — `candidates = _hook_candidate_urls(url)` runs unconditionally, before the first POST. So EVERY hook event does: `host_dir.glob("*/manifest.json")` + open/read/`json.loads` per manifest + `_pid_alive` per manifest — even when the env URL is live and accepts on attempt 1 (the overwhelming case; the probe list exists only for the restart-onto-a-new-port case).
Cost: ~3-8ms per hook event on Windows ARM64 (1 readdir + N file reads + N `ctypes.WinDLL` loads + OpenProcess/CloseHandle), on the path that blocks the agent, at every PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Notification.
Cheaper: make the tail lazy. `_deliver` already consumes in order and only advances on failure — yield the env URL first and enumerate manifests only when the consumer asks for candidate #2. Memoize the enumerated tail at module level so the (COMPANION-CAPTURE) retry sweep reuses it without re-reading disk. Caveat: the failure logs print `candidateUrls`; use the `tried` list `_deliver` already builds (identical in the all-dead test at `pane-map-hook.test.ts:998`, which enumerates everything anyway) — only the budget-exhausted log would name fewer URLs.

**E2. Own-org manifest is read and pid-probed twice, every event.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2379-2381` — `manifest_paths` appends `host_dir/<orgId>/manifest.json`, then `extend`s with `sorted(host_dir.glob("*/manifest.json"))`, which contains that same path. Dedup happens on the resulting URL (`_add`), not on the path, so the loop opens + parses + pid-probes the common-case manifest twice.
Cost: one extra file open+parse and one extra OpenProcess per event.
Cheaper: `seen_paths` set over `manifest_paths` before the loop.

**E3. Pid probe runs before the URL dedup check.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2405` vs `:2413` — `_pid_alive` is called, then `_add` discards the endpoint as a duplicate. In the healthy case the env URL IS the own-org manifest endpoint, so the probe is pure waste.
Cheaper: build `endpoint.rstrip("/") + "/trpc/notifications.hook"` first, `if url in seen: continue`, then probe. Only difference is that the dead-pid log line is not emitted for an endpoint already queued.

**E4. `ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32")` constructed per `_pid_alive` call.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2318` — plus three `argtypes`/`restype` assignments each time.
Cost: small but multiplied by manifest count per event; first `import ctypes` in the process is the expensive part and is already unavoidable, the reload is not.
Cheaper: module-level lazy singleton (`_KERNEL32 = None`, initialize once).

**E5. `stat()` per `_log` call for rotation.** `pane-map-hook.ts:418` — `_log` is on by default (only `SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG == "0"` silences it) and is called several times per event, each now paying a `stat` before the append.
Cost: N stats per process where 1 suffices — a hook process writes a handful of lines totalling <10KB, so it cannot cross 1MB mid-process.
Cheaper: module-level `_ROTATION_CHECKED` flag; check once per process. Rotation guarantee is unchanged.

**E6. The 60s periodic resync turns a rare store-write storm into a permanent per-minute one.** `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:57` + `:449` → `resyncAgentStatus.ts` row loop → `store.ts:445 applySourceAxes`. `applySourceAxes` has NO no-op short-circuit: when the derived status is unchanged it still builds a fresh entry object and calls `set`, which (a) invalidates `sources` for every dot subscriber, (b) triggers the `persist` middleware to JSON-serialize all seven slices into sessionStorage, and (c) emits an `ndots` `console.info` that the main process forwards into electron-log (`store.ts:464`, `store.ts:23`). Previously this ran only on reconnect; now it runs for every row, every 60s, per host, for the life of the session.
Cost: with R agent terminals, R store writes + R full sessionStorage serializations + R main.log lines per host per minute (~1,440 × R log lines/day) with nothing changed. Same unbounded-log shape the diff just fixed in the Python hook.
Cheaper, in order of safety:
 1. Silence the log on no-change: skip `ndots` when `prev` exists, `from === to` and the axis map is unchanged. `resyncAgentStatus` already emits a summary line per resync. No state semantics touched.
 2. Coalesce the persist write: wrap `createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)` with a `setItem` that defers via a queued microtask/`setTimeout(0)`, so one resync pass writes storage once instead of R times. In-memory state and every fence are untouched.
 3. NOT recommended without a correctness pass: an equality short-circuit in `applySourceAxes` returning the existing entry object. It would kill the churn at the source, but `sources` entry IDENTITY is the resync sweep's staleness fence ("byte-for-byte the object that was there before the request went out"), so it changes what the sweep concludes. Flagging as available, not as safe.

**E7. Per-terminal dismiss reads every terminal row in the workspace.** `packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/terminal-agents/terminal-agents.ts:211-217` — the query filters on `originWorkspaceId` only and then `.filter()`s down to `input.terminalId` in JS. The right-click-one-terminal path is the common caller.
Cost: a full workspace row set materialized to drop all but one.
Cheaper: `and(eq(terminalSessions.originWorkspaceId, ...), eq(terminalSessions.id, input.terminalId))` when the id is present. Same DB-is-the-source-of-truth guarantee — the id is still intersected server-side, never trusted from the client.

**E8. Nits, low value.** `store.ts:669-684` — the new logging block iterates all sources in a pass separate from the `set()` that follows; one extra O(sources) walk per dismissal (rare, user-gesture-only). `agent-status-snapshot.ts` `clearPendingQuestionMarkers` — `survivors.includes(owner)` inside the `remaining` loop is O(n²); n is 1-3 owners, so this is cosmetic (`Set`).

**Considered and REJECTED — do not let anyone "optimize" these:**
- Parallelizing the per-terminal loop in `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` (`terminal-agents.ts:220`). The abort message names exactly the terminals that completed BEFORE the failure; concurrency makes that list meaningless and changes which terminals get swept on a fault.
- One parent `readdir(~/.superset/agent-subagent-running)` to skip terminals with no marker dir. It would collapse N ENOENT readdirs into 1, but a dir created between the parent listing and the per-terminal call would be invisible → `pendingAfter: false` for a question raised after the click. EFFICIENCY REVIEW — uncommitted diff. 8 findings + 1 out-of-angle. Ranked by cost.

**E1. Manifest failover is EAGER on the hook fast path.** `apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts:2927` — `candidates = _hook_candidate_urls(url)` runs unconditionally, before the first POST. So EVERY hook event does: `host_dir.glob("*/manifest.json")` + open/read/`json.loads` per manifest + `_pid_alive` per manifest — even when the env URL is live and accepts on attempt 1 (the overwhelming case; the probe list exists only for the restart-onto-a-new-port case).
Cost: ~3-8ms per hook event on Windows ARM64 (1 readdir + N file reads + N `ctypes.WinDLL` loads + OpenProcess/CloseHandle), on the path that blocks the agent, at every PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Notification.
Cheaper: make the tail lazy. `_deliver` already consumes in order and only advances on failure — yield the env URL first and enumerate manifests only when the consumer asks for candidate #2. Memoize the enumerated tail at module level so the (COMPANION-CAPTURE) retry sweep reuses it without re-reading disk. Caveat: the failure logs print `candidateUrls`; use the `tried` list `_deliver` already builds (identical in the all-dead test at `pane-map-hook.test.ts:998`, which enumerates everything anyway) — only the budget-exhausted log would name fewer URLs.

**E2. Own-org manifest is read and pid-probed twice, every event.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2379-2381` — `manifest_paths` appends `host_dir/<orgId>/manifest.json`, then `extend`s with `sorted(host_dir.glob("*/manifest.json"))`, which contains that same path. Dedup happens on the resulting URL (`_add`), not on the path, so the loop opens + parses + pid-probes the common-case manifest twice.
Cost: one extra file open+parse and one extra OpenProcess per event.
Cheaper: `seen_paths` set over `manifest_paths` before the loop.

**E3. Pid probe runs before the URL dedup check.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2405` vs `:2413` — `_pid_alive` is called, then `_add` discards the endpoint as a duplicate. In the healthy case the env URL IS the own-org manifest endpoint, so the probe is pure waste.
Cheaper: build `endpoint.rstrip("/") + "/trpc/notifications.hook"` first, `if url in seen: continue`, then probe. Only difference is that the dead-pid log line is not emitted for an endpoint already queued.

**E4. `ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32")` constructed per `_pid_alive` call.** `pane-map-hook.ts:2318` — plus three `argtypes`/`restype` assignments each time.
Cost: small but multiplied by manifest count per event; first `import ctypes` in the process is the expensive part and is already unavoidable, the reload is not.
Cheaper: module-level lazy singleton (`_KERNEL32 = None`, initialize once).

**E5. `stat()` per `_log` call for rotation.** `pane-map-hook.ts:418` — `_log` is on by default (only `SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG == "0"` silences it) and is called several times per event, each now paying a `stat` before the append.
Cost: N stats per process where 1 suffices — a hook process writes a handful of lines totalling <10KB, so it cannot cross 1MB mid-process.
Cheaper: module-level `_ROTATION_CHECKED` flag; check once per process. Rotation guarantee is unchanged.

**E6. The 60s periodic resync turns a rare store-write storm into a permanent per-minute one.** `HostNotificationSubscriber.tsx:57` + `:449` → `resyncAgentStatus.ts` row loop → `store.ts:445 applySourceAxes`. `applySourceAxes` has NO no-op short-circuit: when the derived status is unchanged it still builds a fresh entry object and calls `set`, which (a) invalidates `sources` for every dot subscriber, (b) triggers the `persist` middleware to JSON-serialize all seven slices into sessionStorage, and (c) emits an `ndots` `console.info` that the main process forwards into electron-log (`store.ts:464`, `store.ts:23`). Previously this ran only on reconnect; now it runs for every row, every 60s, per host, for the life of the session.
Cost: with R agent terminals, R store writes + R full sessionStorage serializations + R main.log lines per host per minute (~1,440 × R log lines/day) with nothing changed. Same unbounded-log shape the diff just fixed in the Python hook.
Cheaper, in order of safety:
 1. Silence the log on no-change: skip `ndots` when `prev` exists, `from === to` and the axis map is unchanged. `resyncAgentStatus` already emits a summary line per resync. No state semantics touched.
 2. Coalesce the persist write: wrap `createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)` with a `setItem` that defers via a queued microtask/`setTimeout(0)`, so one resync pass writes storage once instead of R times. In-memory state and every fence are untouched.
 3. NOT recommended without a correctness pass: an equality short-circuit in `applySourceAxes` returning the existing entry object. It would kill the churn at the source, but `sources` entry IDENTITY is the resync sweep's staleness fence ("byte-for-byte the object that was there before the request went out"), so it changes what the sweep concludes. Flagging as available, not as safe.

**E7. Per-terminal dismiss reads every terminal row in the workspace.** `packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/terminal-agents/terminal-agents.ts:211-217` — the query filters on `originWorkspaceId` only and then `.filter()`s down to `input.terminalId` in JS. The right-click-one-terminal path is the common caller.
Cost: a full workspace row set materialized to drop all but one.
Cheaper: `and(eq(terminalSessions.originWorkspaceId, ...), eq(terminalSessions.id, input.terminalId))` when the id is present. Same DB-is-the-source-of-truth guarantee — the id is still intersected server-side, never trusted from the client.

**E8. Nits, low value.** `store.ts:669-684` — the new logging block iterates all sources in a pass separate from the `set()` that follows; one extra O(sources) walk per dismissal (rare, user-gesture-only). `agent-status-snapshot.ts` `clearPendingQuestionMarkers` — `survivors.includes(owner)` inside the `remaining` loop is O(n²); n is 1-3 owners, so this is cosmetic (`Set`).

- Parallelizing the per-terminal loop in `dismissWorkspaceStatuses` (`terminal-agents.ts:220`). The abort message names exactly the terminals that completed BEFORE the failure; concurrency makes that list meaningless and changes which terminals get swept on a fault.

It would collapse N ENOENT readdirs into 1, but a dir created between the parent listing and the per-terminal call would be invisible → `pendingAfter: false` for a question raised after the click. That is the exact fence the change exists to hold.

Efficiency-wise it is also a dead duplicate definition.

Everything else in the diff (HostNotificationSubscriber refs/timers, `useEffectEvent` closures, `companion-question-sink` forwarding, `applyWorkspaceStatusDismissal`'s fire-and-forget per-terminal reports) is clean — no captured-scope leaks, no sequential work that should be concurrent, no added startup blocking.

## 1. Recommended approach

**Host puts the names on the wire; clients render them. No client-side join for the question sheet.**

### Correction 1 to the trace: the sheet must NOT resolve project/workspace from the cached tree

The trace's option (a) says hoist `sourceLabelFor` and resolve project+workspace client-side from `/v1/tree`. That fails in the primary flow. Their own code says so: `...\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\ConversationViewModel.kt:55-62` — *"a question opened from a push is routinely absent from the last tree simply for having been captured after it."* And `CompanionShell.kt:98-108` opens the sheet regardless of whether `tree.findTerminalForQuestion` resolved.

So the notification-tap path — the main way the sheet opens — is exactly the path where a tree-derived header renders nothing. Since the host is already resolving all three names for the push that woke the phone, sending them in the question response makes the sheet self-sufficient: no join, no staleness, no fallback ladder to drift.

Cost: 3 strings on the sealed channel. No new privacy class — `/v1/tree` already carries project and workspace names in the clear over that channel (`Tree.kt:66-100`), and FCM already carries all three under the 2026-08-16 waiver.

## 3. Data flow

### Question sheet (the flow that matters)

```
renderer  --tab-title snapshot-->  AlertContextRegistry.sync()   [validated: workspace membership,
                                   push-context.ts:120              <=256 terminals, <=512 chars]
push       --FCM v3-->  phone notification  (unchanged)
user taps  --questionId-->  CompanionShell:98  -->  ConversationViewModel.openQuestion:250

                                     +-- resolveContextSafely(...)  -->  resolveAlertContext:754

                                     +-- log line: ids/verdicts only, NO names
           --sealed response-->  BridgeMapping.question:206  -->  QuestionDetail
           -->  QuestionSheetState  -->  QuestionSheet stickyHeader  -->  chatContextLabel(...)
```

Validation sits at two boundaries and nowhere else: the registry's `sync` (already there, refuses a whole bad snapshot rather than truncating), and Kotlin deserialization with defaults. Nothing new is persisted — the registry is process-local memory by design (`push-context.ts:22-27`).

### Chat screen

### Watch

---

**Question sheet.** A compact sticky bar, NOT the whole existing header. The user asked for workspace + tab pinned; pinning the headline and pills too would eat a third of a phone sheet.

- `stickyHeader(key = "context")` renders `ContextBar` first; `item(key = "head") { SheetHeader(...) }` stays exactly as it is, below, and scrolls.
- `ContextBar` MUST have an opaque background. A `stickyHeader` overlays scrolling content; the in-repo precedent is `ProjectHeaderRow`'s `Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)` (`HomeScreen.kt:442-444`). Without it, transcript lines scroll visibly through the header.
- Layout: line 1 = place, `labelMedium`, `onSurfaceVariant`, `maxLines = 1`, `TextOverflow.Ellipsis`. Line 2 = tab, `titleSmall`, `onSurface`, `maxLines = 1`, ellipsis. Both ellipsised — this is chrome, and the never-truncate rule is about question and option text (`QuestionSheet.kt:74-76`), not about a header.
- When `chatContextLabel` returns null: emit no sticky header at all. Not an empty bar.

**Chat TopAppBar.** Already pinned (`Scaffold` topBar, `ChatScreen.kt:99-122`). Title Row becomes a Column:

**Watch.** Existing `Caption(subtitle)` (`QuestionScreen.kt:61-64`) unchanged. Add, directly below, a second `Caption(question.tabTitle)` when non-blank. Two short captions beat one long one on a round screen. `QuestionItemScreen` is used per item, so the caption repeats per item exactly as `sourceLabel` already does.

---

## 5. Naming, wording, degradation rules

**Vocabulary.** Do not print either word. The sidebar prints bare names with no label (`HomeScreen.kt:459-467`) and the notification title is `<project> · <workspace>` (`AlertNotificationText.kt:112`). The header prints bare names in the same order with the same separator, so the app and the notification the user just tapped agree. `UserLabels.PROJECT = "Workspace"` (`AgentTree.kt:36-39`) stays confined to the accessibility strings that already use it (`HomeScreen.kt:483-485`).

**Separator.** Reuse `AlertNotificationPresentation.TITLE_SEPARATOR` (`" "` U+00B7, `AlertNotificationText.kt:45`). One constant, not a second literal.

```
push       --FCM v3-->  phone notification  (unchanged)
```

Validation sits at two boundaries and nowhere else: the registry's `sync` (already there, refuses a whole bad snapshot rather than truncating), and Kotlin deserialization with defaults. Nothing new is persisted — the registry is process-local memory by design (`push-context.ts:22-27`).

- `ContextBar` MUST have an opaque background. A `stickyHeader` overlays scrolling content; the in-repo precedent is `ProjectHeaderRow`'s `Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)` (`HomeScreen.kt:442-444`). Without it, transcript lines scroll visibly through the header.
- Layout: line 1 = place, `labelMedium`, `onSurfaceVariant`, `maxLines = 1`, `TextOverflow.Ellipsis`. Line 2 = tab, `titleSmall`, `onSurface`, `maxLines = 1`, ellipsis. Both ellipsised — this is chrome, and the never-truncate rule is about question and option text (`QuestionSheet.kt:74-76`), not about a header.
- When `chatContextLabel` returns null: emit no sticky header at all. Not an empty bar.

**Chat TopAppBar.** Already pinned (`Scaffold` topBar, `ChatScreen.kt:99-122`). Title Row becomes a Column:

## 5. Naming, wording, degradation rules

**Vocabulary.** Do not print either word. The sidebar prints bare names with no label (`HomeScreen.kt:459-467`) and the notification title is `<project> · <workspace>` (`AlertNotificationText.kt:112`). The header prints bare names in the same order with the same separator, so the app and the notification the user just tapped agree. `UserLabels.PROJECT = "Workspace"` (`AgentTree.kt:36-39`) stays confined to the accessibility strings that already use it (`HomeScreen.kt:483-485`).

**Separator.** Reuse `AlertNotificationPresentation.TITLE_SEPARATOR` (`" "` U+00B7, `AlertNotificationText.kt:45`). One constant, not a second literal.

**Degradation, exact rules for `chatContextLabel`:**
- `place` requires BOTH names non-blank. One missing -> return null for the whole label. This is `AlertContext.isNamed`'s all-or-nothing rule (`AlertContext.kt:43-47`) restated for in-app; a bare `" · "` or an orphan workspace name reads as a bug.
- `tab` = `tabTitle` when non-blank, else null. Independent of `place`.
- **Deliberate divergence from the notification:** the tab shows whenever a title is known, with no `tabCount >= 2` gate. `AlertContext.namesTab` (`:52`) exists because a notification is two lines and must not spend one restating the title. An in-app header has room, and the user's complaint is "I can't tell which tab" — a one-tab workspace answering "the tab is called X" is the correct answer, not noise. `tabCount` is therefore NOT put on the sealed wire.
- Never log the label. `AlertContext.kt:14-18` forbids names in logs on the client; the new phone code inherits that.

## 9. Risks and edge cases

- **Overlap with the red-dot commit.** Real but small. Its `index.ts` hunks are at `+43`, `+155` (imports) and `+1810..1880` (appended after `createNotifyingCaptureSink`); its `question-store.ts` hunk is `+1486` (16 lines). Our host edits sit at `index.ts:1004` and in `read-api.ts`/`types.ts`, which it does not touch at all. Only the import block can conflict, and trivially. Do not start step 2 before step 1 lands anyway — `FEATURES.md` is modified by both.
- **Tab titles are best-effort and non-durable.** Registry is process-local and cleared on bridge stop (`push-context.ts:22-27`, `index.ts:733-738`). After a host restart the header shows place-only until the renderer's next resync epoch. Same contract as the push; do not add a durable store for it.
- **Ambiguous titles resolve to `""`** (`push-context.ts:150`, `:263-267`) — same terminal, two titles in one snapshot. Header silently omits the tab. Correct, but means "tab missing" has two causes.
- **Silent breakage candidate: the sticky header background.** Omit the opaque `Surface` and content scrolls through the header. No test catches it — there are no Compose tests.
- **Second candidate: a name reaching a log.** `read-api.ts:1411` and any new error path. The fork's `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` privacy rule (`push-context.ts:28-31`) is convention plus one client-side test; the new host code is not covered by that test. The log-line assertion in test 1 is the guard — do not drop it.
- **`resolveAlertContext` cost on the tree path** — avoided by injecting the narrow `resolveTabTitle` for the tree, so tree building does no extra `findWorkspace`/`findProject` per terminal.
- **Nightly merge gate.** Any host edit must keep the five `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` markers greppable, and the new row+markers must land in the same commit as the code (`FEATURES.md:10-12`).
- **No migrations. No schema change. No new persisted state.**
- **Concurrency:** registry `sync` can land mid-request; JS single thread makes the map read atomic, and an atomic-replace snapshot means a request sees either the old or the new title, never a half-applied one.

---

## 10. Out of scope

- Making tab titles durable in `host.db`.
- Renaming a tab from the phone or watch.
- The watch transcript/chat screens and the watch's lifecycle alerts.
- Any change to FCM push keys, `AlertContext.namesTab`, the notification wording, or the §13.5 waiver.
- `tabCount` on the sealed wire.
- Unifying `WatchBridge.sourceLabelFor`'s `" / "` separator with the notification's `" · "` (`WatchBridge.kt:672` vs `AlertNotificationText.kt:45`). Pre-existing inconsistency; changing it alters the wrist's notification body, so it wants its own decision.
- Compose UI tests. The repo has none; adding the harness is its own piece of work.

---

## Ambiguity I resolved rather than guessed

The request says the tab name should be clear "when reading a chat", but the chat screen's only tab identity today is the host's derived `"Claude"` label. Satisfying that literally requires the `/v1/tree` change, which the trace did not propose. I designed it in as a **SHOULD** in the same host commit. If it is cut, the chat screen gains the workspace and keeps `"Claude"` as the tab, and the original complaint is only half answered — that should be stated to the user rather than silently accepted.

Verdict: approve the overall split only after the following corrections.

BLOCKER
1. The proposed `stickyHeader(key = "context")` duplicates the existing transcript item key. `QuestionSheet` already declares `item(key = "context")` at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\question\QuestionSheet.kt:109-111`. Lazy-list keys must be unique. Use distinct keys such as `chat-context` and `transcript-context`.
2. `stickyHeader` needs the foundation opt-in in this dependency version. The existing precedent imports `ExperimentalFoundationApi` at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\home\HomeScreen.kt:3` and opts in at `...\HomeScreen.kt:257`, while `QuestionSheet` currently opts in only to Material 3 at `...\QuestionSheet.kt:81`. Add the import and opt-in or the phone module will not compile.

MAJOR
3. The two screens can name different projects for the same terminal after sidebar re-placement. Existing `resolveAlertContext` reads the owning `workspace.projectId` at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts:763-770`. `/v1/tree` groups by `curation.effectiveProjectId(row)` at `...\read-api.ts:981-984`, and that value can come from the mirrored sidebar override at `...\sidebar-filter.ts:340-342`. Therefore the question sheet would show the owner project while the chat header’s proposed `tree.placeOf` would show the sidebar project. Decide and document which identity is required, then use it on both screens. Reusing `resolveAlertContext` unchanged is not enough if visual consistency is the requirement.
4. Do not literally copy the push wrapper’s exception logging. It logs the thrown object at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\push.ts:2257-2261`. An injected resolver can throw `Error(projectName)` and leak a name despite the stated privacy guarantee. Both read wrappers should log only a static failure plus IDs or an error class/code, never the error message, stack, or object. The no-name test must capture every logger and `console.error`, not only the unchanged `companion.question.served` event.
5. The host test plan does not cover the tree half. `handleTree` constructs each terminal at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\read-api.ts:940-959`. Add tests for `resolveTabTitle` returning a title, returning null, the dependency being null, and throwing. Assert `tabTitle` is always emitted as a string, the tree still succeeds, and no title reaches logs.
6. Add a core tree wire-compatibility test. `Terminal` currently has no defaults at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\Tree.kt:138-147`. `QuestionSourceNamesWireTest` covers only the question response. The new `tabTitle = ""` default needs tests for old JSON without the field and new JSON with it.
7. The protocol edit must update the global optional-field rule, not only the two type snippets. `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\PROTOCOL.md:1603-1611` says exactly five optional fields exist. The proposed three optional question names plus optional tree tab title make nine, and the document must say that current bridges emit these four on every applicable object, `""` means unknown, and absence identifies an older bridge.
8. The proposed WatchBridge preference test has no direct seam as written. `sourceLabelFor` is private at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\wear\WatchBridge.kt:667-673`, and the only current `WatchBridgeIntentTest` exercises internal top-level answer helpers, not a `WatchBridge` instance, at `...\WatchBridgeIntentTest.kt:30-113`. Either extract an `internal` pure `sourceLabelFor(source, tree)` helper and test it or exercise `pushQuestion` through a fake repository/link. Do not claim the preference test without specifying that seam.

MINOR
9. The push-absent-from-tree rationale is sound for a stale cached tree, but its citation and wording are wrong. `ConversationViewModel.kt:55-62` is state data, not that comment. The actual evidence is `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\shell\CompanionShell.kt:101-110`, which opens the question even when lookup returns null. A freshly built host tree deliberately includes a pending question even through curation at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\read-api.ts:852-866`, so replace “routinely absent” with “may be absent from the cached tree when a push arrives before refresh.” The wire-name decision still wins over a tree-only lookup.
10. `toResponse` does not literally have one caller. Production has one at `...\read-api.ts:1407`, but `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\session-answer.test.ts:184` also calls it. Say “one production caller.” Resolving in the read API remains the right choice because `summarize()` also uses `resolveSource` at `...\question-store.ts:1674-1695` and must stay contentless.
11. If the new `ChatScreen.place` argument is required, update both preview calls at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\app-phone\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\phone\ui\preview\CompanionPreviews.kt:251-267` and `:274-287`, or give it a nullable default. Also specify one-line ellipsis for both chat top-bar lines; the current terminal line has that guard at `...\ChatScreen.kt:114-118`.
12. Strengthen the redaction test by constructing `WatchQuestion(tabTitle = TAB)`. The current test supplies notification text but not the new raw field at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\test\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\wear\RedactedToStringTest.kt:34-53`. The current hand-written `toString` is safe at `...\WearProtocol.kt:330-332`, but the test should enforce that the new field stays omitted.
13. FEATURES.md has seven, not five, `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` machine-marker rows at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\FEATURES.md:236-242`. Preserve all seven. For `(CHAT-CONTEXT-NAMES)`, add three exact marker-block rows if survival in `read-api.ts`, `types.ts`, and `index.ts` is required; one broad directory row only proves one occurrence survives.

Verified as accurate
- `CompanionJson` has `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `encodeDefaults = true` at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\CompanionJson.kt:22-29`.
- `WearJson` has `ignoreUnknownKeys = true`, `encodeDefaults = true`, and `explicitNulls = false` at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\wear\WearProtocol.kt:105-109`.
- The watch-golden correction is right. `WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt:52-62` decodes old `WatchQuestion` JSON. The exact encode assertion at `:88-91` is only `WatchLifecycleDismiss`.
- Additive compatibility works in all four phone/watch combinations and both host/phone directions if every new Kotlin field has the stated default. A non-null `WatchQuestion.tabTitle` is ignored by old watches; missing fields decode to null/empty on new clients. No version bump is needed.
- The sealed-channel privacy choice is sound. Question bodies already cross the AES-GCM sealed response described at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\PROTOCOL.md:316-385`, and watch relay already carries full question text in `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\wear\WearProtocol.kt:289-332`. The new names do not create a wider transport trust boundary.
- `resolveAlertContext` is cheap enough for one question read: one workspace point lookup, at most one project point lookup, and one in-memory registry lookup at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts:754-797`. The separate tree title resolver is justified because registry lookup is O(1) and avoids repeated DB reads; its implementation is a map lookup at `...\push-context.ts:313-319`.
- The `EMIT-OPTIONAL-FIELDS` pattern is the right wire pattern: TS optional for older senders/receivers, current host emits on every applicable object, Kotlin defaults absorb old payloads. Existing examples and rationale are at `...\types.ts:740-795`.
- The sticky-header approach itself matches the app after the key and opt-in fixes. The existing list uses `stickyHeader` at `...\HomeScreen.kt:328`, and its opaque background is at `...\HomeScreen.kt:442-444`. The claim that there are no Compose tests is also accurate; no `createComposeRule` or `androidTest` source exists, so a manual rendering checklist is appropriate.

Recommended approach remains: enrich only the question response in `read-api.ts`, enrich terminal tree rows through the registry-only resolver, keep names out of summaries/events/logs, default every new Kotlin field, derive one shared display-label value, and relay only the tab title to the existing watch question payload. The question-store alternative loses because `resolveSource` feeds the contentless summary. A single full context resolver for the tree loses because it repeats synchronous DB work per terminal.
</agent-message>

## 0. MAJOR-3 DECISION (delegated) — sidebar-placement identity, for both screens

**Decision: both in-app surfaces use the SIDEBAR PLACEMENT identity, produced by the same code that builds `/v1/tree`. The question wire's names are NOT resolved by `resolveAlertContext`.**

### Why

1. **The tree path already states the principle.** `read-api.ts:968-971`: *"Grouped by the SIDEBAR's placement, not by `workspaces.project_id`: moving a thread under another repo is a curation act, and the phone mirrors where the user put it."* The sheet is a phone surface sitting on top of the list the user just navigated. It must agree with that list.
2. **The divergence is bigger than the reviewers found — three ways to disagree, not one.** Beyond placement (`index.ts:766` `placementProjectId(workspace.projectId)` vs `read-api.ts:983` `curation.effectiveProjectId(row)`), `resolveAlertContext` also derives the two names differently from the tree:
   - project name: `findProject(placement)?.name ?? ""` (`index.ts:769`) vs the tree's `row.name.length > 0 ? row.name : path.basename(row.repoPath || row.id)` (`read-api.ts:1063-1065`);
   - workspace name: `workspace.name` (`index.ts:765`) vs the tree's `row.name.length > 0 ? row.name : row.branch` (`read-api.ts:1009`).
   A repo with an empty `name` row, or a workspace named only by its branch, would render differently in the sheet than in the list directly behind it.
3. **The alternative would change the notification.** Making `resolveAlertContext` curation-aware alters the FCM title for every push. That is a user-visible behaviour change nobody asked for, on the path with the tightest constraints (§13.5 byte budget, waiver scope). The notification stays on the owner identity: it is a two-line alert about a machine, not a view of the user's sidebar. The pre-existing notification/list disagreement is left exactly as it is.
4. **It removes a dependency.** Project and workspace names come from `deps.db`, which `ReadDeps` already has. Only the tab title needs injecting.

### Consequence — names go in a new top-level `place`, NOT inside `source`

`QuestionSource.projectId` is the **owning** project handle: `resolveSource` (`question-store.ts:1714`) reads it from `resolveTerminal`, and `toTerminalSource` sets `hostProjectId: placementProjectId(source.hostProjectId)` (`read-api.ts:241`) — no curation. Putting a placement-derived `projectName` next to an owner-derived `projectId` would assert a pairing that is false whenever a workspace has been dragged.

So: **`QuestionResponse.place: { projectName, workspaceName, tabTitle }`, a new top-level optional object.** `source` is untouched. `source.projectId` keeps its current meaning; correcting it is out of scope (§10).

Side benefit worth stating: `WatchBridge.sourceLabelFor` (`WatchBridge.kt:667-673`) currently joins on `source.projectId` against a placement-grouped tree, so for a re-placed workspace it finds the wrong project and silently drops the workspace name. Preferring `place` fixes that for any current bridge.

### What would change my mind

If the sidebar mirror turned out to be routinely stale or absent in practice, placement would be a guess and owner identity would be the safer default. It is not: `createSidebarCuration` falls back to `effectiveProjectId: (workspace) => placementProjectId(workspace.projectId)` when there is no usable mirror (`sidebar-filter.ts:269`), which is exactly the owner identity. The two agree whenever the mirror cannot be trusted, and differ only where the user has actually re-placed something.

- `QuestionSheet.kt` needs `@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class, ExperimentalFoundationApi::class)` at `:81` plus `import androidx.compose.foundation.ExperimentalFoundationApi` and `import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.stickyHeader` (BLOCKER-2).
- `ContextBar` MUST paint an opaque background or content scrolls through it. Use `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` — the sheet's own `containerColor` (`:99`). Do NOT copy `HomeScreen.kt:443`'s `background`; it is a different colour and would show as a band (MINOR-14).
- Line 1 = place, `labelMedium`, `onSurfaceVariant`. Line 2 = tab, `titleSmall`, `onSurface`. Both `maxLines = 1`, `TextOverflow.Ellipsis`. The never-truncate rule (`QuestionSheet.kt:74-76`) is about question and option text, not chrome.
- `chatContextLabel` null -> emit no sticky header at all. Not an empty bar.

**Chat TopAppBar** (already pinned, `ChatScreen.kt:99-122`). Title Row -> Column:
- Row: `StatusDot(terminal.status, stale)` + tab name = `terminal.tabTitle.ifBlank { terminal.title }` (degrades to today's `"Claude"`).
- Under it: `place.place`, `labelSmall`, `onSurfaceVariant`. Both lines `maxLines = 1` + ellipsis (MINOR-11). Omitted entirely when null.
- Two lines in a 64dp M3 `TopAppBar` can clip vertically — on the manual checklist (MINOR-15).

**Watch.** Existing `Caption(subtitle)` (`:61-64`) unchanged; add a second `Caption(question.tabTitle)` when non-blank. Two short captions beat one long one on a round screen. Repeats per item exactly as `sourceLabel` already does.

---

## 5. Wording and degradation

- **No labels.** The sidebar prints bare names (`HomeScreen.kt:459-467`); the header does too. `UserLabels.PROJECT` (`AgentTree.kt:36-39`) stays confined to the accessibility strings already using it (`HomeScreen.kt:483-485`).
- **Separator:** reuse `AlertNotificationPresentation.TITLE_SEPARATOR` (`AlertNotificationText.kt:45`). One constant.
- `chatContextLabel(place)`:
  - null place -> null.
  - `place` string requires BOTH names non-blank; either blank -> return null for the whole label. This is `AlertContext.isNamed`'s all-or-nothing rule (`AlertContext.kt:43-47`) restated in-app; a bare `" · "` reads as a bug.
  - `tab` = `tabTitle` when non-blank, else null. Independent of `place`.
  - **Deliberate divergence from the notification:** no `tabCount >= 2` gate (`AlertContext.kt:52`). That gate exists because a two-line notification must not spend a line restating the title; an in-app header has room, and the complaint is "I can't tell which tab". `tabCount` therefore does not go on the sealed wire.
- Never log the label (`AlertContext.kt:14-18`).

---

## 6. Wire compatibility

- **Kotlin decode:** `CompanionJson` sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` (`CompanionJson.kt:25`). All four skew directions hold: old bridge + new phone -> `place == null`, `tabTitle == ""`; new bridge + old phone -> keys ignored. No version bump.
- **Host encode:** optional TS fields, always emitted by a current bridge, same as `questionCount`/`multiSelect` (`read-api.ts:936-941`).
- **Watch:** `WearJson` has `encodeDefaults = true` + `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` (`WearProtocol.kt:105-107`). `WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt:52-62` DECODES a hand-written `WatchQuestion` string rather than asserting an exact encode, so the new defaulted field breaks nothing; the exact-encode assertion at `:88-91` is `WatchLifecycleDismiss`, and `WatchLifecycleAlertWireTest.kt:115` is a lifecycle alert. Add a decode assertion; do not rewrite a golden.
- **PROTOCOL.md `:1602-1611` (MAJOR-7).** The sentence "The five fields marked OPTIONAL above are the only ones in this document a sender may omit" becomes false — the count goes to seven (`place`, `Terminal.tabTitle`). Rewrite the rule rather than bumping a number:
  - state the general rule — a field marked OPTIONAL may be omitted and §0's hard-error rule does not cover it;
  - state the per-field meaning of absence, keeping the existing `pinned` / `questionCount` / `multiSelect` paragraphs verbatim;
  - add: **a current bridge always emits `place` and `tabTitle`; `""` means "the bridge could not resolve this name", absence of the field means an older bridge. A client MUST render both as no-name and MUST NOT substitute an id, a handle or a guess.**
  - keep "A bridge that reports these MUST report them on every applicable object, not selectively."
- Watch payload: `tabTitle` is bounded at 512 UTF-16 units by the registry (`push-context.ts:53`); the existing `WatchQuestionOversize` path measures the real payload.

---

**Host — NEW `chat-context-names.test.ts`** (ReadDeps built off the `session-tree.test.ts:79` fixture pattern):

*Question half:*
1. place resolves -> `response.place` carries all three.
2. **placement identity** — a mirror re-placing the workspace under another project: `place.projectName` is the PLACEMENT project, and it equals what `handleTree` groups the same terminal under. Assert against the tree output in the same test, so the two can never drift.
3. project row with empty `name` -> `place.projectName` is the `path.basename(repoPath)` fallback, matching the tree.
4. workspace row with empty `name` -> `place.workspaceName` is the branch, matching the tree.
5. Sessions workspace (`project_id = NULL`) -> `SESSIONS_PROJECT_NAME`.
6. `findWorkspace` returns null -> all three `""`, response still served.
7. `resolveTabTitle` dep `null` -> `tabTitle === ""`, other two still resolve.
8. `resolveTabTitle` **throws** -> `tabTitle === ""`, response still served.
9. `db.findProject` throws -> `projectName === ""`, the other fields survive.

*Tree half (MAJOR-5), against `handleTree`:*
10. title present -> `terminal.tabTitle` set.
11. no registry entry -> `tabTitle === ""`; `typeof` is always `string`, never undefined-when-emitted.
12. dep `null` -> tree still succeeds.
13. resolver throws -> tree still succeeds, `tabTitle === ""`.

*Privacy (MAJOR-4), across both halves:*
14. Capture EVERY sink — `deps.log`, plus spies on `console.error` / `console.warn` / `console.log` — and assert no captured argument, at any depth, contains any name fixture value. Include a case where the resolver throws `new Error(PROJECT_NAME_FIXTURE)`: the class name may be logged, the message may not.

15. NEW `core\...\protocol\QuestionPlaceWireTest.kt` — §7.4 payload without `place` decodes to null; with it decodes verbatim; `place` present with missing sub-keys decodes to `""`.
16. NEW `core\...\protocol\TreeTerminalWireTest.kt` (MAJOR-6) — a `Terminal` JSON WITHOUT `tabTitle` decodes to `""`, and one WITH it decodes verbatim. First defaulted field on that class, so this is the regression guard for the whole forward-compat claim.
17. NEW `app-phone\...\ui\common\ChatContextLabelTest.kt` — both names -> `"a · b"`; either blank -> null (assert output never starts or ends with the separator); tab blank -> `tab == null`; tab present with a single tab -> still shown; null place -> null.
18. NEW `app-phone\...\model\PlaceOfTest.kt` — nested terminal found; unknown id -> null; `tabTitle` carried through.
19. `WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt` — `WatchQuestion` JSON without `tabTitle` decodes to null.
20. `RedactedToStringTest.kt` (MINOR-12) — construct `WatchQuestion` **with `tabTitle` set to a secret fixture** and assert `toString` omits it, so a future generated `toString` is caught.
21. `WatchBridgeIntentTest.kt` (MAJOR-8) — drive the extracted top-level `sourceLabelFor(place, source, tree)`: wire place wins; null place falls back to the tree join; neither -> null. Also cover the re-placed-workspace case, where the tree fallback returns the project only.

**Manual (no Compose tests exist in this repo — all rendering is uncovered by CI):**
- sheet scrolled with a long transcript, header stays;
- notification tap with the app cold -> header populated (the case the design exists for);
- two Claude tabs in one workspace -> chat headers differ;
- host restart before renderer resync -> tab absent, place still shown, never `" · "`;
- **workspace dragged under another project on the desktop -> sheet, chat header and phone list all name the same project** (the MAJOR-3 acceptance test);
- very long names -> ellipsis on both top-bar lines, no wrap, **no vertical clipping in the 64dp TopAppBar**;
- old phone vs new host, and new phone vs pre-change host.

---

## 8. Build order

1. **Land the red-dot commit.** It is uncommitted and touches `companion\index.ts` and `companion\question-store.ts`, and both commits edit `FEATURES.md`.
2. **Fork host commit** `(CHAT-CONTEXT-NAMES)`: `types.ts` -> `read-api.ts` (helpers extracted and `handleTree` switched onto them FIRST, so the refactor is verified before anything new consumes it) -> `index.ts` -> tests -> `FEATURES.md`. Verify: `bun test packages/host-service/src/companion`.
3. **Companion core wire**: `Question.kt`, `Tree.kt` + tests 15, 16.
4. **Companion phone plumbing**: model, `BridgeMapping`, `placeOf`, `ChatContextLabel` + tests 17, 18. No visible change yet.
5. **Companion phone UI**: sheet sticky bar, then `ChatScreen`/`AgentsPane`/`CompanionShell`/previews. First visible step.
6. **Companion watch**: `WearProtocol`, `WatchBridge` seam extraction, `QuestionScreen` + tests 19, 20, 21.
7. **`PROTOCOL.md`** §7.2, §7.4, optional-field rule.

Steps 3-7 degrade cleanly against an un-updated host, so the phone can ship ahead of the desktop.

---

## 9. Risks

- **Overlap with the red-dot commit.** Its `index.ts` hunks are at `+43`, `+155` (imports) and `+1810..1880`; its `question-store.ts` hunk is `+1486`. Our host edits are `index.ts:1004`, `read-api.ts`, `types.ts`. Only the import block can conflict, trivially. `question-store.ts` is not touched at all.
- **`handleTree` refactor is the riskiest edit in the host commit.** Switching `:1009` and `:1063-1065` onto shared helpers changes code on the hot read path. It must be behaviour-identical; `session-tree.test.ts` and `curation-gates.test.ts` are the guard, and test 2 pins tree and sheet together afterwards.
- **`readSidebarMirror()` now runs per `/v1/question`.** `handleTree` already does this per tree fetch, which is far more frequent, so the added cost is negligible — but it is a new DB read on the question path.
- **Tab titles are best-effort and non-durable.** The registry is process-local and cleared on bridge stop (`push-context.ts:22-27`, `index.ts:733-738`); after a host restart the header shows place-only until the renderer resyncs. Do not add durable storage for it.
- **Ambiguous titles resolve to `""`** (`push-context.ts:150`, `:263-267`), so "tab missing" has two causes.
- **Silent-breakage candidates, none covered by CI:** the duplicate LazyColumn key (crashes, caught immediately); a missing opaque sticky background (visual only); a name reaching a log (test 14 is the only guard); TopAppBar vertical clipping.
- **The notification keeps the owner identity while the app uses placement.** A deliberate, documented divergence (§0), not a bug to be "fixed" later without re-reading this section.
- No migrations, no schema change, no new persisted state. Registry `sync` is an atomic replace on a single-threaded runtime, so a request sees the old or the new title, never a half-applied one.

---

## 10. Out of scope

- Correcting `QuestionSource.projectId` to the placement identity (`read-api.ts:241`). It stays the owning-project handle; only `place` is placement-derived.
- Changing the FCM notification wording, `resolveAlertContext`, `AlertContext.namesTab`, push keys, or the §13.5 waiver.
- `tabCount` on the sealed wire.
- Making tab titles durable in `host.db`; renaming a tab from the phone or watch.
- **The watch's contentless and oversize question paths (`WatchQuestionContentless`, `WatchQuestionOversize`) gain no `tabTitle`** — they exist for the case where the body could not be fetched or relayed, so there is no `place` to carry. Absence there is by design, not a bug (MINOR-16).
- The watch transcript/chat screens and lifecycle alerts.
- Unifying `sourceLabelFor`'s `" / "` with the notification's `" · "` (`WatchBridge.kt:672` vs `AlertNotificationText.kt:45`) — pre-existing, and changing it alters the wrist's notification body.
- Compose UI tests; the harness does not exist here.

### Rejected alternative worth naming (MINOR-17)

**Reuse the FCM push extras on the phone instead of a host wire change.** The phone already receives all three names in the push (`CompanionNotifications.kt:156,186`) and discards them after composing the notification. Keeping them and feeding the sheet would need no protocol change at all. It loses on three counts: extras do not survive the sheet being reopened later or the app process dying, so the header would be present once and absent forever after; the watch relay has no push context to draw on; and the chat screen still needs a `Terminal.tabTitle` host change regardless, so the host commit does not disappear — it only gets less useful.
