<agent-message from="arch-notif">
# Blueprint — companion notification-gap fixes (FIX-1/2/3)

All line refs verified by reading. Two repos:
FORK = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`
COMP = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`

## 0. Corrections to the brief (read first)

**R3 does NOT collapse into R1.** Soft-delete leaves terminals alive — `COMP`… no, FORK: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\hooks\useBulkWorkspaceSoftDelete\useBulkWorkspaceSoftDelete.ts:11-13` states the bin move is "worktree, branch and **terminals untouched**". So no exit fires, R1 never triggers, and the phone keeps a ready card for a binned thread. R3 needs its own retirement path (curation-driven, below). Hard delete does dispose (`apps\desktop\src\renderer\react-query\workspaces\useDeleteWorkspace.ts:96-99` → `terminal.disposeWorkspaceSessions` → `packages\host-service\src\terminal\terminal.ts:2939`), so hard delete → R1.

**No new key may be added to the `c` push frame.** `COMP\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\LifecyclePush.kt:234-241` validates the `c` key set with `requireExactKeySet` — an extra key is a hard `ProtocolException` on every shipped phone, i.e. the retraction is dropped and the card is stranded. FEATURES.md restates this ("exact-equality in both directions"). Every wire-level fix below therefore uses existing keys only.

**Pre-existing bug found, fixed as part of FIX-3's addressing work.** `e` retractions today carry a real `t` (`packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-alerts.ts:665`), and the phone's `forgetRetracted` (`COMP\core\...\notify\ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:173-181`) treats a non-empty `t` as "retire the terminal-collapsed READY row up to `gx`". `notifiesPhone` returns true for `e` + `new-cycle` (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:122-124`), so today: agent errors → agent starts new work → the `e` retraction silently cancels the user's unread standing READY card. Live now, independent of FIX-3.

**Ambiguity + assumption (FIX-3 blind fallback).** The user asked for `e` to retract on desktop-seen. I widen the live-map path (covers everything the host still holds) but keep the blind restart fallback `g`-only. Hashing both kinds doubles blind broadcasts on every warm reconnect, which is the exact harm documented at `lifecycle-alerts.ts:1225-1233` (the phone's 64-slot `SeenLifecycleEvents` window evicting real tombstones). Residual stated in §5. Say the word if the user wants both.

---

## 1. Recommended approach

### FIX-1 — durable watch question-retraction (COMP only, no wire change)

Clone the `PendingLifecycleDismissals` shape for resolutions, and give the wrist card a self-timeout.

* Durable queue `PendingQuestionResolutions` (SharedPreferences, `commit()`, cap 256, TTL 6 h), enqueue-before-send, clear on clean delivery, replay on `onHello` — byte-for-byte the same discipline as `COMP\app-phone\...\wear\PendingLifecycleDismissals.kt` and `WatchBridge.kt:335-387`.
* Persist only `questionId | enqueuedAtMs | resolvedAtMs | resolvedBySurface | outcome`. **`resolvedByLabel` is deliberately not persisted**: all three `pushResolved` callers pass `null` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:518-524`, `SessionViewModel.kt:231-237`, `CompanionMessagingService.kt:209-215`) and nothing on the wrist renders it (only `resolvedBySurface`, `app-watch\...\ui\AnswerStateScreen.kt:283`). Keeps the `:`/`,` delimiter encoding safe — every persisted token is base64url or a fixed enum word.
* TTL 6 h, not the dismissals' 24 h: it matches the question staleness horizon and the new wrist timeout, so a queued entry can never outlive the card it cancels. (24 h for symmetry is the alternative; 6 h is self-consistent, pick it.)
* Belt: `setTimeoutAfter` on the wrist question card, computed from `askedAtMs + QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS`. `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS = 21_600_000` mirrors the bridge's `PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS` (`packages\host-service\src\companion\config.ts:377`). Rejected alternative: carry the push's `x` to the watch on `WatchQuestion` — two of the three post paths (`pushQuestionById`, `onHello`) have no push in hand, so it would need the constant anyway; one mechanism beats two.

Why not "replay by re-fetching at hello" (call `pushQuestionById` for queued ids): it needs the desktop reachable at exactly the moment the watch reconnects, which is the case the queue exists for.

### FIX-2 — stuck ready alerts (host-side authority, FORK; one shared Kotlin fix, COMP)

Three producers, three answers, all authored where the fact is known:

* **R1 (terminal died)** — one choke point. Every exit broadcast in the tree funnels through `EventBus.broadcastTerminalLifecycle` (`packages\host-service\src\events\event-bus.ts:224`); the nine call sites are all in `terminal\terminal.ts` and `terminal\reaper\reaper.ts`. Hook a fork-only companion sink there, gated on `eventType === "exit" && confirmed !== false`, and have it call a new `LifecycleAlertManager.retireTerminal()` which is just `supersede(id, { kind: "session-end" })` — the existing, already-correct retirement. **No renderer change**, so nothing collides with the fixer's in-flight `lifecycleEvents.ts` edit.
  Rejected: calling from each of the 9 broadcast sites (silently incomplete the first time someone adds a tenth). Rejected: an `EventBus.onTerminalLifecycle` in-process listener like `onWorkspaceChanged` (`event-bus.ts:258-266`) — better dependency direction, but it needs the `EventBus` threaded into the bridge through both mounts (`serve.ts:134`, `apps\desktop\src\main\host-service\index.ts:154`) for no behavioural gain. The registry sink slot is what `registry.ts:253` exists for and answers "nobody consumed it" when the bridge is off.
  Rejected: polling `liveness.isProvablyGone` from the alert sweep — up to ~90 s late, silent when the daemon is unreachable, and the sweep only runs while a `held` alert exists (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:601-615`).

* **R2 (app restart)** — renderer supplies the one fact only it has, host decides what to retract. New one-shot mutation carrying the cold-start boundary the resync already computes in **host clock** terms (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:393-407`); the host retires `g` alerts with `outcomeAtMs < boundary`. One call per host per launch, zero blind broadcasts, no per-terminal `reportTerminalSeen` storm — which is what `companionAlertSync.ts:419-423` and `lifecycle-alerts.ts:1225-1233` explicitly forbid.
  Rejected: inferring the cold start host-side from `sidebar_mirror_meta.appLaunchId`. `APP_LAUNCH_ID` is `crypto.randomUUID()` at module scope (`...CollectionsProvider\dashboardSidebarLocal\sidebarVisibility.ts:73`) so it changes on a renderer **reload**, where sessionStorage survives and the desktop keeps its green dot — the host would retract a card the user has not read. Wrong proxy.
  Rejected: renderer reporting seen for every cold-seeded terminal — the documented mass-retraction the design forbids.

* **R3 (soft delete / any curation-off)** — the mirror is the authority and already reaches the bridge. On a mirror change, retire live alerts whose workspace is now curated off. The hold rule already exists (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:639`, `createLifecycleCurationProbe`); this applies the same rule to the states the hold cannot reach (`sent`/`standing`). Hook: the existing `mirrorChangeSink` at `packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts:1222-1239`.

* **Phone addressing (shared with FIX-3, MUST)** — `forgetRetracted` returns a key or `null`, and `null` conflates "no record" with "stale retraction" (`ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:171-189`). Cap-64 eviction (`:142`) or an expired row therefore leaves the terminal-keyed card uncancellable. Make the verdict three-valued and cancel the terminal key on **Unknown** only — an unknown record is ignorance, and a stuck card is worse than one extra cancel (the next finish reposts and buzzes). Keep the generation guard on **Stale**, which is the whole point of `gx`.

### FIX-3 — error alerts retract on desktop-seen (FORK + COMP + PROTOCOL)

* Drop the `kind !== "g"` filter in `findReadAlerts` (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:1044`). `notifiesPhone` already returns true for `e` + `seen`, so nothing else in the state machine changes.
* Keep the blind fallback `g`-only (`:1264-1274`), documented (see §0).
* **`fireRetraction` sends `t: ""` for `kind === "e"`.** This is the precise-addressing fix, and it is wire-legal today: PROTOCOL §13.5.1 already says `t` "may be `""` on `q`, `e` and `c`", and both `sanitizeTerminalHandle` (`push.ts:771-775`) and the phone parser (`LifecyclePush.kt:241,247`) accept empty. An `e` card is always event-keyed on both devices (`LifecycleAlertIdentity.key`, `ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:30-35`), so an `e` retraction has no terminal-collapsed row to name — and sending one is the pre-existing collateral bug in §0.
* Record the user's override in the `notifiesPhone` doc (`:118-120`) and in `markLifecycleSeen`'s "ONLY `g`" note (`:1197-1201`), dated 2026-08-20.

---

## 2. Files to create / modify

### FORK — host-service

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-alerts.ts` | **MUST.** Add to `LifecycleAlertManager`: `retireTerminal(hostTerminalId)` (→ `supersede(id,{kind:"session-end"})`), `retireReadyBefore(boundaryMs)` (walk alerts, `kind==="g" && outcomeAtMs < boundaryMs` → `retireAlert(alert,{kind:"seen"})`), `retireCuratedOffAlerts()` (walk alerts, `deps.isCuratedOff(alert.hostWorkspaceId)` → `retireAlert(alert,{kind:"curated-off"})`). New `RetireReason` member `{kind:"curated-off"}`, rank 1 in `retireReasonRank` (`:79-81`) so it is loud and can upgrade a `new-cycle`. `findReadAlerts:1044` — drop the kind filter. `fireRetraction:653-680` — `terminalHandle: alert.kind === "g" ? deps.terminalHandle(...) : ""`. Comments at `:118-120` and `:1197-1201` updated with the user's decision + date. |
| `packages\host-service\src\companion\registry.ts` | **MUST.** Three new `createSinkSlot` slots beside the existing two (`:311-327`): `terminal-gone` (`recordCompanionTerminalGone({hostTerminalId}): boolean`), `cold-start-boundary` (`recordCompanionColdStartBoundary({boundaryMs}): boolean`), `curation-changed` — or fold the last one into the existing mirror sink (preferred: it is already called from `publishCompanionMirrorChanged:203`, so no new slot). Net: **two** new slots. |
| `packages\host-service\src\events\event-bus.ts` | **MUST.** In `broadcastTerminalLifecycle:224-232`, before/after the fan-out: `if (message.eventType === "exit" && message.confirmed !== false) recordCompanionTerminalGone({ hostTerminalId: message.terminalId })`. Fork-only lines → carry a marker token (see FEATURES.md row below). `confirmed !== false` mirrors the renderer's own rule at `lifecycleEvents.ts:187-193`; the reaper emits the confirming exit later (`reaper.ts:472-479`). |
| `packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts` | **MUST.** Register the two new sinks next to the lifecycle-seen sink (`:917-960`), each with an `unwind.push` clear. Extend `mirrorChangeSink` (`:1222-1239`) with `lifecycleAlerts.retireCuratedOffAlerts()` inside its own try/catch — a curation write must never fail on a retraction. |
| `packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\companion\companion.ts` | **MUST.** New `retireStaleReadyAlerts` mutation beside `markLifecycleSeen:398-407`. Input `z.object({ boundaryMs: z.number().int().positive() })`. Returns `{ accepted: boolean }`. Never throws for the off states, same as its neighbour. |
| `FEATURES.md` | **MUST.** One markers row: `(ALERT-RETIRE-ON-EXIT)\tpackages/host-service/src/events/event-bus.ts`. Rationale identical to `(COMPANION-CAPTURE-HOOK)`: the hook lives in an upstream-shaped file and an upstream merge could delete it with every other gate green. Extend the companion-alerts manifest paragraph with the three new retirement triggers. |

Tests to add (bun): `lifecycle-alerts.test.ts` (exists, 1598 lines — extend, do not create). `packages\host-service\src\companion\push-retract.test.ts` for the empty-`t`-on-`e` frame.

### FORK — renderer

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `...\V2NotificationController\lib\companionAlertSync.ts` | **MUST.** New export `reportColdStartBoundary({ hostUrl, boundaryMs }): Promise<boolean>`, same silent-on-failure contract as `reportTerminalSeen:435-468`, but keyed by `hostUrl` directly (the caller has it) rather than through `hostUrlByWorkspaceId`. |
| `...\V2NotificationController\lib\resyncAgentStatus.ts` | **MUST.** At `:398-401`, where `hostSessionBoundaries.set(hostUrl, hostNow - elapsedMs)` runs — fire-and-forget `reportColdStartBoundary`. That map already dedupes per host (`:393`), so it fires exactly once per host per cold launch. Add a `coldStartBoundaryReported` counter to `ResyncResult` for the existing diagnostic log. |
| `...\V2NotificationController\lib\lifecycleEvents.ts` | **NO CHANGE.** R1 is host-side. Avoids the fixer's in-flight edit. |
| `...\stores\v2-notifications\store.ts` | **NO CHANGE.** |

Tests: extend `companionAlertSync.test.ts` (its transport double at `:19-45` already fakes `getHostServiceClientByUrl`) and `resyncAgentStatus.test.ts`.

### COMP — phone

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `app-phone\...\phone\wear\PendingQuestionResolutions.kt` | **NEW, MUST.** `PendingQuestionResolution` data class + `PendingResolutionStore` interface + `PendingQuestionResolutions(store, capacity=256, ttlMs=21_600_000)` + `SharedPreferencesPendingResolutionStore` (own file `companion_question_resolutions`, `commit()`). * **Host-service restart (residual, R2).** Alert state is process-local by design. Desktop restart + host restart ⇒ nothing holds the alert, nothing can name it, and the card lives to its 6 h TTL — the phone's `setTimeoutAfter` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:271`) takes it down, no manual swipe. The only cure is either durable alert state (schema change, needs explicit user approval) or a phone-side lifecycle sweep against the tree — both out of scope.

* Durable host-side alert state (would need a `host.db` schema change and explicit user approval).
* Phone-side reconciliation of *lifecycle* cards against the tree on foreground (`CompanionNotifications.sweep` stays questions-only). This is the only thing that would close the double-restart residual.

* Kanban / sidebar / recycle-bin behaviour: R3 reads the mirror, it never writes curation.

| `app-watch\...\wear\notify\QuestionNotifier.kt` | **MUST.** `post(...)` gains `timeoutAtMs: Long`; `.setTimeoutAfter((timeoutAtMs - now).coerceAtLeast(1))` at `:123-131`, same idiom as `LifecycleNotifier.kt:151`. `notifyQuestion` → `question.askedAtMs + QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS`. `notifyOversize`/`notifyContentless` → `now + QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS` (neither payload carries `askedAtMs`; arrival is a lower bound on the ask, so the card never times out early). |
| `app-watch\...\wear\notify\LifecycleNotifier.kt` | **MUST.** `cancel:...` consumes the same verdict as the phone, same Unknown rule. |

### COMP — core / protocol

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `core\...\core\notify\ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt` | **MUST.** `forgetRetracted` returns a sealed `RetractionVerdict` — `Retired(key)` / `Stale` / `Unknown`. Behaviour otherwise unchanged: terminal branch first, generation guard intact, event branch as today. One rule, both surfaces. |
| `core\...\core\CompanionConstants.kt` | **MUST.** `const val QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS = 21_600_000L` in a new "Question freshness" block. Must equal `PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS` in the fork; cross-repo, so no test can bind them — call that out in the comment on both sides. |
| `PROTOCOL.md` | **MUST.** §15 constants table: `Question staleness horizon | 21 600 000 ms`. §13.5.6: one paragraph — an error retraction carries `t: ""` because an `e` card is event-keyed and has no terminal-collapsed row, and a non-empty `t` on an `e` retraction retires a READY row it was never about. §13.5.5/§11: the wrist question card carries its own `setTimeoutAfter` from `askedAtMs` + the horizon, because the watch has no equivalent of the phone's foreground `sweep`. §13.5.5: question resolutions are eventual, not one-shot — same durable-queue wording as the watch dismissal, TTL 6 h. |

Tests: `PendingQuestionResolutionsTest.kt` (clone `PendingLifecycleDismissalsTest.kt`), extend `ShownLifecycleAlertsTest.kt`, update `WatchBridgeIntentTest.kt` construction, `WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt` for the resolution-queue contract.

---

## 3. Data flow

**FIX-1, resolution:** phone resolves (answer confirmed / sweep / FCM retract) → `WatchBridge.pushResolved` → **enqueue first** (durable, `commit()`) → `WatchLink.sendResolved` → `Delivered && failedNodeCount==0` → `clear(questionId)`. `NoWatchPaired`/`Failed`/partial → row stays. Watch reconnects → `HELLO` → `onHello` → `flushLifecycleDismissals` → `flushQuestionResolutions` → oldest pending question. Watch: `QUESTION_RESOLVED` → `QuestionNotifier.cancel` + `QuestionStore.onResolved` (idempotent for unknown ids, `QuestionStore.kt:327-346`). Independently, every wrist question card self-cancels at `askedAtMs + 6 h`. Validation: at the queue boundary (`enqueue` refuses over cap and reports `SentUnrecorded`, never silently drops) and at `WatchLink.send` (`MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` require).

**FIX-2 R1:** pty exit / dispose / reaper correction → `EventBus.broadcastTerminalLifecycle({eventType:"exit", confirmed?})` → fork hook, `confirmed !== false` → `recordCompanionTerminalGone` → (bridge off ⇒ `false`, no-op) → `lifecycleAlerts.retireTerminal` → `supersede(terminalId, {kind:"session-end"})` → per alert: `held` deleted silently, `sending` flagged (retracted on `markDelivered`), `sent`/`standing` → one `c` each, `retracted` inert. Phone: `routeLifecycleRetract` → suppress tombstone first, then cancel, then watch dismissal (`LifecycleRouting.kt:278-289`). State persisted: none new on the host (alert table stays process-local, per `lifecycle-alerts.ts:416-421`); durable state is the phone's `ShownLifecycleAlerts` + suppression gate.

**FIX-2 R2:** desktop cold start → renderer resync computes `hostSessionBoundary = hostNow - elapsedMonotonic` → `companion.retireStaleReadyAlerts({boundaryMs})` (validated at the tRPC boundary: positive int; the sink additionally refuses `boundaryMs > now()` — a future boundary would retire everything) → `retireReadyBefore` → `retireAlert(..., {kind:"seen"})` per covered `g`. Same instant the renderer seeds those terminals as seen locally (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:509-520`), so both surfaces agree.

**FIX-2 R3:** user bins/archives/snoozes/completes a thread → `useSidebarMirrorSync` full-replace → `sidebarMirror.sync` → `replaceMirror` (`sidebar-mirror.ts:186-260`, content hash decides `changed`) → `publishCompanionMirrorChanged` → `mirrorChangeSink` → `tree.curation` event **and** `retireCuratedOffAlerts()` → `workspaceSidebarVerdict !== "show"` → one `c` per live alert. DB (`sidebar_workspace_state`) is the source of truth for the verdict; the probe's 30 s positive cache is fine here because a cached `true` is the state we act on.

**FIX-3:** user opens the chat on the desktop → `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead` (`companionAlertSync.ts:371-413`) → `companion.markLifecycleSeen` → bridge revalidates terminal↔workspace against host.db (`index.ts:917-953`) → `findReadAlerts` now returns `g` **and** `e` rows with `outcomeAtMs <= seenThroughAt` → `retireAlert(..., {kind:"seen"})` → `fireRetraction` with `t = handle` for `g`, `t = ""` for `e` → phone: `e` cancels its event-keyed row only; `g` cancels event key + terminal key under the generation guard.

---

## 4. Build order

Each step independently verifiable. **Fork work lands as its own commit after the master-workspace feature; companion work is independent and can land first.**

**COMP (independent, ship first — it makes the fork's retractions land correctly on shipped phones):**
1. `ShownLifecycleAlerts` verdict + both cancel sites + tests. Verify: `gradlew :core:test :app-phone:test :app-watch:test`.
2. `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS` + wrist question `setTimeoutAfter` + PROTOCOL §15 row. Verify: unit test on the computed timeout; manual on-wrist check that a card self-clears.
3. `PendingQuestionResolutions` + store + tests (pure JVM, no device).
4. `WatchBridge.pushResolved`/`flushQuestionResolutions`/`onHello` + container wiring + `WatchBridgeIntentTest` update.
5. PROTOCOL §13.5.5/§13.5.6 paragraphs.

**FORK (after the master-workspace commit is in):**
6. `lifecycle-alerts.ts` alone: `findReadAlerts` widening, `fireRetraction` empty-`t`-for-`e`, the three new manager methods, the `curated-off` reason, comment updates. Verify: `bun test packages/host-service/src/companion/lifecycle-alerts.test.ts` + `push-retract.test.ts`. Nothing is wired yet, so this step cannot change runtime behaviour beyond FIX-3.
7. `registry.ts` slots + `index.ts` registration + `mirrorChangeSink` call (R3 live). Verify: bun tests; manual — bin a thread with a ready card on the phone, card disappears.
8. `event-bus.ts` hook + FEATURES.md marker (R1 live). Verify: `bun run scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs`; manual — kill a terminal with a ready card, card disappears.
9. tRPC mutation + renderer `reportColdStartBoundary` + resync call (R2 live). Verify: renderer bun tests; manual — leave a ready card, quit and relaunch the desktop, card disappears.
10. FEATURES.md manifest prose. `/simplify` before commit (production code touched).

---

## 5. Risks and edge cases

* **Marker survival.** The `event-bus.ts` hook is fork-only code in an upstream-shaped file. Without the FEATURES.md marker row a nightly merge can take upstream's version and every gate stays green while R1 silently dies. Same failure class the fork already wrote `(COMPANION-CAPTURE-HOOK)` for.
* **`confirmed: false` exits.** Deliberately not retired — the row stays `active` for the reaper, which emits the confirming exit (`terminal.ts:2905-2915`, `reaper.ts:472-479`). Cost: a card lives until the reaper's pass (observed up to 21 min in the DISPOSE-LIMBO note). Retiring on the unconfirmed exit would retract a card for a terminal that may still be alive.
* **Host-service restart (residual, R2).** Alert state is process-local by design. Desktop restart + host restart ⇒ nothing holds the alert, nothing can name it, and the card lives to its 6 h TTL — the phone's `setTimeoutAfter` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:271`) takes it down, no manual swipe. The only cure is either durable alert state (schema change, needs explicit user approval) or a phone-side lifecycle sweep against the tree — both out of scope.
* **`e` retraction after a host restart (residual, FIX-3).** Blind fallback stays `g`-only, so a read does not retract a restart-orphaned `e`. Dies at TTL.
* **Snooze retracts too (R3).** `curated-off` covers snooze, not just the bin. Defensible ("not now" ⇒ take the buzz away), but it is a behaviour change beyond the literal ask — flag to the user. If unwanted, gate `retireCuratedOffAlerts` on the verdict being `deleted`/`completed`/`archived` only; `workspaceSidebarVerdict` already returns the discriminated reason (`sidebar-filter.ts:95-102`), so the narrowing is one condition.
* **Cancel-on-Unknown (phone).** Trades a possible extra cancel of an unrecorded newer card for never stranding one. The next finish reposts and buzzes, so the worst case is one missed buzz on an unread chat whose record was evicted at cap 64 — the same trade PROTOCOL §13.5.6 already documents ("one extra buzz, never a stuck notification").
* **Retraction storms.** `retireCuratedOffAlerts` runs on every *changed* mirror sync, `retireReadyBefore` once per host per launch. Both are bounded by the alert table (512) and every path goes through `retireAlert`, whose `retracted` rows are inert — no alert can fire two `c`s.
* **Clock.** `boundaryMs` is host clock by construction (`hostNow - elapsedMonotonic`); a renderer that could not read `performance.now()` or `hostNow` skips cold-start seeding entirely (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:394-405`) and must skip the report too — same guard, do not report a boundary the seeding did not use.
* **Concurrency (phone).** `PendingQuestionResolutions` must be `@Synchronized` on the instance and constructed **once** in the container, for the reason `LifecycleNotifier` spells out — the Data Layer dispatches on a pool and a per-call instance is no lock at all.
* **Migration.** The new SharedPreferences file starts empty; a resolution sent by the old build and lost stays lost (bounded by the new wrist timeout once the watch updates). No fork DB schema change anywhere in this design.
* **Rollout order (PROTOCOL §13.5.7 is a hard gate).** The empty-`t`-on-`e` change is safe in either order — every shipped phone already accepts `t: ""` on `c`. The phone's verdict change is a pure improvement. So there is no coupled rollout, which is why the two commits can land independently.
* **Overlap with the in-flight master-workspace work.** `lifecycleEvents.ts`, `events/types.ts`, `terminal/terminal.ts` and `eventBus.ts` (workspace-client) are all dirty right now. This design touches **none** of them except `packages/host-service/src/events/event-bus.ts` (host, not the workspace-client one) — check for a conflict there at rebase time, and re-read `broadcastTerminalLifecycle` after the `created` event lands, since the new `created` variant flows through the same method and must fall through the hook's `eventType === "exit"` guard.

---

## 6. Out of scope

* Durable host-side alert state (would need a `host.db` schema change and explicit user approval).
* Phone-side reconciliation of *lifecycle* cards against the tree on foreground (`CompanionNotifications.sweep` stays questions-only). This is the only thing that would close the double-restart residual.
* Question-path retraction (`v1 r`), the answer path, leases, pairing — untouched.
* Any change to the `q`/`g`/`e` push key sets, to `collapse_key`, or to the dedupe/suppression window.
* The `new-cycle` silent-retirement rule for `g` — unchanged.
* Watch UI beyond the notification timeout.
* Kanban / sidebar / recycle-bin behaviour: R3 reads the mirror, it never writes curation.

# Blueprint — companion notification-gap fixes (FIX-1/2/3)

All line refs verified by reading. Two repos:
FORK = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`
COMP = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`

## 0. Corrections to the brief (read first)

**R3 does NOT collapse into R1.** Soft-delete leaves terminals alive — `COMP`… no, FORK: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\hooks\useBulkWorkspaceSoftDelete\useBulkWorkspaceSoftDelete.ts:11-13` states the bin move is "worktree, branch and **terminals untouched**". So no exit fires, R1 never triggers, and the phone keeps a ready card for a binned thread. R3 needs its own retirement path (curation-driven, below). Hard delete does dispose (`apps\desktop\src\renderer\react-query\workspaces\useDeleteWorkspace.ts:96-99` → `terminal.disposeWorkspaceSessions` → `packages\host-service\src\terminal\terminal.ts:2939`), so hard delete → R1.

**No new key may be added to the `c` push frame.** `COMP\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\LifecyclePush.kt:234-241` validates the `c` key set with `requireExactKeySet` — an extra key is a hard `ProtocolException` on every shipped phone, i.e. the retraction is dropped and the card is stranded. FEATURES.md restates this ("exact-equality in both directions"). Every wire-level fix below therefore uses existing keys only.

**Pre-existing bug found, fixed as part of FIX-3's addressing work.** `e` retractions today carry a real `t` (`packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-alerts.ts:665`), and the phone's `forgetRetracted` (`COMP\core\...\notify\ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:173-181`) treats a non-empty `t` as "retire the terminal-collapsed READY row up to `gx`". `notifiesPhone` returns true for `e` + `new-cycle` (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:122-124`), so today: agent errors → agent starts new work → the `e` retraction silently cancels the user's unread standing READY card. Live now, independent of FIX-3.

**Ambiguity + assumption (FIX-3 blind fallback).** The user asked for `e` to retract on desktop-seen. I widen the live-map path (covers everything the host still holds) but keep the blind restart fallback `g`-only. Hashing both kinds doubles blind broadcasts on every warm reconnect, which is the exact harm documented at `lifecycle-alerts.ts:1225-1233` (the phone's 64-slot `SeenLifecycleEvents` window evicting real tombstones). Residual stated in §5. Say the word if the user wants both.

---

## 1. Recommended approach

### FIX-1 — durable watch question-retraction (COMP only, no wire change)

Clone the `PendingLifecycleDismissals` shape for resolutions, and give the wrist card a self-timeout.

* Durable queue `PendingQuestionResolutions` (SharedPreferences, `commit()`, cap 256, TTL 6 h), enqueue-before-send, clear on clean delivery, replay on `onHello` — byte-for-byte the same discipline as `COMP\app-phone\...\wear\PendingLifecycleDismissals.kt` and `WatchBridge.kt:335-387`.
* Persist only `questionId | enqueuedAtMs | resolvedAtMs | resolvedBySurface | outcome`. **`resolvedByLabel` is deliberately not persisted**: all three `pushResolved` callers pass `null` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:518-524`, `SessionViewModel.kt:231-237`, `CompanionMessagingService.kt:209-215`) and nothing on the wrist renders it (only `resolvedBySurface`, `app-watch\...\ui\AnswerStateScreen.kt:283`). Keeps the `:`/`,` delimiter encoding safe — every persisted token is base64url or a fixed enum word.
* TTL 6 h, not the dismissals' 24 h: it matches the question staleness horizon and the new wrist timeout, so a queued entry can never outlive the card it cancels. (24 h for symmetry is the alternative; 6 h is self-consistent, pick it.)
* Belt: `setTimeoutAfter` on the wrist question card, computed from `askedAtMs + QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS`. `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS = 21_600_000` mirrors the bridge's `PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS` (`packages\host-service\src\companion\config.ts:377`). Rejected alternative: carry the push's `x` to the watch on `WatchQuestion` — two of the three post paths (`pushQuestionById`, `onHello`) have no push in hand, so it would need the constant anyway; one mechanism beats two.

Why not "replay by re-fetching at hello" (call `pushQuestionById` for queued ids): it needs the desktop reachable at exactly the moment the watch reconnects, which is the case the queue exists for.

### FIX-2 — stuck ready alerts (host-side authority, FORK; one shared Kotlin fix, COMP)

Three producers, three answers, all authored where the fact is known:

* **R1 (terminal died)** — one choke point. Every exit broadcast in the tree funnels through `EventBus.broadcastTerminalLifecycle` (`packages\host-service\src\events\event-bus.ts:224`); the nine call sites are all in `terminal\terminal.ts` and `terminal\reaper\reaper.ts`. Hook a fork-only companion sink there, gated on `eventType === "exit" && confirmed !== false`, and have it call a new `LifecycleAlertManager.retireTerminal()` which is just `supersede(id, { kind: "session-end" })` — the existing, already-correct retirement. **No renderer change**, so nothing collides with the fixer's in-flight `lifecycleEvents.ts` edit.
  Rejected: calling from each of the 9 broadcast sites (silently incomplete the first time someone adds a tenth). Rejected: an `EventBus.onTerminalLifecycle` in-process listener like `onWorkspaceChanged` (`event-bus.ts:258-266`) — better dependency direction, but it needs the `EventBus` threaded into the bridge through both mounts (`serve.ts:134`, `apps\desktop\src\main\host-service\index.ts:154`) for no behavioural gain. The registry sink slot is what `registry.ts:253` exists for and answers "nobody consumed it" when the bridge is off.
  Rejected: polling `liveness.isProvablyGone` from the alert sweep — up to ~90 s late, silent when the daemon is unreachable, and the sweep only runs while a `held` alert exists (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:601-615`).

* **R2 (app restart)** — renderer supplies the one fact only it has, host decides what to retract. New one-shot mutation carrying the cold-start boundary the resync already computes in **host clock** terms (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:393-407`); the host retires `g` alerts with `outcomeAtMs < boundary`. One call per host per launch, zero blind broadcasts, no per-terminal `reportTerminalSeen` storm — which is what `companionAlertSync.ts:419-423` and `lifecycle-alerts.ts:1225-1233` explicitly forbid.
  Rejected: inferring the cold start host-side from `sidebar_mirror_meta.appLaunchId`. `APP_LAUNCH_ID` is `crypto.randomUUID()` at module scope (`...CollectionsProvider\dashboardSidebarLocal\sidebarVisibility.ts:73`) so it changes on a renderer **reload**, where sessionStorage survives and the desktop keeps its green dot — the host would retract a card the user has not read. Wrong proxy.
  Rejected: renderer reporting seen for every cold-seeded terminal — the documented mass-retraction the design forbids.

* **R3 (soft delete / any curation-off)** — the mirror is the authority and already reaches the bridge. On a mirror change, retire live alerts whose workspace is now curated off. The hold rule already exists (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:639`, `createLifecycleCurationProbe`); this applies the same rule to the states the hold cannot reach (`sent`/`standing`). Hook: the existing `mirrorChangeSink` at `packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts:1222-1239`.

* **Phone addressing (shared with FIX-3, MUST)** — `forgetRetracted` returns a key or `null`, and `null` conflates "no record" with "stale retraction" (`ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:171-189`). Cap-64 eviction (`:142`) or an expired row therefore leaves the terminal-keyed card uncancellable. Make the verdict three-valued and cancel the terminal key on **Unknown** only — an unknown record is ignorance, and a stuck card is worse than one extra cancel (the next finish reposts and buzzes). Keep the generation guard on **Stale**, which is the whole point of `gx`.

### FIX-3 — error alerts retract on desktop-seen (FORK + COMP + PROTOCOL)

* Drop the `kind !== "g"` filter in `findReadAlerts` (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:1044`). `notifiesPhone` already returns true for `e` + `seen`, so nothing else in the state machine changes.
* Keep the blind fallback `g`-only (`:1264-1274`), documented (see §0).
* **`fireRetraction` sends `t: ""` for `kind === "e"`.** This is the precise-addressing fix, and it is wire-legal today: PROTOCOL §13.5.1 already says `t` "may be `""` on `q`, `e` and `c`", and both `sanitizeTerminalHandle` (`push.ts:771-775`) and the phone parser (`LifecyclePush.kt:241,247`) accept empty. An `e` card is always event-keyed on both devices (`LifecycleAlertIdentity.key`, `ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:30-35`), so an `e` retraction has no terminal-collapsed row to name — and sending one is the pre-existing collateral bug in §0.
* Record the user's override in the `notifiesPhone` doc (`:118-120`) and in `markLifecycleSeen`'s "ONLY `g`" note (`:1197-1201`), dated 2026-08-20.

---

## 2. Files to create / modify

### FORK — host-service

| `packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-alerts.ts` | **MUST.** Add to `LifecycleAlertManager`: `retireTerminal(hostTerminalId)` (→ `supersede(id,{kind:"session-end"})`), `retireReadyBefore(boundaryMs)` (walk alerts, `kind==="g" && outcomeAtMs < boundaryMs` → `retireAlert(alert,{kind:"seen"})`), `retireCuratedOffAlerts()` (walk alerts, `deps.isCuratedOff(alert.hostWorkspaceId)` → `retireAlert(alert,{kind:"curated-off"})`). New `RetireReason` member `{kind:"curated-off"}`, rank 1 in `retireReasonRank` (`:79-81`) so it is loud and can upgrade a `new-cycle`. `findReadAlerts:1044` — drop the kind filter. `fireRetraction:653-680` — `terminalHandle: alert.kind === "g" ? deps.terminalHandle(...) : ""`. Tests: extend `companionAlertSync.test.ts` (its transport double at `:19-45` already fakes `getHostServiceClientByUrl`) and `resyncAgentStatus.test.ts`.

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `core\...\core\notify\ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt` | **MUST.** `forgetRetracted` returns a sealed `RetractionVerdict` — `Retired(key)` / `Stale` / `Unknown`. Behaviour otherwise unchanged: terminal branch first, generation guard intact, event branch as today. One rule, both surfaces. |

| `PROTOCOL.md` | **MUST.** §15 constants table: `Question staleness horizon | 21 600 000 ms`. §13.5.6: one paragraph — an error retraction carries `t: ""` because an `e` card is event-keyed and has no terminal-collapsed row, and a non-empty `t` on an `e` retraction retires a READY row it was never about. §13.5.5/§11: the wrist question card carries its own `setTimeoutAfter` from `askedAtMs` + the horizon, because the watch has no equivalent of the phone's foreground `sweep`. §13.5.5: question resolutions are eventual, not one-shot — same durable-queue wording as the watch dismissal, TTL 6 h. |

Tests: `PendingQuestionResolutionsTest.kt` (clone `PendingLifecycleDismissalsTest.kt`), extend `ShownLifecycleAlertsTest.kt`, update `WatchBridgeIntentTest.kt` construction, `WatchRelayedTextWireTest.kt` for the resolution-queue contract.

---

## 3. Data flow

**FIX-1, resolution:** phone resolves (answer confirmed / sweep / FCM retract) → `WatchBridge.pushResolved` → **enqueue first** (durable, `commit()`) → `WatchLink.sendResolved` → `Delivered && failedNodeCount==0` → `clear(questionId)`. `NoWatchPaired`/`Failed`/partial → row stays. Watch reconnects → `HELLO` → `onHello` → `flushLifecycleDismissals` → `flushQuestionResolutions` → oldest pending question. Watch: `QUESTION_RESOLVED` → `QuestionNotifier.cancel` + `QuestionStore.onResolved` (idempotent for unknown ids, `QuestionStore.kt:327-346`). Independently, every wrist question card self-cancels at `askedAtMs + 6 h`. Validation: at the queue boundary (`enqueue` refuses over cap and reports `SentUnrecorded`, never silently drops) and at `WatchLink.send` (`MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` require).

**FIX-2 R1:** pty exit / dispose / reaper correction → `EventBus.broadcastTerminalLifecycle({eventType:"exit", confirmed?})` → fork hook, `confirmed !== false` → `recordCompanionTerminalGone` → (bridge off ⇒ `false`, no-op) → `lifecycleAlerts.retireTerminal` → `supersede(terminalId, {kind:"session-end"})` → per alert: `held` deleted silently, `sending` flagged (retracted on `markDelivered`), `sent`/`standing` → one `c` each, `retracted` inert. Phone: `routeLifecycleRetract` → suppress tombstone first, then cancel, then watch dismissal (`LifecycleRouting.kt:278-289`). State persisted: none new on the host (alert table stays process-local, per `lifecycle-alerts.ts:416-421`); durable state is the phone's `ShownLifecycleAlerts` + suppression gate.

**FIX-2 R2:** desktop cold start → renderer resync computes `hostSessionBoundary = hostNow - elapsedMonotonic` → `companion.retireStaleReadyAlerts({boundaryMs})` (validated at the tRPC boundary: positive int; the sink additionally refuses `boundaryMs > now()` — a future boundary would retire everything) → `retireReadyBefore` → `retireAlert(..., {kind:"seen"})` per covered `g`. Same instant the renderer seeds those terminals as seen locally (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:509-520`), so both surfaces agree.

**FIX-2 R3:** user bins/archives/snoozes/completes a thread → `useSidebarMirrorSync` full-replace → `sidebarMirror.sync` → `replaceMirror` (`sidebar-mirror.ts:186-260`, content hash decides `changed`) → `publishCompanionMirrorChanged` → `mirrorChangeSink` → `tree.curation` event **and** `retireCuratedOffAlerts()` → `workspaceSidebarVerdict !== "show"` → one `c` per live alert. DB (`sidebar_workspace_state`) is the source of truth for the verdict; the probe's 30 s positive cache is fine here because a cached `true` is the state we act on.

**FIX-3:** user opens the chat on the desktop → `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead` (`companionAlertSync.ts:371-413`) → `companion.markLifecycleSeen` → bridge revalidates terminal↔workspace against host.db (`index.ts:917-953`) → `findReadAlerts` now returns `g` **and** `e` rows with `outcomeAtMs <= seenThroughAt` → `retireAlert(..., {kind:"seen"})` → `fireRetraction` with `t = handle` for `g`, `t = ""` for `e` → phone: `e` cancels its event-keyed row only; `g` cancels event key + terminal key under the generation guard.

---

## 4. Build order

Each step independently verifiable. **Fork work lands as its own commit after the master-workspace feature; companion work is independent and can land first.**

**COMP (independent, ship first — it makes the fork's retractions land correctly on shipped phones):**
1. `ShownLifecycleAlerts` verdict + both cancel sites + tests. Verify: `gradlew :core:test :app-phone:test :app-watch:test`.
2. `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS` + wrist question `setTimeoutAfter` + PROTOCOL §15 row. Verify: unit test on the computed timeout; manual on-wrist check that a card self-clears.
3. `PendingQuestionResolutions` + store + tests (pure JVM, no device).
4. `WatchBridge.pushResolved`/`flushQuestionResolutions`/`onHello` + container wiring + `WatchBridgeIntentTest` update.
5. PROTOCOL §13.5.5/§13.5.6 paragraphs.

**FORK (after the master-workspace commit is in):**
6. `lifecycle-alerts.ts` alone: `findReadAlerts` widening, `fireRetraction` empty-`t`-for-`e`, the three new manager methods, the `curated-off` reason, comment updates. Verify: `bun test packages/host-service/src/companion/lifecycle-alerts.test.ts` + `push-retract.test.ts`. Nothing is wired yet, so this step cannot change runtime behaviour beyond FIX-3.
7. `registry.ts` slots + `index.ts` registration + `mirrorChangeSink` call (R3 live). Verify: bun tests; manual — bin a thread with a ready card on the phone, card disappears.
8. `event-bus.ts` hook + FEATURES.md marker (R1 live). Verify: `bun run scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs`; manual — kill a terminal with a ready card, card disappears.
9. tRPC mutation + renderer `reportColdStartBoundary` + resync call (R2 live). Verify: renderer bun tests; manual — leave a ready card, quit and relaunch the desktop, card disappears.
10. FEATURES.md manifest prose. `/simplify` before commit (production code touched).

---

## 5. Risks and edge cases

* **Marker survival.** The `event-bus.ts` hook is fork-only code in an upstream-shaped file. Without the FEATURES.md marker row a nightly merge can take upstream's version and every gate stays green while R1 silently dies. Same failure class the fork already wrote `(COMPANION-CAPTURE-HOOK)` for.
* **`confirmed: false` exits.** Deliberately not retired — the row stays `active` for the reaper, which emits the confirming exit (`terminal.ts:2905-2915`, `reaper.ts:472-479`). Cost: a card lives until the reaper's pass (observed up to 21 min in the DISPOSE-LIMBO note). Retiring on the unconfirmed exit would retract a card for a terminal that may still be alive.
* **Host-service restart (residual, R2).** Alert state is process-local by design. Desktop restart + host restart ⇒ nothing holds the alert, nothing can name it, and the card lives to its 6 h TTL — the phone's `setTimeoutAfter` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:271`) takes it down, no manual swipe. The only cure is either durable alert state (schema change, needs explicit user approval) or a phone-side lifecycle sweep against the tree — both out of scope.
* **`e` retraction after a host restart (residual, FIX-3).** Blind fallback stays `g`-only, so a read does not retract a restart-orphaned `e`. Dies at TTL.
* **Snooze retracts too (R3).** `curated-off` covers snooze, not just the bin. Defensible ("not now" ⇒ take the buzz away), but it is a behaviour change beyond the literal ask — flag to the user. If unwanted, gate `retireCuratedOffAlerts` on the verdict being `deleted`/`completed`/`archived` only; `workspaceSidebarVerdict` already returns the discriminated reason (`sidebar-filter.ts:95-102`), so the narrowing is one condition.
* **Cancel-on-Unknown (phone).** Trades a possible extra cancel of an unrecorded newer card for never stranding one. The next finish reposts and buzzes, so the worst case is one missed buzz on an unread chat whose record was evicted at cap 64 — the same trade PROTOCOL §13.5.6 already documents ("one extra buzz, never a stuck notification").
* **Retraction storms.** `retireCuratedOffAlerts` runs on every *changed* mirror sync, `retireReadyBefore` once per host per launch. Both are bounded by the alert table (512) and every path goes through `retireAlert`, whose `retracted` rows are inert — no alert can fire two `c`s.
* **Clock.** `boundaryMs` is host clock by construction (`hostNow - elapsedMonotonic`); a renderer that could not read `performance.now()` or `hostNow` skips cold-start seeding entirely (`resyncAgentStatus.ts:394-405`) and must skip the report too — same guard, do not report a boundary the seeding did not use.
* **Concurrency (phone).** `PendingQuestionResolutions` must be `@Synchronized` on the instance and constructed **once** in the container, for the reason `LifecycleNotifier` spells out — the Data Layer dispatches on a pool and a per-call instance is no lock at all.
* **Migration.** The new SharedPreferences file starts empty; a resolution sent by the old build and lost stays lost (bounded by the new wrist timeout once the watch updates). No fork DB schema change anywhere in this design.
* **Rollout order (PROTOCOL §13.5.7 is a hard gate).** The empty-`t`-on-`e` change is safe in either order — every shipped phone already accepts `t: ""` on `c`. The phone's verdict change is a pure improvement. So there is no coupled rollout, which is why the two commits can land independently.
* **Overlap with the in-flight master-workspace work.** `lifecycleEvents.ts`, `events/types.ts`, `terminal/terminal.ts` and `eventBus.ts` (workspace-client) are all dirty right now. This design touches **none** of them except `packages/host-service/src/events/event-bus.ts` (host, not the workspace-client one) — check for a conflict there at rebase time, and re-read `broadcastTerminalLifecycle` after the `created` event lands, since the new `created` variant flows through the same method and must fall through the hook's `eventType === "exit"` guard.

---

## 6. Out of scope

* Durable host-side alert state (would need a `host.db` schema change and explicit user approval).
* Phone-side reconciliation of *lifecycle* cards against the tree on foreground (`CompanionNotifications.sweep` stays questions-only). This is the only thing that would close the double-restart residual.
* Question-path retraction (`v1 r`), the answer path, leases, pairing — untouched.
* Any change to the `q`/`g`/`e` push key sets, to `collapse_key`, or to the dedupe/suppression window.
* The `new-cycle` silent-retirement rule for `g` — unchanged.
* Watch UI beyond the notification timeout.
* Kanban / sidebar / recycle-bin behaviour: R3 reads the mirror, it never writes curation.

A transport failure or `accepted: false` leaves the host eligible on the next resync — `retireReadyBefore` is idempotent (a `retracted` row is inert, `retireAlert:896`), so retries are free.     targetVisible &&

    transition.axes === null &&

**No debounce, deliberately.** Idempotence is structural: one report per event, keyed by that event's own instant; a duplicate WS delivery produces an identical `seenThroughAt`; `retireAlert` is idempotent and the tombstone path (`retractById:955-992`) dedupes repeats. `targetVisible` is per-target, so a burst across terminals cannot fan out. **Not `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead`.** Its guard `if (!clearedReview && outstandingAt === null) return` (`companionAlertSync.ts:395`) refuses precisely this case — there is no review entry and no outstanding record, by construction. Call `reportTerminalSeen` directly.

The report matters when the window is visible but unfocused and presence has lapsed. The renderer can never beat the mint — the router mints synchronously at `:341`, before the renderer's round trip.

**`resolvedByLabel` is not persisted.** All three `pushResolved` callers pass `null` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:518-524`, `SessionViewModel.kt:231-237`, `CompanionMessagingService.kt:209-215`) and nothing on the wrist renders it (`app-watch\...\ui\AnswerStateScreen.kt:283` reads only `resolvedBySurface`). ### 3.2 `app-phone\...\phone\wear\WatchBridge.kt` (MUST)

`forgetRetracted:165-189` returns a three-valued verdict instead of `String?`:

```kotlin

### 3.5 `app-phone\...\phone\notifications\CompanionNotifications.kt` + `app-watch\...\wear\notify\LifecycleNotifier.kt` (MUST)

The `Unknown` branch is the cap-64 / expired-record hole: `record:142` keeps only the last 63 rows, so a busy phone loses the record while the card is still on screen and the terminal-keyed card becomes uncancellable. Trade: at worst one extra cancel of a card whose record was evicted, and the next finish reposts and buzzes — the same "one extra buzz, never a stuck notification" trade PROTOCOL §13.5.6 already documents. **Test both directions: `Stale` never cancels, `Unknown` cancels** (review pt 14).

`post:89-135` gains `timeoutAtMs: Long`; add to the builder, **as a relative duration** (review pt 6), matching `LifecycleNotifier.kt:151`:

```

## 4. Data flow

**FIX-1.** Any resolution (answer confirmed / foreground sweep / FCM retract / `pushQuestionById` / `onAnswerIntent` stale-or-resolved reply) → `deliverResolution` → enqueue durably (`commit()`) → `WatchLink.sendResolved` → clean delivery clears the row; `NoWatchPaired`/`Failed`/partial leaves it. Watch reconnects → `HELLO` → `flushLifecycleDismissals` → `flushQuestionResolutions` → oldest pending question. Watch: `QUESTION_RESOLVED` → `QuestionNotifier.cancel` + `QuestionStore.onResolved` (idempotent for unknown ids, `QuestionStore.kt:327-346`). Independently, every wrist question card self-cancels at `askedAtMs + 6 h`.

**FIX-2 R1.** pty exit / dispose / reaper correction → `broadcastTerminalLifecycle` → guard → `recordCompanionTerminalGone` (bridge off ⇒ `false`, no-op) → `retireTerminal` → `supersede(..., terminal-gone)` → per alert: `held` deleted silently, `sending` flagged and retracted on `markDelivered:697-722`, `sent`/`standing` one `c` each, `retracted` inert → phone `routeLifecycleRetract` (`LifecycleRouting.kt:278-289`): suppress tombstone **first**, then cancel, then watch dismissal.

**FIX-2 R2.** Cold desktop start → resync computes `hostNow - elapsedMonotonic` → floor → `companion.retireStaleReadyAlerts` → tRPC validates positive finite int → sink refuses `> now()` → `retireReadyBefore` → `g` alerts with `outcomeAtMs < boundary` retired as `desktop-relaunch`. Latched per host on `accepted` only.

**FIX-2 R3.** Bin/archive/snooze/complete → `useSidebarMirrorSync` full replace → `sidebarMirror.sync` → `replaceMirror:186-260` (content hash decides `changed`; the hash covers `appLaunchId`, so a cold launch always counts as changed) → `publishCompanionMirrorChanged` → `mirrorChangeSink` → `tree.curation` publish, then, separately guarded, `retireCuratedOffAlerts(fresh probe)` → flip-scoped retirement of `sending|sent|standing` only. `sidebar_workspace_state` is the source of truth for the verdict.

**FIX-2 phone addressing.** Every `c` above → `cancelLifecycle` → unconditional event-key cancel + legacy raw-id cancel → verdict → `Retired`/`Unknown` cancel the terminal key, `Stale` does not.

**FIX-3, two entry points.** (a) User opens the chat → `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead:371-413` → `companion.markLifecycleSeen` → bridge revalidates terminal↔workspace against host.db (`index.ts:917-953`) → widened `findReadAlerts` returns `g` **and** `e` → `fireRetraction` with `t = handle` for `g`, `t = ""` for `e`. (b) Turn ends while the pane is visible → `updatePaneStatus` hop → `reportTerminalSeen(seenThroughAt = payload.occurredAt)` → same path, exact id match.

Validation boundaries: tRPC input schemas (both mutations); the bridge's host.db revalidation for the seen signal; the relaunch sink's `boundaryMs <= now`; `assertLifecycleIdentity` + `sanitizeTerminalHandle` when the frame is built; `requireExactKeySet` on the phone. Persisted state: no new host DB schema anywhere. New durable client state: one SharedPreferences file on the phone.

---

## 5. Build order

Each step independently verifiable. **COMP first and shippable on its own; FORK strictly after the master-workspace commit lands.**

**COMP (independent):**
1. `ShownLifecycleAlerts` verdict + both cancel sites + tests (`Stale` never cancels, `Unknown` cancels). `gradlew :core:test :app-phone:test :app-watch:test`.
2. `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS` + wrist `setTimeoutAfter` (relative) + PROTOCOL §15 row.
3. `PendingQuestionResolutions` + store + `PendingQuestionResolutionsTest.kt` (clone `PendingLifecycleDismissalsTest.kt`: cap, TTL, restart survival, unwritable store, idempotent enqueue).
4. `deliverResolution` + all three call sites + `flushQuestionResolutions` + `onHello` order + container wiring + `WatchBridgeIntentTest.kt` construction update.
5. PROTOCOL §13.5.5 / §13.5.6 paragraphs.
   **Steps 2 and 3 ship in the same release, non-negotiable** (review pt 10): the 6 h queue TTL is only defensible because the wrist card times itself out at the same horizon. Shipping the TTL alone leaves a card with no expiry and a queue that stops retrying under it.

**FORK (after the master-workspace commit):**
6. `lifecycle-alerts.ts` only — widened `findReadAlerts`, empty-`t`-for-`e`, three reasons, three methods, doc updates. Nothing wired; the only live behaviour change is FIX-3(a). `bun test packages/host-service/src/companion/`.

10. `lifecycleEvents.ts` visible-clear hop → **M4 live**. Manual: with the window visible but unfocused and presence lapsed, let a turn fail on the front pane; the phone's error card clears.
11. FEATURES.md manifest prose. `/simplify` before commit (production code touched).

**Tests to add**

*Host (bun, extend `lifecycle-alerts.test.ts` — 1598 lines, do not create a new file):* retireTerminal across all five states; retireReadyBefore boundary-exclusive and `g`-only and includes `held`; retireCuratedOffAlerts flip-only, `held`-preserving, fresh-probe-not-cached, throw ⇒ retires nothing; the three reasons rank 1 and notify the phone; `findReadAlerts` returns `e`; blind fallback still `g`. *`push-retract.test.ts`:* `e` retraction has `t === ""` and a real `gx`; `g` retraction unchanged.
*Host events:* exit records terminal-gone; `confirmed: false` does not; `created` does not; command-start/end do not.

*Kotlin (JVM):* as listed per step.
*Manual only:* every real FCM/Data-Layer delivery, doze behaviour, the wrist timeout expiring, and cross-repo constant equality.

## 6. Documented residuals

1. **Unconfirmed dispose delay.** `confirmed: false` exits are deliberately not retired; the reaper's confirming pass is what fires the retraction — observed up to 21 minutes in the DISPOSE-LIMBO note at `terminal.ts:2884-2892`. Retiring on the unconfirmed exit would retract a card for a terminal that may still be running.
2. **Double restart.** Alert state is process-local by design (`lifecycle-alerts.ts:416-421`). Desktop **and** host-service both restarting leaves no row to name, so nothing retracts and the card lives to its 6 h TTL — taken down by the phone's own `setTimeoutAfter` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:271`), never needing a manual swipe. 3. **`e` after a host restart.** The blind fallback stays `g`-only, so a read does not retract a restart-orphaned error alert; it dies at TTL. Reversible in one line if the user prefers the doubled blind broadcasts.
4. **Cap-64 eviction.** Cancel-on-`Unknown` closes the stuck-card case at the cost of a possible extra cancel of an unrecorded newer card; bounded to one missed buzz, re-raised by the next finish.
5. **Snooze retracts.** `curated-off` includes snooze. Behaviour change beyond the literal ask, one condition to narrow.
6. **Cross-repo constant.** `QUESTION_STALE_AFTER_MS` and `PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS` cannot be bound by a test. Comments on both sides are the only guard.
7. **Merge exposure.** The `event-bus.ts` hook is fork-only code in an upstream-shaped file; the marker line is what makes its removal a red nightly rather than a silent regression.

## 7. Out of scope

Durable host-side alert state; phone-side lifecycle sweep against the tree (`CompanionNotifications.sweep` stays questions-only); the `v1 r` question-retraction path; the answer path, leases, pairing; any change to the `q`/`g`/`e`/`c` key sets, `collapse_key`, or the dedupe/suppression window; the `new-cycle` silent-retirement rule; watch UI beyond the notification timeout; the `BackgroundRunning`-sets-review oddity at `statusTransitions.ts:105-112` (noticed, pre-existing, unrelated).

Supersedes the blueprint. All 15 review points folded in. Every anchor below re-read this session.

FORK = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`
COMP = `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`

---

## 0. Decisions carried in from review, and one new finding

**Confirmed pre-existing bug (both reviewers).** `fireRetraction` passes a real terminal handle for every kind (`packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-alerts.ts:665`); the phone reads a non-empty `t` on a `c` as "retire the terminal-collapsed READY row up to `gx`" (`COMP\core\...\notify\ShownLifecycleAlerts.kt:173-181`); `notifiesPhone` fires for `e` + `new-cycle` (`:122-124`). So an error followed by fresh work silently cancels the user's unread ready card, today, with no part of this feature enabled. Fixed by §FIX-3's empty-`t` rule.

**New finding — M4's hop is exact, not a hash guess.** `notifications.ts:307-318` computes `occurredAt = nextLifecycleInstantMs(...)` **once** and passes the same value to `broadcastAgentLifecycle` (`:317`) and to `forwardCompanionLifecycle` (`:341`). So the renderer's `payload.occurredAt` for a `Stop`/`Failed` event **is** the `outcomeAtMs` the alert id hashes. The visible-clear report can therefore use `seenThroughAt = payload.occurredAt` and land on the live map every time — no blind broadcast, no `canProveAbsence` gamble.

**M4 scope, pinned.** Only `eventType === "Stop"` and `"Failed"` can mint an alert: `apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts:2981-2985` sets `lifecycle_outcome` to `"failed"` / `"ready"` for exactly those, and `lifecycle-alerts.ts:1153` ignores every other outcome. The report must be scoped to those two event types — **not** to "any event reaching the `statusTransitions.ts:98` tail", because `BackgroundRunning` reaches that tail too and mints nothing.

**Intentional asymmetry, stated so nobody "fixes" it.** R2 (desktop relaunch) retires `g` only. FIX-3 retracts `e` on a real read of that terminal; a cold relaunch is not a read of anything — the renderer's cold-start seeding is a heuristic about idle greens, and silently dropping an unseen agent-death on app restart is the failure this alert class exists to prevent.

**Fail-direction split, stated so nobody unifies it.** The curation HOLD fails open (uncertain ⇒ fire the alert, `lifecycle-alerts.ts:288-295`). The curation RETIRE fails closed (uncertain ⇒ retire nothing). Both fail toward the user being told.

**FIX-1.** Any resolution (answer confirmed / foreground sweep / FCM retract / `pushQuestionById` / `onAnswerIntent` stale-or-resolved reply) → `deliverResolution` → enqueue durably (`commit()`) → `WatchLink.sendResolved` → clean delivery clears the row; `NoWatchPaired`/`Failed`/partial leaves it. Watch reconnects → `HELLO` → `flushLifecycleDismissals` → `flushQuestionResolutions` → oldest pending question. Watch: `QUESTION_RESOLVED` → `QuestionNotifier.cancel` + `QuestionStore.onResolved` (idempotent for unknown ids, `QuestionStore.kt:327-346`). Independently, every wrist question card self-cancels at `askedAtMs + 6 h`.

**FIX-2 R1.** pty exit / dispose / reaper correction → `broadcastTerminalLifecycle` → guard → `recordCompanionTerminalGone` (bridge off ⇒ `false`, no-op) → `retireTerminal` → `supersede(..., terminal-gone)` → per alert: `held` deleted silently, `sending` flagged and retracted on `markDelivered:697-722`, `sent`/`standing` one `c` each, `retracted` inert → phone `routeLifecycleRetract` (`LifecycleRouting.kt:278-289`): suppress tombstone **first**, then cancel, then watch dismissal.

**FIX-2 R2.** Cold desktop start → resync computes `hostNow - elapsedMonotonic` → floor → `companion.retireStaleReadyAlerts` → tRPC validates positive finite int → sink refuses `> now()` → `retireReadyBefore` → `g` alerts with `outcomeAtMs < boundary` retired as `desktop-relaunch`. Latched per host on `accepted` only.

**FIX-2 R3.** Bin/archive/snooze/complete → `useSidebarMirrorSync` full replace → `sidebarMirror.sync` → `replaceMirror:186-260` (content hash decides `changed`; the hash covers `appLaunchId`, so a cold launch always counts as changed) → `publishCompanionMirrorChanged` → `mirrorChangeSink` → `tree.curation` publish, then, separately guarded, `retireCuratedOffAlerts(fresh probe)` → flip-scoped retirement of `sending|sent|standing` only. `sidebar_workspace_state` is the source of truth for the verdict.

**FIX-2 phone addressing.** Every `c` above → `cancelLifecycle` → unconditional event-key cancel + legacy raw-id cancel → verdict → `Retired`/`Unknown` cancel the terminal key, `Stale` does not.

**FIX-3, two entry points.** (a) User opens the chat → `markTerminalSeenAndReportRead:371-413` → `companion.markLifecycleSeen` → bridge revalidates terminal↔workspace against host.db (`index.ts:917-953`) → widened `findReadAlerts` returns `g` **and** `e` → `fireRetraction` with `t = handle` for `g`, `t = ""` for `e`. (b) Turn ends while the pane is visible → `updatePaneStatus` hop → `reportTerminalSeen(seenThroughAt = payload.occurredAt)` → same path, exact id match.

Validation boundaries: tRPC input schemas (both mutations); the bridge's host.db revalidation for the seen signal; the relaunch sink's `boundaryMs <= now`; `assertLifecycleIdentity` + `sanitizeTerminalHandle` when the frame is built; `requireExactKeySet` on the phone. Persisted state: no new host DB schema anywhere. New durable client state: one SharedPreferences file on the phone.

content:
<agent-message from="s3-simple">
SIMPLIFICATION REVIEW — master-workspace feature diff. Not clean; 11 findings, none behavioural. Ordered by payoff.

## 1. eventBus.ts:295-327 — 4-arm nested ternary, 4 indent levels
`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\workspace-client\src\lib\eventBus.ts`
Adding `created` pushed an already-3-deep conditional expression to 4, re-indenting all three existing arms (that's most of the file's diff churn — the real change is one new arm). The added comment "a new type added without a branch here would be silently relabelled" is describing a hazard the shape creates.
Cost: ~40 lines of ternary, whole-block re-indent on every future eventType, plus a test (eventBus.test.ts:138-214) that exists to pin the hazard.
Simpler: extract `function toTerminalLifecyclePayload(message): TerminalLifecyclePayload` with a `switch (message.eventType)` and `default: never` exhaustiveness. Flat, one arm per type, next eventType is +6 lines and no re-indent, and the compiler enforces what the comment currently asks a reader to remember.

## 2. useSubmitWorkspace.ts:100-140 — in-flight ref reset 3× for refusals that don't need it
`...\PromptGroup\hooks\useSubmitWorkspace\useSubmitWorkspace.ts`
The three refusals (linkedPR :105, `!hostUrl` :114, no-agent :136) are all synchronous and mutate nothing, yet each sits *after* `masterSubmitInFlight.current = true` and each has to undo it.
Cost: 3 duplicated `masterSubmitInFlight.current = false;` lines, and the "check and set MUST stay adjacent, no await between" invariant now spans 40 lines of guard code instead of 2.
Simpler: hoist all three refusals above :100, leaving `if (inFlight) return; inFlight = true;` immediately before the `try`. Only the `catch` resets. Behaviour identical (double-click already toasts twice today, since click 1 resets the ref before click 2 resumes).

## 3. useSubmitWorkspace.ts:111-121 — `!hostUrl` guard contradicts its own type
After the `mode === "master"` narrow, `hostUrl` is `string`, so this only catches `""`. The resolver already owns the nullish case (resolveMasterMode.ts:154, `hostUrl == null`). Two owners for one precondition, and the comment's stated reason ("the host can drop between that render and this click") can't happen — `masterTarget` is a value captured at render.
Simpler: change resolveMasterMode.ts:154 to `if (!hostUrl) return { mode: "loading" };` and delete lines 112-121 here. Same safety, one owner, -10 lines.

## 4. useSubmitWorkspace.ts:126-142 — no-agent refusal duplicated, with a divergent message
Same rule lives in PromptGroup.tsx:344-355 (`submitBlocker`), which `handleSubmit` checks before calling `createWorkspace`. Not defense-in-depth in practice: PromptGroup can never reach it, and NewWorkspaceScreen passes `BRANCH_ONLY_TARGET` so it can't either — it is currently unreachable from both call sites.
Worse than dead: the two copies word it differently. Blocker falls back `masterName ?? selectedProject?.name ?? "this project"`; this one falls back `masterName ?? "this project"`. Two strings to keep in sync for one rule.
Simpler: pick one owner. Keeping the hook's copy (so the hook is safe for a future third caller) is defensible — then delete the blocker rung and let `handleSubmit` fall through to the toast, or export the message builder so both read one source. Keeping both as-is is the only option that costs a divergence.

## 5. useProjectGitState.ts:96-100 — nested ternary for a two-term OR
```ts
const isError = gitProbeEnabled ? gitProbeErrored : multiRepoEnabled ? multiRepoProbeErrored : false;
```
Simpler, and reads as the comment's own sentence ("only the ENABLED probe's error counts"):
```ts
const isError = (gitProbeEnabled && gitProbeErrored) || (multiRepoEnabled && multiRepoProbeErrored);
```
Equivalent — the two probes are mutually exclusive by construction, which the comment already states.

## 6. useMasterWorkspaceTarget/index.ts — barrel 3 exports too wide
Exports `MASTER_FOLDER_MISSING_REASON`, `ResolveMasterModeInput`, `resolveMasterMode`. No consumer outside the folder imports any of them (grepped all of `apps/desktop/src`); the tests import from `./resolveMasterMode` directly. Only `useMasterWorkspaceTarget`, `MasterWorkspaceTarget` and `BRANCH_ONLY_TARGET` are actually used.
Simpler: export those three; leave the rest folder-internal.

## 7. selectHiddenMainsToSurface.ts:60-66 — 5 positional params, 2 of them containers built by the caller
The hook (useSurfaceHiddenMainWorkspaces.ts:78-83) builds a `Map` and a `Set` inside the effect purely to feed this signature, including a `{ sidebarState: row }` re-wrap of every row. `SidebarRowForSurfacing` exists only to name that wrapper.
Cost: ~8 lines of effect scaffolding, one type that carries no meaning, and a 5-arg call site where three args are `readonly`-qualified container types.
Simpler: take the two flat arrays (`rows: readonly {workspaceId, ...HiddenMainSidebarState}[]`, `sidebarProjectIds: readonly string[]`) and build the Map/Set inside the selector. Drops the wrapper type, the re-wrap map, and both effect-local constructions; tests get shorter too.

## 8. PromptGroup.test.tsx — dead knobs and one duplicate test
`...\PromptGroup\PromptGroup.test.tsx`
- `gitProbeErrored` (:44, :62, :136): never set `true` by any test. The mock's `isError: enabled && gitProbeErrored` is permanently `false`. Dead knob — either add the errored-probe case (it's a real rung) or delete all three lines.
- `masterWorktreeExists` (:45, :63, :74) + `masterRow()` (:90): the stubs read `hostWorkspaceRows`, never this variable. Its one consumer (:541) sets *both* it and the row. Simpler: delete variable and helper; that test does `hostWorkspaceRows[0].worktreeExists = false`.
- `"a Recycle-Binned master is restored, not launched into inside the bin"` (:580): sets up nothing bin-specific — no `deletedAt` anywhere — so it runs the identical scenario as `"restores the master to Active before launching"` (:570) with weaker assertions. Its `not.toContain("unarchive:...")` is vacuous: the mock never exposes `unarchive`. Simpler: delete it, move its (good) comment onto :570.

## 9. sidebarMutations.ts:150-152 — comment describing absent code
Three lines explaining why the deleted pin sweep isn't needed, sitting where the loop was. The reason already lives on `tombstoneSidebarWorkspaceRecord` (:76-78, "A row must never be hidden and pinned at once"). Simpler: drop it, or fold one clause into the tombstone loop above.

## 10. PromptGroup.tsx:349 — re-derives `isMasterMode`
`masterTarget.mode === "master" && selectedAgent === "none" && ...` — `isMasterMode` is already computed at :317 and no narrowing is needed here (the branch uses `masterRunsInLabel`, not `masterTarget.masterName`). Use `isMasterMode`. Nit; the other two `mode === "master"` checks in the file genuinely need the discriminant for narrowing.

## 11. V2WorkspaceView.tsx:350-353 — unrelated hunk
The `onAddChatV3` reflow is formatter noise in a feature diff. Harmless, just widens the review surface.

---

## Answers to the specific questions you asked

**`resolveMasterMode` input width (12 fields):** justified. I checked each for derivability — none is. Rejected two collapses as net-negative: (a) folding `mainWorkspaceId`/`masterName`/`masterWorktreeExists`/`hostUrl` into one `master` object would force the hook to memoize it separately, trading 4 primitive deps for 1 unstable reference; (b) precomputing rung 2 into an `isLocalHost` boolean would move the ladder's most subtle judgement (identity must be PROVEN, two nulls aren't a match) out of the tested pure function. One optional tightening: `isResolved` + `isError` are two booleans encoding three states, and `{isResolved: true, isError: true}` is unrepresentable-but-typeable. A `probe: "ok" | "error" | "pending"` merges rungs 7 and 8 into a switch. Take it or leave it — the flat form matches `useProjectGitState`'s own shape.

**`useMasterWorkspaceTarget` memo:** earning its keep. Its job is stable identity for `masterTarget`, which is a dep of both `submitBlocker`'s memo and `submitWorkspace`'s callback; without it both rebuild every render. The 12 deps are all primitives, so it's cheap and correct. No change.

**Master submit guard/refusal layering vs `submitBlocker`:** two of the four layers are redundant, not defense-in-depth — see #3 and #4. The other two (the in-flight ref, the linkedPR refusal) are genuinely reachable and should stay; the ref in particular can't reuse `isCreating`, which is cloud-mutation-only (:416).

**`selectHiddenMainsToSurface` exported types:** `SidebarRowForSurfacing` is a one-field wrapper that exists to satisfy the classifier's parameter shape — see #7. `LocalWorkspaceForSurfacing` and `HiddenMainSidebarState` both earn their exports.

**Sweep classify structure:** clean. The three-outcome try/catch is the point of the change and reads as three outcomes. `probeIsGitRepo` injection follows the existing `runArchivedWorkspaceReconcile` idiom. No finding.

**PromptGroup gating conditionals:** one redundant re-derive (#10). The branch-vs-master JSX fork is a genuine either/or over five sibling elements — a derived config object would be worse. No finding.

**Test bloat:** not bloated. `resolveMasterMode.test.ts` is 19 one-line tests over 130 lines, one per rung plus the ordering cases — that ratio is right. `selectHiddenMainsToSurface.test.ts` already table-drives its bucket matrix. Only real duplication is in `PromptGroup.test.tsx` (#8). Tiny nit: three resolveMasterMode tests repeat the full master result literal (:38, :123, :155) — a `MASTER_RESULT` const would save 12 lines.

---

## Out of angle, but cheap to fix while you're here
`FEATURES.md` markers block lists `(MASTER-PLUS-LAUNCH)` only under `apps/desktop/src/renderer`, but the marker is also load-bearing in `packages/host-service` (terminal.ts:3747, events/types.ts:40) and `packages/workspace-client` (eventBus.ts:44). As written, a merge that drops the host-side `created` broadcast passes the marker gate. `(MASTER-ALWAYS-ACTIVE)` correctly lists both its paths.
</agent-message>

Boot git spawns for this sweep went 1×N → 2×N, serial, N = every project row ever. On Windows ARM64 a git spawn is ~50-150ms, so 30 projects ≈ +2-5s. <agent-message from="s3-eff">
EFFICIENCY REVIEW (wasted work only, no correctness findings). 7 findings, ranked.

**1. MEDIUM — every terminal:lifecycle event refetches terminal.list**
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/routes/_authenticated/_dashboard/v2-workspace/$workspaceId/hooks/useAutoAdoptBackgroundSessions/useAutoAdoptBackgroundSessions.ts:65-74`
Subscribed invalidate-only, no eventType filter, but only `created` is needed. `command-start` / `command-end` / synthesized prompt-redraw ends broadcast per foreground command on any OSC 133 shell (`packages/host-service/src/terminal/terminal.ts:3627,3640,3654`). Cost per event: `terminal.list` is not a cheap read — renderer→host RPC → `getDaemonClient()` + `daemon.list()` IPC round-trip + DB read (`terminal.ts:1060-1100`); then `isFetching` flips true→false = 2 re-renders of `V2WorkspaceCenter` (the query is tracked in this hook, mounted there); then the adopt effect re-runs (`sessions` is a new array) doing a localStorage parse, 2 Set builds and a tab walk. So a shell running 20 commands = 40 daemon round-trips + 80 center re-renders that can adopt nothing.
Also: grep shows no other lifecycle→`terminal.list.invalidate` in the tree, so the comment's "same shape `useTerminalAgentBindings` uses" isn't load-bearing cost precedent.
Cheaper: first line of the callback `if (payload.eventType !== "created") return;`. Keeps the created→pane invariant exactly; drops ~all volume. (`exit` already has its own consumers.)

**2. MEDIUM — sweep spawns a git process per project per boot, serially, unconditionally**
`packages/host-service/src/runtime/main-workspace-sweep.ts:31-62` (probe at :53)
`isGitRepoStrict` = `checkIsRepo()` = one git spawn. `ensureMainWorkspaceStrict` then spawns git AGAIN for the git path (`symbolic-ref --short HEAD`, ensure-main-workspace.ts:93-94). Boot git spawns for this sweep went 1×N → 2×N, serial, N = every project row ever. On Windows ARM64 a git spawn is ~50-150ms, so 30 projects ≈ +2-5s. Non-blocking for server start (background IIFE, `app.ts:219`) but it is `await`ed ahead of `runArchivedWorkspaceReconcile` (`app.ts:230` then `:238`), so the crash-recovery reconcile is delayed by the whole added time.
Cheaper, invariant-preserving:
 (a) bounded concurrency (pool of 4-8) over `rows` — loop bodies are independent per project; tri-state handling unchanged.
 (b) skip the probe entirely for projects that already have a `type='main'` row whose `branch !== NON_GIT_BRANCH` — one indexed SQL read replaces N spawns. Those rows take the git path today and, if the folder stopped being a repo, `ensureMainWorkspaceStrict` throws → wrapper swallows → row untouched: identical to pre-diff behaviour, no rewrite risk, so the fail-closed guarantee survives.
Do NOT reuse the TTL-cached `isGitRepo` — the diff's comment is right that it reintroduces the ambiguity.

**3. LOW-MEDIUM — modal fires host RPCs for probes master mode will never read**
`apps/desktop/.../DashboardNewWorkspaceModal/hooks/useMasterWorkspaceTarget/useMasterWorkspaceTarget.ts:28` → `useProjectGitState`
`resolveMasterMode` rungs 1-3 return `branch` for a cloud host, a remote host, or a multi-repo project — but `useProjectGitState`'s `enabled` doesn't know that. Selecting a REMOTE host with a main workspace issues a `git.isRepo` RPC across the relay to that host; `multi-repo-info` fires against the local host for any project with no local main (incl. while cloud is selected). `staleTime: Infinity` so it's once per key, not per render, but each is a network round-trip for a value rung 2 discards.
Cheaper: add an `enabled` param to `useProjectGitState` (default true, kanban unaffected) and pass `selectedHostId === machineId && selectedHostId !== CLOUD_HOST_ID` from `useMasterWorkspaceTarget`. Predicate order and fail-closed rungs untouched.

**4. LOW — three full scans of the workspace list per modal keystroke**
`useMasterWorkspaceTarget.ts:27, 28 (inside useProjectGitState:43), 36`
`useProjectMainWorkspaceId` is an unmemoized `workspaces.find` (`kanban/hooks/useProjectMainWorkspaceId/useProjectMainWorkspaceId.ts:22`) and is called twice — directly and again inside `useProjectGitState` — plus the `workspaces.find` at :36. `PromptGroup` re-renders per keystroke (`draft.prompt` is in the `useShallow` selector, `DashboardNewWorkspaceDraftContext.tsx:60`), so that's 3×O(W) over every workspace on every host, per character. Absolute cost small; it's pure duplication.
Cheaper: find the master ROW once in a `useMemo` here, derive `mainWorkspaceId` from it, and pass the id into `useProjectGitState` (or memoize inside `useProjectMainWorkspaceId`).

**5. LOW — duplicate live query over the same two collections in the same component**
`AgentHooks/hooks/useSurfaceHiddenMainWorkspaces/useSurfaceHiddenMainWorkspaces.ts:48-73` vs `AgentHooks/hooks/useSidebarMirrorSync/useSidebarMirrorSync.ts:459-491`
Both mounted in `AgentHooks`. The mirror's `v2WorkspaceLocalState` projection is a strict SUPERSET of the reconciler's (adds projectId/sectionId/tabOrder/pinnedAt), and its `v2SidebarProjects` projection is a superset too. Two incremental views maintained and two result arrays allocated for every curation change where one pair would do.
Cheaper: lift one pair of queries into `AgentHooks` (or a shared `useSidebarCurationRows`) and pass rows to both consumers. Note the mirror gates on its own `isReady`, so this is a small refactor, not a one-liner.

**6. LOW — reconciler materialises every workspace, then filters**
`useSurfaceHiddenMainWorkspaces.ts:35-44` and `:75-93`
The memo allocates W objects (all workspaces, all hosts) though only local `main`s can be candidates (~1 per project); the effect then builds a Map over ALL local-state rows and a Set over ALL sidebar projects before the first candidate check. Frequency is fine — `workspaces` is memoized upstream with react-query structural sharing, so the 30s poll (`useHostWorkspaces.ts:24,208`) doesn't churn identity, and the live queries emit on genuine leaf changes — so this runs per real change, not per render.
Cheaper: filter `type === "main" && hostId === machineId` inside the memo (the pure selector re-checks both, so the bucket-only predicate is unweakened), and early-return before building Map/Set when that list is empty — the normal case. Polish, not a hot path.
Also note: unlike the mirror, this hook has no debounce/signature gate; today's per-run cost doesn't justify one, but if the effect ever grows past Map/Set building the mirror's gate is the precedent.

**7. TRIVIAL — dead memo**
`useAutoAdoptBackgroundSessions.ts:66-68`: the `useCallback` is pointless — `useWorkspaceEvent` already wraps the callback in `useEffectEvent` (`renderer/hooks/host-service/useWorkspaceEvent/useWorkspaceEvent.ts:64`), so identity never matters. Inline it.

Cost per event: `terminal.list` is not a cheap read — renderer→host RPC → `getDaemonClient()` + `daemon.list()` IPC round-trip + DB read (`terminal.ts:1060-1100`); then `isFetching` flips true→false = 2 re-renders of `V2WorkspaceCenter` (the query is tracked in this hook, mounted there); then the adopt effect re-runs (`sessions` is a new array) doing a localStorage parse, 2 Set builds and a tab walk. **2. MEDIUM — sweep spawns a git process per project per boot, serially, unconditionally**
`packages/host-service/src/runtime/main-workspace-sweep.ts:31-62` (probe at :53)
`isGitRepoStrict` = `checkIsRepo()` = one git spawn. `ensureMainWorkspaceStrict` then spawns git AGAIN for the git path (`symbolic-ref --short HEAD`, ensure-main-workspace.ts:93-94). Boot git spawns for this sweep went 1×N → 2×N, serial, N = every project row ever. On Windows ARM64 a git spawn is ~50-150ms, so 30 projects ≈ +2-5s. - Reconciler as an `AgentHooks` sibling: right. Placement under `AgentHooks/hooks/` matches co-location, the ordering rationale (after `usePlaceLocalWorktreesInSidebar`, before `useSidebarMirrorSync`) is stated and correct, and the pure `selectHiddenMainsToSurface` / React-wiring split is the right seam. - Restoring the auto-adopt mount in `V2WorkspaceCenter` rather than upstream's `page.tsx` is correct: the hook needs `store` + `isLayoutReady`, which the center owns.
